articleTitle: High gain DC-DC converter based on Quasi-Z-Source
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper introduces an innovative non-isolated, high-voltage-gain DC-DC converter utilizing a quasi-Z source topology integrated with a switching capacitor mechanism. This converter boasts the capability of achieving substantial voltage amplification even at low duty cycles, making it an efficient and straightforward solution. Furthermore, the article delves into the fundamental operating principles of this converter, outlines a method for parameter optimization, and compares its performance to alternative high-gain DC-DC converters, highlighting its unique advantages. Finally, a 30V to 180V, 100W converter with an efficiency of 91.2% was fabricated to verify the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Research on improved current control strategy of LCL grid-connected inverter under weak grid
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Under weak grid conditions, significant changes in grid impedance can lead to decreased stability in grid-connected inverter systems, and grid harmonics and LCL filter resonance issues often distort the current waveform. To address these challenges, this paper proposes an improved current control method. The strategy utilizes a negative second-order high-pass filter, and the three-phase LCL-type grid-connected inverter is modeled, with the control parameters optimized. This approach enhances the system’s phase margin, increases the inverter’s adaptability in weak grids, and improves power quality. The accuracy and efficacy of this control method are confirmed through Matlab/Simulink simulations.

articleTitle: GIS Partial discharge identification based on AlexNet neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Gas Insulated Switchgear (GIS) is an important part of the current power system, and its safe and stable operation is directly related to people’s production and life. Partial discharge (PD) is an important reason for the decline of GIS insulation level, so the diagnosis of GIS PD faults can promptly eliminate insulation faults and guarantee the high-quality operation of the power system. This paper analyses the GIS PD PRPD(Phase Resolved Partial Discharge) pattern features of UHF signals, and perform image preprocessing with grey scale, binarization and image segmentation. In order to avoid the subjectivity of feature data extraction, this paper adopts AlexNet neural network to identify the pattern, and finally the total identification rate reaches $97.70 \%$, which achieves the purpose of timely operation and maintenance of GIS.

articleTitle: Turbine Data cleansing based on conditional depth convolution generation confrontation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the advantages of fast response speed and high processing capacity, Big data technology provides great convenience for the operation data analysis of power plant thermal equipment. A large amount of operation data will be generated during the operation of steam turbine, but data loss, discontinuity, abnormality and other situations will occur due to various reasons. Through Big data cleaning algorithm, data content can be optimized, data application accuracy can be improved, and subsequent data processing can be facilitated. In this paper, the C-DCGAN model is used to take the turbine boundary conditions as the input condition information, and the trained discriminator and generator are used to clean the Data cleansing. It can effectively eliminate the Outlier of the unit data to be cleaned and the data filling of the missing data after the value elimination. While ensuring the consistency of the data volume before and after cleaning, the data change trend of the filled complete data set is relatively flat and more consistent with the actual unit data distribution trend.

articleTitle: Discussion on the strategy of orderly power utilization scheme based on the new power load management system
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: ordered electricity use is one of the vital load management methods to alleviate the contradiction between power supply and demand. the orderly electricity use plan is the basis for implementing orderly electricity use. traditional orderly electricity use plans rely too much on manual intervention in the preparation process, which seriously affects work efficiency and the effectiveness of orderly electricity use execution. this article takes into account factors such as regional economic structure, electricity consumption characteristics, internal installed capacity, industrial impact, and green electricity consumption. it explores the use of a new power load management system to intelligently generate orderly electricity consumption plans, ensuring fairness and scientificity in the execution of orderly electricity consumption, ensuring the full formulation of orderly electricity consumption plans, and meeting relevant national policy requirements to improve the efficiency of the preparation of orderly electricity consumption plans.

articleTitle: Grid partitioning method for medium voltage distribution network based on improved k-means algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Using principal component analysis method to reduce the dimensionality of medium voltage distribution network data. Using the farthest distance algorithm to solve the length between two pairs of data in the medium voltage distribution network, applying the improved k-means algorithm to cluster all data into multiple clusters based on distance measurement, achieving clustering of distribution network data. Based on this, grid positioning is carried out for the medium voltage distribution network to evaluate the power flow value of the distribution network. Finally, design the grid division process for the distribution network. The experimental results show that the medium voltage distribution network structure divided by the research method is reasonable. Under the application of this method, the load in different areas is relatively balanced, and there is no cross between the matching line segment and the main supply line segment in the research method division results, which meets the condition of non cross power supply of the line.

articleTitle: A Markov Matrix Based Method for Prediction Direction in Wind Power Forecasting Attacks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Deep learning has a wide range of applications in the field of wind power prediction, but it is susceptible to attacks. The fast gradient sign method based on selected directions achieves better performance than methods relying on random direction determined by judging directions. However, this method still lacks sufficient interpretability and understanding of its underlying mechanisms. In this paper, we propose a method based on the Markov transition matrix to predict directions, which is comparable to the method using selected directions in terms of prediction effectiveness. Furthermore, this paper explains the reason behind such predictable outcomes, namely, that wind power data from the previous time step makes a significant and primary contribution to the wind power at the current time step.

articleTitle: Short-term Solar Power Forecasting: An Accuracy Comparison of Machine Learning Methods versus Typical Daily Curve
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In this study, we perform short-term power generation prediction for the fluctuation of seasonal new energy power generation, and firstly, we explore the shortcomings of the traditional K-means clustering method in the prediction of solar power generation. Then, in order to improve the prediction accuracy and model robustness, we systematically evaluate a variety of advanced machine learning models, such as Random Forest(RF), Back Propagation Neural Network (BPNN), Stacked Regression(STAC), Linear Regression (LiR), Random Forest(RF) and XGBoost(XGB), BPNN+STAC, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Gradient Boosted Decision Tree (GBDT), BPNN+STAC, Long-short-term memory network (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), etc., and ultimately select the best-performing BPNN+STAC combined model. Based on the results, we compare the performance of BPNN+STAC model with typical daily curve by K-means method, by quantifying the key indexes of MAE, RMSE, RMAPE and $\mathrm{R}^{2}$, the results show that the BPNN+STAC model has a significant advantage in terms of prediction accuracy and stability, and the MAE and RMSE are reduced by 44.55% and 50.12%, respectively, and the $R^{2}$ is improved by $49.23 \% .49 .23 \%$. This study not only provides a new theoretical framework for the accurate prediction of wind power generation, but also demonstrates its strong potential for practical application in virtual power systems and its wide spread value.

articleTitle: A control method for an improved H-bridge and NPC hybrid cascaded static var generator
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Adopting a Hybrid Cascade Static Synchronous Compensator (HC-SVG), which integrates Neutral-Point Clamped (NPC) three-level power units and Cascade H-bridge (CHB) power units, can reduce the number of CHB power units, making it a current research hotspot in the field of reactive power compensation. However, the introduction of high-voltage NPC power units causes high-order harmonics in the DC bus capacitors on both the NPC and CHB sides, affecting the overall compensation performance of the device. This paper proposes an improved control method that extracts and filters the high-order harmonic content of the DC-side capacitors in the reactive power compensation device, resulting in more stable system operation. Finally, a simulation platform is constructed to verify the effectiveness of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Research on the Value-adjusted Levelized Cost of Electricity and Its Application
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of renewable energy into the power grid, its intermittent and fluctuating nature presents challenges to the safe and stable operation of the power system, and the resulting cost changes become the key to affecting the economics of renewable energy. The value-adjusted levelized cost of electricity (VALCOE) adds energy, capacity and flexibility to the evaluation of the life-cycle cost of power generation technologies, providing a powerful tool for comprehensively evaluating the impact of various power generation technologies on the economics of power systems. At present, there is no mature method for defining the base capacity value and flexibility value multiplier involved in applying VALCOE to the economic evaluation of renewable energy in China. Therefore, this paper determines the base capacity value by calculating the annual capital repayment amount of the existing lowest-cost peaking power plant according to the actual situation in China and provides an appropriate flexibility value multiplier that fully considers the adjustability of domestic generator sets. VALCOE assessment reveals that the economy of coal-fired thermal power units in major areas of China in 2040 is still far superior to that of newly built renewable energy units. In the process of carbon neutralization, countries should consider their own national conditions and different state-owned resources, measure the safety and economy of large-scale replacement of traditional energy sources, and gradually integrate renewable energy into the power grid.

articleTitle: Application of Federated Learning in Smart Grid Fault Diagnosis: Privacy Protection and Efficiency Improvement
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper proposes a framework based on Federated Learning (FL) for power line fault diagnosis. By constructing Random Forest (RF), Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Linear Regression (LR) models, power line faults are predicted and diagnosed. The study compares federated learning, centralized learning and decentralized learning frameworks to find out the most suitable method for power grid fault diagnosis. Experimental results show that when using random forest and support vector machine techniques, federated learning outperforms centralized and decentralized frameworks in terms of mean square error (MSE), while centralized learning performs best when using linear regression models. In addition, in terms of model training delay, federated learning performs better when using linear regression and random forest models, while decentralized learning has the smallest delay when using support vector machines. Results indicates that the FL-SVM achieved the lowest MSE, which is 0.047.

articleTitle: Coupling Evaluation of New Energy Consumption Levels and Resource Potential
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: To promote the sustainable development of new energy, it is of great significance to clarify the level of new energy consumption and resource potential in each province. In this study, firstly, the assessment indicators of new energy consumption level and new energy resource potential are selected, and the CRITIC-TOPSIS method is used to determine the weights of the indicators and make a comprehensive assessment. Secondly, the coupling level of new energy consumption level and resource potential in each province is calculated using the coupling degree model. Finally, the K-means clustering method is used to cluster the new energy development of each province. The new energy data of 31 provinces in 2022 are utilized for empirical analysis. The results show that Inner Mongolia, Henan, and Shandong have the highest new energy consumption level; Xinjiang, Tibet, and Inner Mongolia have the highest new energy resource potential; Inner Mongolia, Yunnan, and Qinghai have the highest coupling level; and 31 provinces can be divided into seven categories.

articleTitle: Intelligent Planning Method for “Big Branch” of Feeder Considering Pipeline-Grid Coupling Intelligent Planning of Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Due to the lack of effective intelligent planning methods, distribution networks planning has to heavily rely on manual planning, resulting in low efficiency. Here, we propose an intelligent planning method for “big branch” problem. Firstly, a coupling model between the pipeline and the power grid is constructed. Then, A fast method for diagnosing and locating large branches is proposed based on the practical guidelines for distribution networks planning. Subsequently, the hippopotamus optimization algorithm (HOA) and the single source shortest path algorithm are used to generate a renovation plan for the “big branch” problem. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified on a real distribution network example.

articleTitle: Modeling of Power Supply System And Determination of Component Reliability Parameters Based on Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The reliability index of power supply and distribution system is a key index that affects the design and operation performance of the system structure. The reliability calculation and analysis can provide a powerful guide for building a more reliable structure of power supply and distribution system. In this paper, a mathematical model of power supply and distribution system structure is established by using Boolean algebra, and the influence curve of each component on the final reliability index of the system in a certain reliability interval is analyzed, which is used to understand the macro trend of the global index change. The reliability index of different system structures is compared, and the best system structure meeting the user’s requirements is determined. The reliability index requirements of each component are analyzed under the condition of reliability index requirements of users. Through the above reliability calculation and analysis, the reasonable, feasible and lowest optimal system structure and component reliability index boundary interval which meet the requirements of users are determined.

articleTitle: Modeling and Evaluation of Multi-time Scale Demand Response Capability of Charging Stations Considering Vehicle-Pile Information
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Under the dual-carbon policy, the rapid growth of Electric Vehicles(EV) on a large scale and the large-scale configuration of charging piles have threatened the safe operation of the distribution network. As a bridge for massive EVs to access the grid, charging stations can participate in grid-side demand response by aggregating EV loads as generalized energy storage devices through incentives. However, due to the self-interest, mobility and other uncertainties inherent in EVs, it is easy to lead to the failure of the quantization of charging station’s demand response capability. Therefore, this paper firstly establishes a Generalized Energy Storage Model(GESM) for charging stations considering vehicle-pile information and users’ subjective responsiveness, and secondly establishes an evaluation model for the demand response capacity of charging piles with multiple time scales, which reduces the uncertainty of charging station’s callable capacity to the greatest extent, and provides conditions for the realization of charging station’s participation in demand response. Finally, the arithmetic example shows that the scheme proposed in this paper has some reference significance for the capacity evaluation of charging stations participating in demand response.

articleTitle: Cross-platform data interaction technology for UHV transmission line engineering based on 3D model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: UHV engineering 3D design platforms, and each specialty often adopts different platforms, which leads to the existing interaction technology being limited to the application of a certain platform and cannot realize cross-platform interaction. In this paper, the cross-platform data interaction technology based on 3D model is studied for UHV line engineering. The research ideas and steps of this technology are elaborated from four aspects: model analysis, model structured storage, model local update, and model data hooking, and the cross-platform data interaction based on 3D model is preliminarily realized.

articleTitle: The Study of Unit Commitment Based on Adaptive Mixed-Variable Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The unit commitment (UC) problem is a crucial type of economic dispatch problem in power systems, and its mathematical model is a complex, large-scale mixed-integer nonlinear problem, making it difficult to obtain a theoretical optimal solution. To address this, an adaptive mixed-variable particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm is proposed in this paper, considering the remaining cycle count of the energy storage battery. This approach not only enhances the traditional PSO, which tends to fall into local optima, but also handles continuous, binary, and integer variables effectively. To evaluate the impact of transfer functions on the algorithm, eight different transfer functions are compared. Results from two case studies demonstrate that the proposed algorithm can efficiently solve the UC problem with nonlinear mixed variables, while also being robust. This makes it a feasible method to mitigate the unpredictability and stochastic nature of sustainable distributed generators and other intermittent energy sources.

articleTitle: Study on ice shedding mode of transmission conductors based on Monte Carlo method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Ice shedding from transmission conductors can trigger significant dynamic responses, potentially leading to interphase flashovers and damage to power structures. To accurately estimate these dynamic responses, it is essential to determine a practical ice shedding mode and its corresponding shedding rate. This study investigates a more reasonable ice shedding mode for a single-span transmission line using the Monte Carlo method and kernel density estimation. Inverse transform sampling was employed to simulate the initial ice shedding of a conductor under the influence of external loads. The impact of initial ice shedding on remaining ice and the variations in impact due to differences in the spatial location of the unshed ice were considered. The Monte Carlo method was used to generate a sample of 1 million shedding modes for the single-span conductor. The ice shedding rate for these samples, with a 95% confidence level, was derived using kernel density estimation, and a formula for calculating the shedding rate was provided. This paper ultimately develops a more reasonable ice shedding mode and shedding rate compared to current design standards, offering valuable reference points for the structural design of transmission lines.

articleTitle: QAOA-based Day-ahead Clearing Model for Electricity Spot Market
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The high degree of uncertainty in the operation of new power systems with large-scale access to new energy sources has increased the difficulty of clearing spot transactions in the power market, and the computational volume and complexity of model solving have become higher and higher. The rapid development of quantum computers provides a new idea for the future power market spot trading model solution. In this paper, we propose a model for day-ahead clearing in the electricity spot market using a quantum approximation optimization algorithm. The original day-ahead security constrained unit combination model of the electricity spot market is decoupled into a discrete-variable model and a continuous-variable model by the alternating direction multiplier method. The discrete-variable model is solved by the quantum approximation optimization algorithm, and the continuous-variable model is solved by the solver, and the start-stop state solutions of the units are obtained by constant alternating iterations. Based on the optimized unit start-stop solution, the winning power and node marginal tariff of the unit are solved by the security constrained unit combination model. Simulation examples based on the IEEE 39 -node system are performed to verify the validity of the proposed model.

articleTitle: Impedance model of complex grid network based on transfer matrix
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The distribution network has a complex network architecture with a large number of connected loads and a variety of types, which makes it difficult to accurately analyze the channel characteristics of the distribution lines as a carrier signal transmission channel due to the influence of various factors. This paper constructs an simple impedance model for complex grid network based on transmission line theory and transfer matrix, and proposes a method for calculation of signal propagation attenuation on complex distribution network. Through simulation of signal transmission from 30 kHz to 30 MHz, the impedance and propagation attenuation characteristics of the power line communication link affected by the number of nodes and the distribution of nodes were analyzed.

articleTitle: An overlapping entity relation extraction method for electricity marketing audit information
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In the field of electricity marketing inspection, large amounts of unstructured text data (such as inspection reports, work orders, and supporting documentation) present significant challenges for traditional information extraction methods. Traditional pipeline-based entity relation extraction methods and joint extraction methods are difficult to solve complex problems such as overlapping relations and nested entities. To tackle these challenges, this paper proposes an entity-relationship extraction technique for electricity marketing based on a cascaded pointer network. First, in order to improve the accuracy of entity recognition, a domain-specific PowerSpanBERT model was trained by incorporating both domain text and the specialized lexicon, and adversarial training with gradient accumulation was introduced to enhance the model’s accuracy in extracting electricity marketing knowledge and predicting unfamiliar information. In the joint recognition layer for relationships and tail entities, a multi-head attention mechanism was introduced to strengthen the feature rep-resentation of the output vectors from the encoding layer, enabling joint extraction of entities and relationships. Finally, experimental results show that the pro-posed joint extraction method significantly improves knowledge extraction accuracy, achieving an F1 score of $86.04 \%$, making it a powerful tool to support advanced applications such as intelligent information retrieval and decisionmaking in marketing inspections.

articleTitle: Strategies for dealing with false data injection attacks in power grid measurement based on unsupervised learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Under the attack of false data injection, existing power data recovery methods often suffer from problems such as poor data quality and weak self-healing ability to restore a normal power grid. This article innovatively proposes a strategy for responding to false data injection attacks in power grid measurement based on unsupervised learning. Firstly, based on the basic principles of generative adversarial network (GAN) algorithm and particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, an improved generative adversarial network (IGAN) algorithm model and an improved particle swarm optimization (IPSO)algorithm model are constructed, respectively. Then, considering the correlation between power grid measurement data and their own time series characteristics and using the physical topology information of the power grid as specific labels, an improved method for recovering power grid measurement data using generative adversarial networks is proposed. Finally, simulation analysis verifies that the strategy proposed in this article can effectively solve the problem of false data caused by injection attacks on the power grid.

articleTitle: Research on the Monitoring System for the Execution Process of Power Supply and Power Grid Collaborative Project Clusters
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Under the strategic goal of building a new electricity system, the Chinese government has set higher requirements for power supply projects dominated by new energy and their supporting transmission projects: it is necessary to strengthen the overall planning and coordination of power grids and power supplies, and to connect the construction progress of source and grid projects to ensure the coordinated development of power supply and power grid. This study, based on the current situation of control of power supply projects and their supporting power grid projects, constructs a control and monitoring indicators system for source-grid collaborative project clusters from 3 phases: planning, approval, and construction. Based on the characteristics of each index, the calculation method, and the threshold values of the indicators, the warning rules for abnormal project clusters are clarified, and a statistical supervision model for the project clusters is constructed. By applying this model to identify problematic project clusters, it helps enterprises to enhance their collaborative control capabilities in the execution process, to reduce risks and ensure that the implementation of resource allocation plans conforms to the strategic goals of the building the new electricity system.

articleTitle: Research on CLLC resonant converter control hybrid strategy based on OMA
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The symmetric CLLC resonant converter permits the flow of energy in both directions with identical converter structures, while maintaining the characteristics of the original LLC resonant converter. The fundamental harmonic approximation (FHA) is often used to analyze resonant converters. Its advantage is its simplicity and intuitive nature. However, its accuracy is only maintained near the resonant frequency. Therefore, the choice of modal analysis method, according to the actual operation of the circuit, is essential for accurately describing the circuit’s operating state and gain characteristics. The control strategies that are more frequently employed in CLLC resonant converters can be classified into two principal categories: frequency control and phase-shift control. This paper presents a hybrid control strategy based on frequency control and double phase shift control, and a simulation circuit is constructed for the purpose of verifying the circuit.

articleTitle: A power feedback loop against grid frequency disturbances of virtual synchronous generators
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Output active power and frequency transient oscillations of the virtual synchronous generators (VSGs) occur under external disturbances. Existing transient improvement strategies improve the power characteristics but deteriorate the power-frequency response characteristics during grid frequency disturbances. In this regard, this paper proposes the method of parallel low-pass power feedback in the control loop, which increases the degree of freedom of the VSG, makes the improvement of phase margin possible, and effectively resists the grid frequency disturbances. Finally, a 15 kW VSG simulation model verifies the proposed method has a better ability to resist grid frequency disturbances compared with the existing VSG transient oscillation suppression methods.

articleTitle: Distributed resource low-delay interaction method for low-voltage substation based on communication quality-aware reinforcement learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In the distribution substation, edge computing can optimize the allocation and utilization of overall distributed resources, which is essential for ensuring efficient energy utilization and stable operation of the power grid. However, because of electromagnetic interference during data transmission at the device, the traditional upper confidence bound (UCB) algorithm neglects the impact of communication quality when estimating confidence bounds, leading to a deviation in the value estimation of actions and an increase in data processing delay. To tackle this issue, a distributed resource low-delay optimization algorithm for substations based on communication quality-aware UCB is proposed. Firstly, we propose the low-delay interaction architecture for low-voltage substations with communication quality-aware distributed resources. Moreover, by optimizing the data migration strategy, the problem of minimizing edge-edge collaborative data processing delay is formulated. To address this issue, we convert it into a multi-armed bandit (MAB) problem and solve it by using the proposed algorithm. This algorithm incorporates communication quality weight into the calculation formula for edge server preference value, enabling real-time awareness of migration channel quality during the data migration process and improving the efficiency of distributed resource interaction in the distribution substation. Finally, the proposed algorithm’s effectiveness is confirmed through simulation.

articleTitle: Design of an off-grid photovoltaic power generation system for a household in Xinjiang region
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This project presents the design of an off-grid photovoltaic power supply system for a user in the Xinjiang region. Based on local electricity consumption habits and the number of household appliances, the daily electricity consumption of the user is estimated at $9.824 \mathbf{k W h}$. The system utilizes five CS7N-670MS photovoltaic modules from Canadian Solar, connected in a 1 series $\times 5$ parallel configuration, with a module spacing of 3.172 m. The battery system employs AcmeG 12V 200 batteries from Narada, connected in a 4 series $\times 2$ parallel configuration. The selected inverter model is Sun2000-10kTL-M1 200vac. PVsyst software simulation indicates that with a system tilt angle of 60°, the power generation over the project's 25 -year lifespan is $109,434 \text{kWh}$. This translates to savings of $33,103.785 \text{kg}$ of standard coal equivalent, and reductions in emissions of 601.996 kg of sulfur dioxide, $96,750.599 \text{kg}$ of carbon dioxide, and 189.102 kg of nitrogen oxides. This project provides a theoretical reference for the design of household off-grid photovoltaic power generation systems.

articleTitle: Efficiency optimization for multi-coil-domino wireless power transfer system
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: To address the challenges of limited transmission range in wireless power transfer systems (WPT), domino system employs the strategy of incorporating relay coils to enhance both the transmission distance and efficiency of the system. When multiple coils are present in the system, the positioning of the coils and their crossing mutual inductance significantly influence the system’s efficiency. Therefore, this paper analyzes an n-coil system, uses the 5 -coil system as an example, and utilizes a genetic algorithm (GA) to determine the optimal spatial position for each coil, aiming to maximize system efficiency. Meanwhile, by comparing the maximum efficiency values calculated under various conditions with the actual maximum efficiency of the system, it is concluded that neglecting all cross-coupling inductance significantly simplifies the calculation and yields an efficiency value closest to the actual efficiency. This validates the rationality of neglecting all cross-coupling inductance.

articleTitle: Tie line power allocation model based on day ahead scheduling
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In the electricity market, the interconnection line serves as a key link connecting different power grid regions, and the optimization of its planned allocation is an important link to ensure the safe, economical, and efficient operation of the power system. For the tie line plan allocation problem, this paper proposes a tie line power allocation model based on the day ahead scheduling plan. Through algorithm optimization and reference to historical values, the tie line power allocation is carried out on the basis of meeting the constraints related to clearing in the province, which to a certain extent reduces the problem that the formal link of planning causes the related operating constraints to exceed the limit. The model can also adapt to the changes in grid operating conditions, and dynamically adjust the tie line power allocation. The effectiveness and applicability of the model proposed in this paper are verified through numerical example analysis.

articleTitle: Electrical Response and Energy Absorption of Surge Arresters in 35 kV Lines Under Multiple Lightning Strikes: A Simulation Study Using ATP-EMTP
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: 35 kV line lightning arrester as an important lightning protection equipment, bear the role of absorbing and releasing lightning impact energy. Multiple lightning strikes as a common natural phenomenon, its characteristics and impact on the line arrester impact on the power industry safety protection has practical reference significance. In this paper, ATP-EMTP electromagnetic transient simulation software is used to simulate the process of multiple lightning strikes, and the electrical response characteristics and energy absorption of lightning arrester under multiple lightning strikes are studied. The results of the study have a certain guiding role and reference value for the lightning protection of 35kV lines.

articleTitle: SVC suppression damping system oscillation control method considering additional line loss correlation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: As one of the important devices in flexible AC transmission systems, Static Var Compensators (SVC) can help improve the stable operation of power systems. To further enhance system stability, this paper proposes an SVC suppression damping system oscillation control method that considers additional line loss correlation. Constructing a mathematical model of a power system containing SVC, based on the analysis of the correlation between additional line losses, and introducing additional control elements to enhance system damping and suppress system oscillations as a control method. Introducing additional damping control in SVC can suppress system oscillations while regulating reactive power. Practice has shown that this method has significant advantages in suppressing low-frequency oscillations, improving voltage stability, and enhancing overall system performance, which helps to reduce power grid losses and costs.

articleTitle: Research on Active Equalization Strategy of Retired Batteries for Microgrid Energy Storage Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Retired power batteries are wired in series and parallel to create sizable battery packs for microgrid energy storage applications that necessitate more rigorous equalization management during operation. In this paper, the real-time estimation of the state of charge (SOC) of batteries is achieved through the establishment of an equivalent model of retired power batteries and the adoption of the extended Kalman filter method. A bidirectional active equalization structure is employed, wherein the SOC serves as the equalization variable. To achieve inter-battery equalization between battery packs, an inductive equalization topology and a differential fuzzy control equalization strategy are utilized. The results of the simulation analysis demonstrate that the proposed equalization method is an effective and expedient approach for addressing the inconsistency issues observed in retired battery packs.

articleTitle: A counterfactual method to measure the potential carbon emission reduction cost of Chinese grid
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This study utilizes support vector regression (SVR) technology to establish a relationship model between power cost and various related indicators. The model construction includes data collection, preprocessing, and parameter optimization using Bayesian optimization. The data influencing power costs at different times are normalized and integrated into the model to calculate predicted power cost values before the carbon market commences. The model’s predictions are validated against historical data from 2012 to 2021. By comparing actual and predicted costs before and after the carbon market starts, this study quantifies the impact of carbon market policy on power cost, providing a robust foundation for optimizing carbon emission reduction strategies. This research not only enhances understanding of the correlation between carbon markets and grid carbon emission reduction costs, but also furnishes scientific decision-making support for policymakers.

articleTitle: An Improved Multi-Verse Optimizer Algorithm For Solving The Analytic Model Of Grid Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The analytical model of grid fault diagnosis can convert the fault diagnosis problem into a 0-1 integer planning problem for solving the minimum value, so that the objective function can be solved by mathematical solution methods to get the final set of fault components. In view of the problems of omission of solutions that may occur in the processing of traditional grid analytical model problems, the corresponding weights of all levels of protection and circuit breakers are taken into account on the basis of the original analytical model, so as to make the analytical model of faults more consistent with the actual relay protection device hierarchical coordination relationship; on this basis, a grid fault diagnostic analysis model solution method based on the multivariate universe optimization algorithm is also given, aiming at the fast solution of the improved fault analysis model. The improved grid analysis model using multi-verse optimization algorithm is shown to be highly accurate with good performance of fast convergence by solving cases on IEEE14 node system.

articleTitle: Design of Intelligent Charging System for New Energy Vehicles and Research on Supercapacitor Control Scheme
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This thesis proposes a smart charging system design and supercapacitor control scheme for new energy vehicles, and the core technologies include smart dispatching technology, Internet of Things technology, smart power distribution technology, and safety technology. The system is equipped with real-time power monitoring, real-time safety detection, automatic power distribution and charging, intelligent human-machine interaction, etc. It aims to significantly enhance the charging efficiency of new energy vehicles with high efficiency, safety, and intelligence, improve the user experience, alleviate the charging troubles of vehicle owners, and promote the promotion and application of new energy vehicles. In addition, the ideal control scheme for supercapacitors in transport systems proposed in this project ensures that the power outputs of the charging system and the chassis power system are consistent by connecting the Chassis power supply to the chassis power system and using the FSBB (four-switching boost converter) to achieve constant power charging and discharging during charging to enhance the overall performance of the system. This research result not only provides new ideas for charging solutions for new energy vehicles but also lays the foundation for the intelligent development of charging infrastructure in the future.

articleTitle: Study on the influence of long cable on motor end overvoltage of a ship's power system
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the development of green intelligent ships, pure electric ships are expanding from small and medium-sized ships to medium and large ships, and from passenger ships and tourist ships to cargo ships. As a result, the distance between the motor and the converter equipment of some ships is relatively long. Due to the influence of long-line cable distribution parameters, overvoltage may be generated at the motor end of the motor to affect the motor insulation characteristics. Through theoretical analysis, simulation and evaluation of the side-over-voltage of Marine motor are carried out in this paper, and the correctness of the design simulation is verified by the test of a typical real ship.

articleTitle: Study on Hybrid Energy Storage Power Allocation Strategies for Smoothing Wind Power Fluctuations
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: To solve the wind power fluctuation problem caused by hybrid energy storage system (HESS) connected to wind farms, a HESS power allocation strategy scheme was proposed to control variations in wind power. First, the limiting average filtering algorithm was used to filter the raw wind power and the grid-connected power and HESS reference power complying with the grid connection standard were calculated. Then, the Osprey-Cauchy-Sparrow Search Algorithm (OCSSA), which integrates the osprey and Cauchy variants, was used to optimize the Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) parameters K (the quantity of modes) and $\alpha$ (the penalty component). After the optimal parameter combination [$K, \alpha$] was obtained, the HESS reference power was decomposed into high and low-frequency power constituents by VMD, which were allocated to the supercapacitor and the battery. The numerical example results showed that the proposed HESS power allocation strategy can effectively improve the economic efficiency of HESS.

articleTitle: Compressive Sensing based Channel Estimation Method for MIMO-OFDM Power Line Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Due to the complex nature of the power line channel and the interference of impulse noise, the performance of traditional channel estimation methods is limited in low signal-to-noise ratio environments. To overcome these challenges, this paper proposed a compressive sensing based channel estimation method for MIMO-OFDM PLC. Considering the sparse characteristics of the power line communication channel, the method reconstructs the sparse channel using the Orthogonal Matching Pursuit (OMP) algorithm, effectively improving the accuracy and speed of channel estimation. In MIMO systems, this method can estimate multiple sub-channels simultaneously, fully leveraging the advantages of multiple input multiple output. Simulation results demonstrate a significant performance improvement of the proposed algorithm compared to traditional methods under the same signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) conditions, validating the effectiveness and robustness of the algorithm. This study provides a new technical approach to enhance the communication quality and reliability of MIMO-OFDM PLC systems.

articleTitle: Pilot Protection of Voltage Source Converter High Voltage Direct Current Transmission Line Based on Directional Traveling Wave Amplitude
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the development of High Voltage Direct Current (HVDC) transmission technology, the limitations of traditional protection methods in dealing with complex fault conditions have become increasingly apparent. This paper proposes a pilot protection method for Voltage Source Converter (VSC)-HVDC transmission lines based on the amplitude of directional traveling waves and designs a novel directional traveling wave amplitude protection algorithm. This algorithm utilizes the arrival time and amplitude information of traveling waves to quickly identify and locate fault positions. By detailing the basic principles of directional traveling wave amplitude and exploring its feasibility in VSC-HVDC systems, a specific protection algorithm process was designed, including fault detection, traveling wave direction determination, and fault location. Simulation results indicate that the algorithm can quickly and accurately identify and locate faults under various fault conditions, significantly enhancing the operational safety and stability of VSC-HVDC transmission systems. VSC-HVDC systems have significant advantages in long-distance, highcapacity transmission, and submarine cable transmission, particularly due to their flexible power control, absence of commutation failure, and compact design. However, existing protection methods have shortcomings in terms of rapid response, selectivity, and anti-interference capability. The protection method based on directional traveling wave amplitude detects the arrival time and amplitude of traveling waves by monitoring voltage and current traveling wave signals on the line, thus achieving fault location. Simulation experiments were designed for different scenarios, including Direct Current (DC)-side short-circuit faults, grounding faults, and Alternating Current(AC)-side faults, to comprehensively evaluate the algorithm’s performance. The results show that the algorithm can detect traveling wave signals within a few milliseconds after a fault occurs and quickly locate the fault point, with a location error of less than 50 meters.

articleTitle: Research on miniaturization application of large language model in power industry
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper discusses the application of large language model (LLM) in the miniaturization of power industry. This paper first introduces the basic principles of LLM and Transformer model, and then makes a comprehensive comparison of several mainstream Chinese LLM models to analyze their characteristics and performance. The core part of the study elaborates the construction process of knowledge base for the power industry, which provides a high-quality industry-specific data set for the subsequent model training. The performance of untuned LLM, knowledge base tuned LLM and modified knowledge base tuned LLM are compared by using low-rank decomposition method. The experimental results show that the LLM trained by the improved power industry knowledge base has achieved significant improvement in all three indexes and is most suitable for miniaturization applications in the power industry. The research results are important for promoting the implementation of LLM technology in real industries, as well as promoting the intelligent and digital transformation of the power industry.

articleTitle: Classification and recognition method of aerial photo insulators based on improved K-means algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Insulator is one of the most important infrastru ctures in transmission lines, and its accurate identification is an important prerequisite for self-monitoring and fault diagnosis of transmission lines. In order to accurately identify the insulators in UAV aerial photography inspection, a classification and identification method based on improved K-means algorithm was proposed. Firstly, the insulator image is processed gray-scale, and the improved K-means algorithm is used to cluster the gray-scale image. Secondly, the segmentation defect is compensated by morphological filtering. Finally, according to the mean color difference of the target area of the insulator, the classification problem of the insulator is simplified to a one-dimensional data classification problem, so as to achieve classification recognition. The experimental results show that the proposed method can quickly and accurately classify and identify the insulators under complex background and the same shooting Angle, and the total recognition rate can reach $\mathbf{9 5. 5 6 \%}$, which provides a new idea for the classification and recognition of transmission line insulators in UAV inspection.

articleTitle: Capacity optimization configuration and economic analysis of off-grid type wind-photovoltaic-hydropower-hydrogen energy coupling system
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Aiming at the problems of low energy efficiency and poor economy in the off-grid hydrogen energy coupling new energy system, this paper innovatively proposes the method of capacity optimization configuration (COC) of off-grid type wind-photovoltaic-hydropower-hydrogen energy coupling system. Firstly, a multi-objective function is constructed to minimize the cost of hydrogen production and the abandonment rate of new energy (wind and PV). Secondly, based on the net power condition of the system, the optimal operation control strategy (OCS) of the multi coupling system is proposed. Then, the multi-objective function is combined with the control strategy to form the COC model, and the constraints such as the upper and lower limits of the electrolytic cell are taken as constraints, and the improved particle swarm optimization algorithm (IPSOA) is used to solve the COC model. Finally, the effectiveness and economy of the proposed method are verified by analyzing the results of capacity allocation and economy.

articleTitle: Learning-Integrated Unit Commitment Optimization Based on GCN-GRU and Load Scenario Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Unit commitment (UC) is a fundamental problem in power systems, typically formulated as a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) model. As the scale of the system expands, numerous variables and constraints, especially binary variables, impose a significant computational burden on solving the UC problem. This paper proposes a learning-integrated optimization framework to accelerate the solution of the UC problem. First, a graph convolutional network (GCN)-gated recurrent unit (GRU) based model is employed to predict commitment decisions. Next, multiple prediction models are established by clustering load scenarios to reduce learning complexity. Finally, the UC problem is solved by fixing high-confidence predictions through confidence filtering. Case studies conducted on the IEEE 118-bus system using data generated from real-world load scenario characteristics demonstrate that the proposed framework effectively accelerates the solution of the UC problem with only a slight loss in solution quality.

articleTitle: Research on the evaluation system of MR model engine for three dimensional auxiliary maintenance of GIS equipment in pumped storage power stations
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The increasing demand for efficient and safe operation of pumped storage power plants has highlighted the importance of three-dimensional auxiliary maintenance of GIS (Gas Insulated Switchgear) equipment. Mixed Reality (MR) technology has demonstrated immense potential in the maintenance of power plant equipment. This paper proposes an evaluation system for MR model engines, focusing on Unity 3D and Unreal Engine, specifically for three-dimensional auxiliary maintenance of GIS equipment in pumped storage power plants. The system comprehensively assesses various dimensions, including graphics rendering quality, ease of use, cross-platform support, community resources, performance optimization, development cost, user experience, plugin extensibility, and technical support. The results indicate that this evaluation system effectively evaluates the application of different engines in the construction of MR models for GIS equipment in pumped storage power plants, providing a basis for decision-making in the development of MR models for three-dimensional auxiliary maintenance of GIS equipment.

Author Keywords: Pumped storage power plant GIS equipment

articleTitle: Load optimization configuration method for electric vehicle charging stations based on second-order cone programming algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In order to achieve State of Charge (SOC) control of battery packs, optimize grid load, and extend battery life. Propose a load optimization configuration method for electric vehicle charging stations based on second-order cone programming algorithm. Firstly, the equivalent circuit models of first-order RC and second-order RC power batteries were analyzed, and the mathematical relationship between output voltage and input current was established. Next, the ensemble learning method of feature combination stacking fusion is adopted to predict SOC, in order to improve the accuracy of prediction. Finally, based on the predicted SOC values, a charging control strategy was proposed, and the charging behavior was optimized using a second-order cone programming algorithm to reduce grid load fluctuations and peak valley differences. The research results indicate that this method not only improves the accuracy of SOC prediction, but also achieves SOC balancing of the battery pack, which helps to extend the service life of power batteries.

articleTitle: A method for sensing the operating status of switchable residual current transformers based on information entropy
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In response to the problem of poor perception accuracy of the operating state of open close leakage current transformers, this paper proposes a method for sensing the operating state of open close leakage current transformers based on information entropy. This method utilizes information entropy theory to conduct in-depth analysis of a large amount of data during the operation of transformers, in order to quantify the uncertainty and information content in the data. By calculating the entropy of information, real-time monitoring and evaluation of the health status of transformers can be achieved, effectively identifying abnormal operating conditions and warning potential faults in advance. The experimental results show that this method has higher sensitivity and accuracy, and has better efficiency in sensing the operating status of open close leakage transformers, providing strong guarantees for the safe and stable operation of power systems.

articleTitle: Numerical study on the combustion process of different coal blending in 1795t/h boiler
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: By numerically simulating the combustion process in a 1795t/h boiler blended with Shenhun No. 2 coal under different blending conditions, the temperature field of the furnace combustion simulation results and the distribution of flue gas temperature at the furnace exit were studied. The results show that when blending more Shenhun No. 2 coal, the temperature inside the furnace will increase, and the exit temperature of the furnace chamber will also increase accordingly, while the softening temperature of ash of Shenhun No. 2 coal is low compared with that of bituminous coal, which limits the number layers of Shenhun No.2, at the same time, the oxygen concentration at the furnace outlet decreases, the carbon monoxide concentration increases, and the reducing atmosphere increases, increasing the probability of coking, so the maximum blending of Shenhun No. 2 under the premise of safe operation of the boiler The safe way to mix No. 2 is the working condition3: $\mathrm{A}, \mathrm{B}, \mathrm{C}, \mathrm{D}$ four layers of blending Shenhun No. 2,. The analysis of the simulation results of blending of coal combustion of Shenhua coal No. 2 can provide a reference for the blending coal combustion of the same type of boiler.

articleTitle: Effect of AC Voltage Frequency on Partial Discharge Characteristics of GIS
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In recent years, the development of advanced power electronic technology has created favorable conditions for high-voltage and high-power converters, and power transmission is no longer limited to the traditional power frequency, and low-frequency transmission system has become an important direction of power development in the new century. Partial discharge (PD) is an important index of insulation state evaluation of electrical equipment. The on-line detection and fault diagnosis evaluation of PD under low frequency environment are still lacking of engineering practice and reference standards. Therefore, this paper takes power GIS equipment as the object, designs four typical insulation defects, and conducts partial discharge experiments from 20Hz to 100Hz based on UHF method. The discharge characteristics of typical GIS insulation defects under low frequency environment and power frequency environment are compared and analyzed. PDIV, PDEV, discharge phase, pulse repetition rate, discharge amplitude and other parameters of partial discharge change with frequency were compared and analyzed. Meanwhile, the difference between low frequency and power frequency discharge spectrum was studied, providing reference for GIS partial discharge type diagnosis at low frequency.

articleTitle: High-temperature superconducting energy storage technology for new diversified power systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Given the escalating shortage of fossil energy and the worsening environmental pollution, the development and utilization of renewable energy have emerged as the primary focus of global energy development. However, the diversification of energy access to power systems will bring challenges in terms of stability and supply-demand balance. The rapid development of electric vehicles and the growth of global energy demand further exacerbate the complexity. High-temperature superconducting energy storage technology, with its high efficiency and fast energy storage characteristics, exhibits great application potential in stabilizing fluctuations, improving stability and power supply quality, optimizing energy distribution, and reducing transmission losses. The research and application of high-temperature superconducting materials provide support for it, and commercial applications have become a realistic possibility. As renewable energy progresses and the energy structure evolves, high-temperature superconducting energy storage technology is anticipated to play a crucial role in shaping a new, diversified power system and fostering an intelligent, efficient, and sustainable energy supply system.

articleTitle: Variable Load Electric Vehicle Speed Regulation Feedforward Compensation Composite Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: A feedforward compensation composite control method for a variable load electric vehicle speed regulation system transforms the traditional control model based on surface-mounted permanent magnet synchronous motors into a state equation of system error. This method effectively characterizes the system’s adaptability to variable load conditions. By combining the boundary term with the first and second system states, a feedforward compensation composite control is designed and its stability is proven. Both theoretical and practical validations demonstrate the effectiveness of the designed method.

articleTitle: Intelligent optimization design of antipodal Vivaldi antenna for partial discharge detection of cables
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In this study, a modified non-dominated sorting whale optimization algorithm (MNSWOA) is utilized for optimizing UHF antennas for partial discharge (PD) detection to satisfy the requirements of minimal return loss and maximal gain in the target frequency band. Based on an elite retention strategy, MNSWOA, significantly improving algorithm optimization and increasing population diversity, employs the one-point binary crossover and polynomial variation. Then, a Pareto optimal solution is selected as the proposed UHF antenna. Finally the experimental results demonstrate that the antenna achieves a reflection coefficient of less than -10 dB and an average gain of 4.4 dBi within the frequency range from 1 GHz to 3 GHz.

articleTitle: An overview of the current status of V2G technology in improving grid resilience
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper reviews the research and application of electric vehicles (EVs) and vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technologies in enhancing power system resilience, analyzes the potential of EVs as distributed energy storage resources for grid load management and emergency power supply, and explores smart charging strategies, distributed energy participation, and emergency response capabilities during grid failures and natural disasters. Meanwhile, the article discuss-es technical challenges, social acceptance, battery life, and charging facility compatibility, and proposes corresponding policy and technology recommendations with a view to improving the rapid resilience and resilience of the power system to extreme events.

articleTitle: Day-ahead Scheduling of Distribution Network with Electric Vehicle based Virtual Power Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The electric vehicle (EV) is a promising tool to provide flexibility to the distribution system operator (DSO). However, the massive quantities of EVs make it very challenging to harness their flexibility. One of the promising ways is to formulate the EV at charging station (CS) as a virtual power plant (VPP). Firstly, the EV flexibility is estimated with time and energy index, then the VPP is formulated with EV at the same CS. And then during day-ahead scale, the VPP will participate in the energy market, which enables DSO to utilize EV based VPP flexibilities and provide auxiliary services to improve system efficiency, such as peak-shaving and valley-filling. Simulation test demonstrated the effectives of the approach proposed in this paper. Comparison tests are conducted between the proposed approach and the uncoordinated charging, which demonstrated the approach employed in this paper can offer a tradeoff solution between the total cost and operation efficiency.

articleTitle: Evaluation method for voltage flexibility of DN considering spatiotemporal characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In response to the difficulty of evaluating the voltage flexibility (VF) of distribution network (DN) with a high proportion of distributed photovoltaics from multiple perspectives, this paper proposes a VF evaluation method for DN that considers spatiotemporal characteristics. Firstly, the evaluation indicators for the spatiotemporal flexibility of distribution network voltage (DNV) were defined from two dimensions: time and space. The evaluation indicators were combined with constraints such as power flow models and line voltage and current to construct a DNV flexibility evaluation model. Then, the solution process for the spatiotemporal flexibility evaluation model of DNV was provided. Finally, taking the improved IEEE33 node grid structure as an example, a comparative analysis was conducted on the flexibility of DNV under different distributed photovoltaic penetration rates, verifying the effectiveness of the method proposed in this paper.

articleTitle: Photovoltaic Power Prediction Model Based on Dual Domain Decomposition and Dual Network Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In order to improve the accuracy of Photovoltaic (PV) power prediction, a model considering signal decomposition technique and hybrid deep learning is proposed. First, a dualdomain decomposition model based on maximal overlap discrete wavelet transform (MODWT) and complete ensemble empirical mode decomposition with adaptive noise (CEEMDAN) is proposed to preprocess the data. Secondly, these components are correlated and analyzed into temporal and stochastic components, where the temporal component is input into the long short-term memory network for training, and the stochastic component with several types of environmental factors is jointly input into the convolutional neural networks (CNN) for training, and then the component predictions of the dual network are reconstructed to obtain the point prediction results. The examples show that the proposed model for the point prediction session is optimal among all models of the setup, and the average absolute error (MAE), mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) and root mean square error (RMSE) are improved by 21.75%, 15.84%, and 21.11%, respectively, compared to the dual decomposition single mesh model, which is the best performer among the compared models.

articleTitle: An improved FCS-MPC strategy for quadratic boost converter with CPL
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper proposes an improved finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC) strategy, which provides a new solution for the control of the quadratic boost converter (QBC) with constant power load (CPL) in the DC microgrids. Based on the internal model principle, the negative impedance characteristic of the CPL is embedded into MPC as a distinctive feature. Under the control of the improved FCS-MPC, the control accuracy of the output voltage is visibly improved. When the load or input changes, the robustness of the proposed strategy is significantly enhanced compared with the dual-loop PI. Meanwhile, the proposed controller is simple in design and easy to implement. The simulation verified the effectiveness of the proposed control strategy.

Author Keywords: finite control set model predictive control (FCS-MPC)

articleTitle: Study on low-carbon optimal operation of park-level integrated energy system considering light intensity, temperature, and wind speed correlation scenario generation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In this paper, the relationship between wind speed, temperature, and light intensity is explored, and a joint density function of the three is constructed using the kernel density function and Gaussian-Copula, so as to derive typical scenarios to reduce the uncertainty of renewable energy. In addition, an optimization model including carbon transaction cost is established in this paper, which is proven to be effective in reducing carbon emissions through comparative analysis of examples, demonstrating its potential and application value in optimizing the operation of integrated energy systems.

articleTitle: FDRformer: A Transformer-based electrical substation flooding disaster risk forecasting model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In this paper, we propose FDRformer model, a novel Transformer-based model designed for substation flooding disaster risk prediction. The model integrates a gated feature selection network and an encoder-decoder network to effectively reduce redundant information and capture complex nonlinear relationships among multiple variables, thereby enhancing prediction accuracy. Using real-world data from an electric power research institute in central China, the FDRformer model is trained and evaluated. Experimental results show that FDRformer outperforms existing machine learning and deep learning models, achieving a $32.87 \%$ reduction in RMSE compared to conventional deep learning methods. The proposed model is highly effective in predicting flood risks, providing valuable insights for disaster mitigation and resource allocation in substation management.

articleTitle: Virtual power consumption rights trading mechanism for multiple prosumers in distribution systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Demand response is an effective way to address electricity supply shortages. However, traditional incentive-based and price-based demand response mechanisms have drawbacks of sacrificing user autonomy and lacking control precision, respectively. Therefore, China is currently exploring a new mechanism based on virtual electricity rights trading. This paper introduces a novel virtual power consumption rights trading mechanism designed for multiple prosumers to ensure the economic operation of distribution systems under conditions of insufficient power supply. The proposed mechanism coordinates power consumption rights among prosumers, allocating these rights to those with a higher willingness to consume electricity, thus maintaining an economical state for the distribution system during power shortages. Simulation results show that, using the proposed mechanism, allowing power consumption rights trading significantly increases the net profit of each prosumer and reduces load reduction losses for high-loss prosumers compared to cases where trading is not allowed. This verifies the effectiveness of the proposed mechanism.

articleTitle: Application of fan coil + floor radiation system in a villa in Jinan
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper comprehensively considers the factors such as comfort, initial investment and operating cost, and takes a villa in Jinan as an example to design the air conditioning system. It adopts the form of fan coil + floor radiant heating, and the cold and heat source adopts the air source heat pump. Airpark software was used to simulate indoor thermal comfort under fan-coil cooling in summer and radiant floor heating in winter, both of which met the requirements of indoor thermal comfort levels. At the same time, compared with traditional heating methods, fan-coil + floor radiant heating system has low operating cost and high energy saving.

articleTitle: Energy System Fault Reconstruction Control Strategy Based on Multi-agent Deep Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In order to achieve intelligent management of faults in the energy system of stratospheric airships, this paper proposes an energy system fault reconstruction control strategy based on multi-agent deep reinforcement learning. For the architecture of distributed energy cabins, an agent is equipped for each energy cabin. Multiple agents share the same dueling double deep Qlearning (D3QN) strategy to accelerate the training process of the agents. A simulation environment was set up in the Gym of Open AI, and the results showed that the method proposed in this paper can effectively achieve rapid reconstruction of energy systems after single point and multi-point simultaneous failures.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Temperature Rise Characteristics for Structural Parameters of Triple-opening Busbar applied to Large-Capacity GIS
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In order to realise the practical application of threeopening busbar in large-capacity GIS, it is necessary to fully grasp the temperature rise response characteristics of the specific structural parameters of the three-opening busbar, so as to guide the product design. In this paper, the method of numerical simulation calculations, through a simplified calculation model to study the angle of rotation (opening direction), gap degree, conductor wall thickness on the temperature rise response characteristics of large-capacity SGIS internal, the results show that: with the increase of the angle of rotation, the system’s maximum steady-state temperature rise value successively decreases, when $\gamma=0^{\circ}$ has a better temperature rise performance; with the increase of the opening degree, the system’s maximum steady state temperature rise value is first rapidly reduced and then increased, when $\beta$ in the 10° to 20° has better temperature rise performance; with the increase in conductor wall thickness, the maximum steady-state temperature rise value of the system first decrease tends to flatten out, and then a slight rise, taking into account the performance of the temperature rise and manufacturing costs, the recommended conductor wall thickness is greater than 1.6 times the depth of metal penetration. Targeted design in accordance with the laws studied in this paper can significantly improve the internal temperature rise performance of GIS, which can provide guidance for the application of threeopening busbar in large-capacity GIS.

articleTitle: Research on Two-Switch Bridge Buck-Boost Converter Based on Active Disturbance Rejection Control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Power electronic converters, especially buck-boost circuits, play a vital role in energy management, electric vehicles, renewable energy systems and other fields. Due to the traditional PID control, there are some problems such as complex parameter setting, accurate mathematical model, sensitivity to external interference and limited response speed. In this paper, the second-order active disturbance rejection control is used as the basic control structure of the main circuit, which solves the problems of slow dynamic response speed, complex parameter setting and high accuracy of model requirements of PID control. At the same time, the selection of the main circuit structure also has the function of realizing wide input, which can be applied to many occasions. Finally, by analyzing and comparing the output voltage waveforms under the active disturbance rejection control strategy and the double closed-loop proportional integral control applied in different working conditions, the robustness and effectiveness of the active disturbance rejection control strategy applied in this paper are verified.

articleTitle: Consider the independent multi-micro-grid coordination of the demand-side response and the energy management
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In order to optimize resource allocation and improve the system economy, enhance the reliability of power system, promote the integration of renewable energy, enhance user participation, and provide data support for policy formulation, this paper proposes the independent multi-micro grid coordinated energy management. First, the independent operation model of multi-micro grid based on the improved particle swarm optimization algorithm is constructed, and taking into account demand-side response technologies, a variety of operation modes are constructed, and examples are solved on MATLAB2018B simulation software, and then the benefits of demand response technology on the coordination and optimization results of multi-microgrid system are analyzed. Simulation results show that the coordinated management of independent multi-microgrids considering demand side response provides an important guarantee for realizing an intelligent, green and sustainable energy future.

articleTitle: Research on Grounding Fault Location of Large Hydropower Station Generator Transformer Unit
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: At present, the grounding protection of the generator cannot locate single-phase grounding faults in the generator transformer unit.
