This article first conducts simulation analysis on single-phase grounding faults in the generator transformer unit, then introduces the fault location method through case studies, and finally conducts theoretical analysis and verification on the case of ferromagnetic resonance caused by single-phase grounding.

articleTitle: Research on the Propagation Characteristics of Partial Discharge Signals in 10kV Three-Phase Cable
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Currently, damped AC (DAC) voltage technique is extensively used in the field of insulation defect detection for 10 kV distribution cables. However, with the ongoing efforts to improve quality and efficiency in power enterprises, researchers have proposed conducting simultaneous three-phase partial discharge tests during DAC voltage experiments. Yet, the propagation characteristics of partial discharge signals across different phases during simultaneous detection remain under-researched. This paper employs the ATP-EMTP electromagnetic transient software to establish a simulation model, a typical three-phase distribution cable model was established using the LCC module, and a partial discharge source based on the three-capacitor model was positioned in the middle section of the cable. At the connection point between the DAC high voltage output and the three-phase cable, the three-phase partial discharge detection unit facilitates the detection of partial discharge signals across the three phases and isolates the high-frequency signal transmission channels between phases. By analyzing the simulation data from the partial discharge detection, the feasibility and effectiveness of conducting simultaneous three-phase partial discharge testing during DAC testing have been validated.

articleTitle: Simulation study on flue gas heat exchanger before dust collector in coal-fired power plant boiler
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The heat loss of flue gas from coal-fired power plant boilers accounts for the largest proportion of boiler heat loss, and installing flue gas heat exchangers for waste heat recovery can improve the economics of power plants. The flue gas composition after coal combustion contains a certain share of fly ash, especially for lignite. Fly ash has a significant impact on the flue gas heat exchanger, causing instability in the flow field, poor heat transfer, increased wear, and other adverse effects. This article takes the flue gas heat exchanger installed in front of the dust collector as the research object, conducts simulations of the deposition of fly ash particles and heat transfer on the heating surface of the flue gas heat exchanger, and conducts optimization research on the structure of the flue gas heat exchanger’s heating surface. Based on the simulation results, corresponding conclusions are drawn, providing a basis for further optimizing and improving the flue gas heat exchanger.

articleTitle: Multi-objective Cuckoo Boundary Search based Partitioning Flexible Interconnection Grid Planning Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The stochastic and volatile nature of large-scale new energy grid integration has posed a major challenge to the new power system. In this paper, we firstly introduce the reliability indicator system for planning the AC-DC interconnected main grid, which accounts for the spatio-temporal distribution, and then we comprehensively assess and optimize the reliability of AC/DC hybrid grid based on the spatio-temporal distribution characteristics. Secondly, an optimization problem is constructed to optimize different performance indicators in a compromise manner. Thirdly, a multi-objective cuckoo search optimization based partitioning flexible interconnection grid planning algorithm is proposed, which is able to quickly find the global optimal solution or near-optimal solution, adapting to the system demand changes and taking into account a variety of practical constraints. Finally, simulation results verify that the proposed algorithm improves the convergence performance by 37.15% and $\mathbf{5 9. 3 1 \%}$, and the adaptability by $\mathbf{7 1. 3 2 \%}$ and 78.24%, respectively, compared with the two baseline algorithms.

articleTitle: A real-time early warning method for water leakage in steel pipe section of inlet ball valve of pumped storage power plant based on visual perception
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Since the environment of pumped storage power plants is usually more complex, and the water leakage phenomenon is manifested as tiny water droplets or fine streams, the real-time early warning system needs to process the image data and respond quickly, which puts forward high requirements on the processing speed and efficiency of the algorithms. Therefore, this study aims to propose a real-time early warning method for water leakage in the steel pipe section of the intake ball valve of a pumped storage power plant based on visual perception, in order to help find and deal with water leakage problems in time, and to ensure the safety and stability of power plant operation. Firstly, a high-resolution camera is used to monitor the inlet ball valve steel pipe section in real time and obtain the video data of the pipe. Then, the video data is analysed and identified through image processing and computer vision technology to detect whether there is water leakage in the pipeline. Then, combined with real-time data transmission technology, the detection results are transmitted to the monitoring centre or relevant staff in a timely manner to achieve real-time warning and response to water leakage events. Finally, the accuracy and reliability of the method in the water leakage warning of the intake pipe of pumped storage power plants are verified through experimental validation to provide technical support for improving the safety management level of power plants.

articleTitle: Research on an Intelligent Identification Method for Carbon Monitoring Big Data Anomaly Based on Improved Support Vector Machine
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Conventional carbon monitoring big data anomaly identification and definition methods are mostly target-based division, and the scope of identification is limited, resulting in an increase in the error rate. To this end, a study on an intelligent identification method for carbon monitoring big data anomalies based on improved support vector machines is proposed. According to the current measurement needs, data preprocessing and abnormal feature extraction are first performed, and the limit values are broken through a two-way definition method to complete the fuzzy definition of failure outliers and outlier outliers. On this basis, an improved support vector machine carbon monitoring big data anomaly intelligent identification model is constructed, and a dynamic continuous monitoring method is used to realize anomaly intelligent identification processing. The test results show that: for five randomly selected test groups, compared with the deep belief network data anomaly identification method and the improved M-robust regression data online anomaly identification method, the improved support vector abnormal data identification method designed this time finally obtained. The misidentification rate is relatively low and can be controlled below 15%. This shows that with the assistance of improved support vectors, the designed anomaly identification method in carbon monitoring big data is more targeted and stable, and can perform better in different background environments, the overall efficiency and accuracy of this recognition form are also higher.

articleTitle: High precision and strong anti-interference performance positioning technology for multi-port synchronous detection using electroacoustic joint detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In order to understand the high-precision and strong anti-interference performance positioning technology of electro acoustic joint detection, research on multi-port synchronous detection of electro acoustic joint high-precision and strong anti-interference performance positioning technology has been proposed. This paper first introduces the performance and development architecture of TMS320C6678, and explains the peripherals to be used. Secondly, the specific process of the time difference frequency difference joint positioning algorithm in multi-core DSP parallel operation and the workflow of the entire system was introduced. Finally, the system was tested and analyzed, mainly focusing on the testing of positioning time and accuracy, as well as the impact of multi-core and single-core positioning. Through analysis, it was found that the joint positioning of time difference and frequency difference can be processed on multiple cores to achieve faster and more accurate target positioning. This verified that the processing speed of multiple cores is better than that of a single core, and finally verified the rationality and feasibility of this system.

articleTitle: Study on Surface Charge Distribution of Scaled-down Gas-Insulated Bushings under High-Voltage Direct Current
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The capacitor core-SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> composite insulation sleeve is widely used in ultra-high voltage engineering, and the interface between the capacitor core and SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> is prone to surface charge accumulation in the strong normal component of the DC electric field. The uneven surface charges accumulated in the insulation layer and core of the casing will distort the nearby electric field, becoming a trigger for flashover accidents and threatening the safe and reliable operation of the casing. This article discusses the direct current voltage applied to gas reduction sleeves under different voltages and polarization times. The results indicate that the core of the reduced ratio bushing capacitor is mainly composed of positive polarity charges, and the gas side current is the main source of charge accumulation. As the absolute value of the applied voltage increases, the positive polarity charge gradually increases on the inner wall of the shrink fit sleeve sheath, and the solid body current gradually increases. It is speculated that the formation of charge spots is caused by tiny metal particles adsorbed on the surface. The accumulation of surface charges in both the inner core of the casing and the Fr4 shell may be due to uneven material distribution in practice. The positive charge at the end of the core and the negative charge of the sheath will increase the gas insulation pressure, resulting in radial electric field distortion. This article provides experimental evidence and theoretical basis for the potential safety hazards that may exist during the operation of actual real casing.

articleTitle: Study on stability control of flexible DC transmission system based on VSG
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: At present, the construction and operation of the flexible DC transmission project has been launched, because the overall rotational inertia of the power grid is reduced, the traditional PQ control is difficult to support the system in voltage magnitude and frequency. For this reason, VSG technology is introduced into the flexible DC transmission system to increase the system’s stability and realize the friendly support to the grid. This paper analyzes the flexible DC transmission control technology based on a virtual synchronous motor, analyzes its control strategy and system stability, and conducts a test in the Yu-E project to compare the existing PQ control strategy technology. After the test, the results show that the VSG control strategy system meets the system requirements.

articleTitle: Random forest based heating power prediction for single crystal furnace
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The thermal output of the heating element undergoes temporal variations throughout the fabrication of monocrystalline silicon via the Czochralski process. The isodiameter stage is the most critical link in the whole crystal pulling process. This marks the shift from the neck growth phase to the phase where the crystal maintains a consistent diameter, significantly influencing the final quality of the crystal rods. The heater power has a direct influence on the heat field distribution inside the furnace. Given the difficulty of measuring this internal temperature distribution directly, achieving control objectives requires indirect methods, such as optimizing the temperature regulation path. Throughout the isodiameter phase, adjustments to the heater’s power output should be made dynamically using real-time production data to ensure stable hot zone temperatures. This study introduces a model for forecasting heater power, utilizing the random forest algorithm to enable real-time predictions. Test outcomes indicate that the model exhibits strong prediction accuracy and robustness, offering a novel technological solution for controlling crystal growth.

articleTitle: Research on data processing of power terminal plug and play system based on convolutional neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to use convolutional neural network (CNN) to improve the data processing capability of power terminal plug and play system, and realize intelligent equipment identification and fault diagnosis. Firstly, real-time data of power terminal equipment, including voltage, current and power signals, is collected and pre-processed to improve data quality through de-noising and normalization. Then, the CNN architecture suitable for power data processing is designed, including input layer, convolution layer, pooling layer, fully connected layer and output layer, and ReLU activation function and cross entropy loss function are used. Large-scale power system data sets are used for model training, parameters are adjusted by optimization algorithms, and model performance is evaluated by cross-validation and test data. Experimental results show that the CNN-based system is superior to traditional methods in feature extraction, recognition accuracy and real-time performance.

articleTitle: Source-Sink Matching Optimization Based on the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Effective matching of CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission sources and storage sites is a critical prerequisite for the successful implementation of Carbon Capture, Utilization, and Storage (CCUS) technologies. In this study, we employ the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm to solve the source-sink matching optimization problem, and enhance the traditional PPO algorithm by incorporating techniques such as orthogonal initialization, state normalization, gradient clipping, and learning rate decay, realizing the solution of the source-sink matching optimization problem by unconventional mathematical modeling methods. The results demonstrate that the proposed algorithm not only ensures efficient iteration and convergence speed but also consistently delivers high-quality solutions. This advancement provides new technical support for optimizing the matching of carbon sources and sinks.

articleTitle: Multi attribute data classification mining method for power grid cloud platform
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In order to achieve efficient processing of complex multidimensional data generated by power grid operation and improve the intelligence level of power grid operation, this paper studies the multi-attribute data classification mining method in the power grid cloud platform. This method uses decision tree optimization and feature selection techniques to extract key attribute features from power grid data. Based on the C5.0 decision tree algorithm, it accurately identifies and classifies key attributes in power grid data, thereby achieving real-time monitoring, anomaly detection, and optimized scheduling of power grid status. The experimental results show that this method has high accuracy and good classification efficiency in mining multi-attribute data on the power grid cloud platform, which can improve the stability and security of power grid operation and provide strong data support for the refined management and decision-making of smart grids.

articleTitle: Design and application of new distributed photovoltaic anti-islanding protection device
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In recent years, the proportion of investment in distributed photovoltaic power generation has been increasing. However, when grid-connected power generation systems experience islanding effects, the quality of power supply to the entire power network and the personal safety of grid staff can be severely compromised. To address this issue, this paper proposes a new type of distributed photovoltaic anti-islanding protection device. The device is characterized by its simplicity and ease of implementation, reliable operation, and low cost. It eliminates the potential pitfalls associated with “islanding operation” and resolves the “island” risk that has plagued grid systems for years.

articleTitle: Anomalous Power Usage Pattern Detection Based on Markov Model Clustering
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Cluster analysis of the features of the load profile has the problem of difficult feature construction. In the face of a large amount of smart meter data, this paperuses a data dimensionality reduction method based on symbolic aggregation approximation (SAX), and proposes a new dynamic clustering method for electricity consumption behaviour. The term dynamic refers to the transition trend between electricity consumption states in neighbouring periods. The method is applied to the detection of anomalous electricity consumption patterns, which improves the detection rate and accuracy of the anomalies.

articleTitle: Research on the performance evaluation model of intelligent distribution network from the perspective of low-carbon development
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the increasing global attention to environmental sustainability and low-carbon development, the smart distribution network not only improves the efficiency and reliability of the power system, but also promotes the low-carbon and sustainable use of energy. In this paper, we propose a joint analysis method of TOPSIS + gray correlation degree based on combination empowerment, and construct a comprehensive evaluation system for the performance of intelligent distribution network. First of all, the weight is determined by the entropy weight method and the hierarchical analysis method to achieve a comprehensive evaluation of the benefits of all aspects of the intelligent distribution network. Then, based on the grey correlation degree analysis improved by TOPSIS, the sample data were analyzed and then the evaluation results were obtained, which verified the high rationality and effectiveness.

articleTitle: Loss Reduction Potential Mining Method for Distribution Networks Based on Improved Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Large-scale access of distributed PV to the power grid has become a future trend, which is easy to cause problems such as power flow reversal, resulting in an increase in system line loss. In this paper, a method for mining the loss reduction potential of the distribution network based on the improved genetic algorithm is proposed, the distributed photovoltaic and energy storage components are selected as the reactive power compensation devices, and the multi-objective function is established by embodying the sub-objectives in the form of penalty functions, and the loss reduction potential and related optimization parameters of the distribution network are finally obtained based on the improved genetic algorithm, and the simulation verification is carried out by the IEEE30 node test system. The results show that the proposed method can obtain the potential loss reduction potential of the distribution network.

articleTitle: Transmission Line Lightning Fault Detection Based on Fiber Optic Temperature Measurement Recursive Accumulative Average Denoising
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Fiber optic temperature sensors are widely used for temperature monitoring of transmission lines due to their insulation, corrosion resistance, and resistance to electromagnetic interference. Therefore, this paper proposes a transmission line lightning fault detection method based on fiber optic temperature measurement recursive cumulative average denoising. Firstly, use fiber optic temperature sensors to obtain preliminary data for lightning fault detection in transmission lines. Then, in order to optimize the results of fiber optic temperature measurement and detection, a recursive cumulative average denoising method is used to process the collected data, reduce noise interference, and improve the signal-to-noise ratio of the signal. Standardize the collected sample frequency values within the range of $500-950 \mathrm{kHz}$, and based on the calculation results of the fault characteristic vector of the transient current traveling wave frequency window, divide the lightning fault frequency band information into three levels: A, B, and C. Among them, A level indicates that lightning activity is far away, B level indicates that lightning is more likely and close, and C level indicates that lightning is about to occur and very close, requiring immediate emergency measures. The experimental results show that the proposed method not only improves the accuracy of lightning fault detection in transmission lines, but also provides strong guarantees for the safe operation of transmission lines.

articleTitle: Construction of Transient Calculation Analysis Model Based on Power Grid Graph Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of new energy, the requirements for the stability and reliability of the power system are increasing. Transient fault analysis, as a key in the design and operation of power systems, is of great significance for preventing and handling power grid faults. This paper presented the process of constructing a transient analysis model based on a power grid graph model, and used the constructed transient analysis model achieving simulation of transient analysis on the ten thousand level of power grid graph. the transient calculation analysis model based on power grid graph model is not only improve the efficiency and accuracy of transient fault analysis but also adapt to dynamic changes in power grid topology. In this paper, the main network topology, transient parameters, transient models, and transient faults of the power grid are modeled in a graph database firstly,and how to map the physical structure of the power grid to the graph model in the graph database is elaborated in detail; Then, the specific content of using the established model for transient fault design of selected unit and load equipment was described, including the binding and storage of transient parameters and transient models, the definition of transient faults, transient fault storage, and transient calculation model generation; Finally, a southern provincial power grid was utilized for the case study, the entire process of constructing the transient calculation analysis model results were listed in detail to verify the feasibility and progressiveness of the proposed graph constructing method, providing a foundation for the next step of transient model calculation.

articleTitle: A Digital Twin-based Method for Identifying Weak Points in Integrated Energy Smart Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The setting of weak point identification nodes in integrated energy intelligent systems is usually based on basic layout, with a low identification frequency, resulting in an increase in the false identification rate of the final weak point. Therefore, a weak point identification method for comprehensive energy smart systems based on digital twins is established. Adopting a multistage approach to increase recognition frequency, deploying multistage recognition nodes, setting weak point recognition constraints, constructing a weak point recognition model for the digital twin integrated energy intelligent system, and using a secondary verification calibration method to identify weak points in the integrated energy intelligent system. The test results show that the final weak point misidentification rate obtained is relatively low, indicating that the weak point identification method of the integrated energy intelligent system is more flexible and versatile, with strong stability and security, and the overall identification efficiency is further improved.

articleTitle: Design and research of ship shore system for pure electric ship
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The design and research of pure electric ship shore systems is a multifaceted engineering and technical field, involving power systems, charging infrastructure, ship design, and other aspects. The main focus of this article is the design and research of a ship shore operation and maintenance system. The ship shore operation and maintenance system can be interconnected with the ship navigation system, propulsion remote control system, energy management system, engine room monitoring system, and other systems through communication interfaces. This article focuses on the design and research of the ship shore operation and maintenance system for pure electric ships. The topology and architecture design of the ship shore operation and maintenance system have been completed, and the data processing, storage, and transmission of the ship shore operation and maintenance system have been implemented. A small prototype of the ship shore operation and maintenance system has been built, and the data processing, transportation, and display of the power system and shore based operation and maintenance system of a pure electric ship have been completed. Finally, the design and research of the ship shore system have been achieved.

articleTitle: Thoughts and suggestions on uninterruptible power supply operation and maintenance management of wind turbines
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: As the main backup power supply of the grid-involved control system of a wind turbine, UPS (Uninterrupted Power Supply) plays a crucial role in the process of fault voltage crossing of the wind turbine. By explaining the working principle of the uninterruptible power supply of wind turbines and combining the case of the off-grid event of wind farm units, the paper analyses the impact of uninterruptible power supply failure on the fault voltage crossing of wind turbines and analyses the technical and management problems behind the off-grid event. It puts forward suggestions on attaching importance to the daily operation, maintenance, investigation, and treatment of the uninterruptible power supply of wind turbines. Promote the healthy operation level of wind farms.

articleTitle: An Improved Harmonic Detection Method for Power Quality Based on Hybrid Convolution Interpolation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In order to suppress the spectrum leakage and fence effect caused by fast Fourier change, a new hybrid convolution window is constructed by combining the Hanning window with narrow main lobe and the four fifth-order Nuttall Windows with fast fading sidelobe. In addition, four-line interpolation is used to obtain the correction formulas of amplitude, frequency, phase and other parameters by polynomial fitting to solve the fence problem. This hybrid convolution window four-line spectrum interpolation harmonic detection method can realize the detection and analysis of complex signals in MATLAB environment. The proposed algorithm in this paper is compared with the single-window interpolation algorithm, which verifies the ability of the proposed algorithm to improve the harmonic detection accuracy.

articleTitle: Spectrum Normalization-Based Adversarial Network and CNN for Electricity Theft Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Power theft is the main reason for the non-technical loss of the power grid. The massive user power consumption data provides a basis for the data-driven power theft detection. However, the imbalance of the data seriously affects the effect of power theft detection. Aiming at the data imbalance in power theft detection, an oversampling method and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) power theft detection classification model are proposed. Through the confrontation training of SNGAN generator and discriminator, the generator is prompted to generate false samples similar to real power theft samples, judge the diversity, fidelity and accuracy of SNGAN generated samples by Inception Score and structural similarity index (SSIM), and use the generated samples with good validation effect to enhance the original power theft data. The CNN convolution classification model with the same network structure as SNGAN is trained on the enhanced data set, and conduct power theft detection on the test set. The results show that compared with the traditional sampling algorithm and GAN derived sampling algorithm, SNGAN oversampling method generates samples with more realistic value and has smaller false detection rate. Compared with the traditional classification model, the convolution classification model equipped with SNGAN sampling algorithm has higher detection rate and AUC value, which meet the requirements of power theft detection.

articleTitle: A risk assessment method for distribution stations using multi-source data fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The distribution station is an important component of the distribution network, and its safe and reliable operation is crucial for ensuring power supply. Considering the problems of single evaluation data and high manpower consumption in traditional methods for evaluating the operation status of distribution stations, this paper proposes a risk assessment method for the safe and reliable operation of distribution stations based on multi-source information fusion and fuzzy analytic hierarchy process. Multi source data fusion is performed on environmental, device status, and gas data obtained from different intelligent perception devices. The Analytic Hierarchy Process is used to determine the weights of twelve evaluation factors, and the membership degree is calculated based on the trapezoidal triangle membership function. A fuzzy algorithm is used to establish a comprehensive evaluation model for the status of the distribution station. Based on Python software, the engineering instance data is calculated to obtain the risk assessment results for the safe and reliable operation of the distribution station, and the effectiveness of the proposed method is verified. The proposed method can improve the efficiency of evaluating the operation status of distribution stations, and the research results can provide decision-making basis for operation and maintenance personnel.

articleTitle: Research on Microgrid Operation Prediction Based on Grey BP-NNSP Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the profound transformation of the global energy structure and the rapid development of smart grid technology, microgrids, as an important part of distributed energy systems, have a significant impact on the stability and economy of the power system. Especially in the context of large-scale integration of renewable energy, accurate prediction of microgrids can not only improve the flexibility of the power system but also effectively alleviate the problems brought by the intermittence and uncertainty of new energy generation. This paper proposes an innovative Grey BP-NNSP algorithm to address the issue of decreased prediction accuracy caused by spatial differences between meteorological forecast data and actual geographic locations. By combining active network management theory, it achieves high-precision prediction of microgrid operation and accurate calculation of deep peak regulation requirements. Experimental results show that the algorithm can significantly improve the prediction accuracy of regional load and photovoltaic output, optimize the allocation of grid resources, reduce the electricity cost for users during peak hours, and enhance the capacity of new energy to be carried and the self-healing ability of the distribution network.

articleTitle: Proportional solenoid valve comprehensive test system
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Based on LabVIEW software development platform, according to the relevant national standards and user standards to design a set of proportional solenoid valve test system for the various tests. This paper mainly focuses on the current-pressure curve test introduces the hydraulic system, electrical system and test software development. Through the proportional amplifier output precision, tremor frequency on the experiment to analyze the impact of the comparison of different precision under the changes in the experimental curve, and optimize it to meet the requirements of the test curve.

articleTitle: Research on flood risk prediction of substation based on Temporal Fusion Transformer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The flood disaster caused by extreme weather seriously affects the safety and stability of substations, and flood risk prediction is the key to ensure the reliability of power supply. Flooding in substations is affected by many factors, which involve dynamic and static features, making its accurate prediction challenging. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a substation flood risk prediction model based on Temporal Fusion Transformer (TFT). Different modules are used for feature importance analysis, static covariate feature extraction, and temporal feature mining of risk sequences. The results of experiments and case studies demonstrate that this model is superior to the current mainstream time series prediction models, and can be used for multi-risk scenarios analysis, thereby providing auxiliary decision support for flood prevention efforts.

articleTitle: Based on the improved YOLOv8 photovoltaic module defect detection method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The photovoltaic power station covers a wide area, the detection environment is complex, and the defect recognition of photovoltaic modules is difficult. An improved defect recognition and detection method of photovoltaic modules based on YOLOv8 model is proposed. Based on the backbone network structure, the progressive feature pyramid (AFPN) is used to fuse images at different levels to extract multi-scale information. Instead of each pooling layer and each step convolution layer of the original model, a SPD convolution neural network is established to improve the defect recognition ability of small target features such as hot spots and black edges in photovoltaic panel images. The improved YOLOv8 model improves the fault recognition ability of small target features such as hot spots and black edges in photovoltaic module images. The experimental results show that the recall rate and accuracy of the improved model are better than those of the original model, and the average accuracy reaches $\mathbf{8 4. 2 \%}$.The detection and recognition of small target defects of photovoltaic cells are realized, and the feasibility of the model is verified.

articleTitle: Design Optimization of the IGBT’s Raising N-Buffer Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative analysis focusing on the design of the Raised N-buffer layer of IGBT (RN-IGBT), as opposed to the traditional FS-IGBT, with validation conducted utilizing the Silvaco Technology Computer-Aided Design (TCAD) platform. The RN-IGBT structure features a quasi-neutral N-drift region insert into Negative-type buffer layer and Positive-type collector region. Additionally, the raised N -buffer layer in the drift region results in $\mathbf{4. 7 \%}$ improvement of critical breakdown voltage for the same on-state losses or, up to $22 \%$ turn-off losses reduction, while preserving the same level of on-state voltage decrement, as compared to a standard FS-IGBT configuration. The utilization of RN-IGBT extends to RC-IGBT implementations, enabling the mitigation of snapback phenomena.

articleTitle: A New Cost Estimation Model for Small-scale Grid Infrastructure Projects based on CNN and SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Over the past few years, there has been a progressive upsurge in the quantity of infrastructure with small scale initiatives within the electrical grid. Predicting the cost of such projects can effectively control construction fees and reduce investment risks. This paper integrates convolutional neural networks and support vector machine to construct a CNN-SVMbased prediction model, which not only leverages the strengths of both CNNs and SVMs but also overcomes their respective limitations, thereby achieving superior predictive performance. In order to enhance the model’s ability to optimize parameters and to prevent it from falling into local minimums, northern goshawk optimization algorithm is introduced to train the penalty parameter and kernel function parameter within the model. Through a numerical experiment, the proposed model is demonstrated to perform better than the single model.

articleTitle: Construction of a standardized model for predicting line losses in distribution networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Due to the excessive reliance on the accuracy and completeness of input data in existing distribution network line loss (DNLL) prediction models, the reliability of DNLL prediction results is poor. This article innovatively proposes a BPNN line loss (LL) prediction method based on adaptive genetic algorithm (AGA) optimization. Firstly, based on the PCA algorithm, five main influencing indicators of DNLL were selected, including electricity theft and leakage loss, meter error loss, peak electricity load, power supply, and sales volume. Secondly, the DNLL prediction data are preprocessed from two aspects: standardizing the operating parameters of the distribution network (DN) and normalizing the LL data. Then, based on the BP neural network (BPNN) and AGA, a standardized model for predicting LL in DN is constructed. Finally, by analyzing the standardized prediction results of DNLL, it is verified that the standardized model for DNLL prediction built in this paper can effectively improve the reliability of DNLL prediction results.

articleTitle: Big Data Intelligent Analysis - Study on the Relationship Between Waveform Structural Characteristics The Responses of Paleozoic Oil Layers in the Tahe Oilfield
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the development of seismic exploration technology, the collection and processing of massive seismic data have become an important topic. Big data and artificial intelligence technologies provide new methods and tools for the storage, processing, and analysis of seismic data. This study focuses on the in-depth analysis of the waveform structure characteristics of seismic data from the Paleozoic Ordovician reservoirs in Block 4 of the Tahe Oilfield, Tarim Basin. The results indicate that the Ordovician reservoirs in Block 4 of the Tahe Oilfield exhibit significant responses in waveform structure characteristics of seismic data. Subsequent deployments using the “method for predicting hydrocarbon-bearing formation by waveform structure characteristics of seismic data” in a series of drilling operations have confirmed these findings, significantly improving the drilling success rate and achieving notable economic benefits.

Author Keywords: waveform structural characteristics of seismic data

articleTitle: Progress in Energy Efficiency Limit Values and Energy Efficiency Grades for Power Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper mainly introduces the technical parameters and requirements of power transformers, as well as the progress of energy efficiency limit values and energy efficiency grades. It mainly compares the energy efficiency limit values and energy efficiency grades of 10 kV oil immersed distribution transformer in GB20052-2006, GB20052-2013, and GB20052-2020 standards, and discusses the subsequent energy efficiency limit values and energy efficiency grades of power transformers.

articleTitle: Sequence-to-point learning methods for Non Intrusive Load Disaggregation: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Energy disaggregation, also known as non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM), is a single-channel blind source separation (BSS) problem. It aims to decompose the total energy consumption of a dwelling into individual appliance energy usage. This is achieved by disaggregating the aggregate power signal recorded by the smart meters and into individual appliance readings. Sequence to point methods are a form of Deep neural networks that have shown promise in tackling this problem. These methods use a window of the mains data as input and output a single data point representing the targeted appliance’s energy consumption. This work surveys contemporary sequence-to-point deep learning techniques and outlines our upcoming research in this field.

articleTitle: Research on distributed energy management system based on artificial intelligence
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The reliability and stability of the power system are crucial to social life and economic development as an essential infrastructure of modern society. However, power system failures can lead to serious consequences such as power supply interruptions and equipment damage, making timely and accurate power load forecasting particularly important. Traditional power load forecasting techniques based on rules and statistics have limitations that make it difficult to meet the complex and real-time requirements of the power system. This paper will explore and discuss artificial intelligence-based power load forecasting for the power system, comparing it with traditional methods while focusing on the application of reinforcement learning, big data technology, and abnormal flow identification technology in order to provide new ideas and methods for improving the reliability and stability of the power system.

articleTitle: Optimizing Current Sharing in Interleaved LLC Converters via Variable Magnetizing Inductance
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the increasing power demands of server supplies, multiphase LLC converters have become widely adopted due to their excellent characteristics. However, slight variations in resonant parameters among phases can lead to significant current imbalances, resulting in various operational issues. This paper proposes a method based on variable magnetizing inductance to address these challenges. Through control of an auxiliary winding current, which generates an orthogonal magnetic flux, the magnetizing inductance of the transformer is varied. Therefore, the gain of the LLC converter could be adjusted to be the same with same load. Hence, all the LLC converters’ currents are equally shared. To validate the effectiveness of this approach, the paper analyzes its impact on system performance, specifically examining phase voltage gain as a metric. Simulation results confirm the viability and correctness of the proposed method.

articleTitle: Reactive power compensation technology of hybrid capacitor in terminal low voltage distribution network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In modern power systems, efficient terminal low-voltage distribution networks are vital for stable and quality power supply. Increasing industrial and commercial electricity demand raises the proportion of inductive loads, causing power quality issues like low power factor, high energy loss, and voltage fluctuations. [1] Reactive power compensation technology is key to enhancing power system efficiency and stability. Energy routers, intelligent interfaces, leverage advanced sensing and control strategies to monitor grid status in real-time and dynamically adjust reactive power compensation equipment for optimal power quality. the energy router has been considered the crucial element that builds the net structure between the different electrical components components by connecting and controlling the bidirectional power and data flow. [11] This method boosts response speed, compensation accuracy, and grid adaptability to sudden events. Hybrid reactor reactive power compensation technology combines capacitors and reactors. Reactive power compensation with Capacitor Banks is one of the most successful approaches used in distribution systems, mainly due to their versatility, long-term acceptance in the power industry, and reduced costs. Most allocation methods, [12]Capacitors provide leading reactive power, while reactors absorb lagging reactive power. By precisely calculating and configuring these components, grid reactive power is balanced, improving power factor, reducing energy loss, and stabilizing voltage. Practical applications need to consider load characteristics, grid structure, operating costs, and maintenance. Tunable hybrid reactors may be necessary for loads with significant changes. High intelligence in energy routers is essential to accurately adjust compensation strategies, avoiding over- or under-compensation. Hybrid reactor technology in terminal low-voltage distribution improves power supply quality and operational efficiency, supporting green energy transformation and sustainable development goals. With ongoing technological advancements, this field will unlock more potential and applications in the future.

articleTitle: A two-stage voltage regulation method based on Raft algorithm for photo-storage combination
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Distributed photovoltaic large-scale access to the grid has become a future trend, making the distribution network transformed from a single radial to a multi-source weak-ring mesh structure, which is prone to cause problems such as backward tidal flow and voltage overruns. This paper proposes a two-stage voltage regulation method based on the Raft algorithm for combined light - storage, selecting the active output ratio of $P V$ inverter and the amount of storage charge state change as state variables, and using the Raft algorithm consistency coordination. Realise the burden of voltage regulation is borne by each node of the grid on average to complete the voltage regulation, and simulation verification is carried out through 8-node 220v low-voltage distribution network. The results show that the two-stage voltage regulation effectively suppresses the voltage overrun problem.

articleTitle: Fire Risk Assessment of An Energy Storage Station Based on Bayesian Network and PyroSim
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Lithium-ion battery storage stations have become a crucial component of modern power systems, yet their inherent instability poses severe fire risks during storage. Existing research primarily addresses post-fire control and suppression, leaving a gap in understanding the comprehensive factors influencing fire risk before and after an incident. This study aims to bridge this gap by proposing an integrated risk assessment method combining Bayesian networks and PyroSim. The Bayesian network is employed for both qualitative and quantitative analysis of key factors contributing to fire risk in storage stations, identifying high-risk nodes. PyroSim software is then used to simulate fire scenarios based on these critical risk factors, enabling dynamic analysis of smoke dispersion and heat transfer throughout the fire process. Our findings reveal a substantial $\mathbf{6 9 \%}$ probability of fire originating from thermal runaway in battery modules. Moreover, with an operational fire suppression system, internal fire temperatures can be reduced by up to $400^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$. This integrated approach enhances understanding and management of fire risks in lithium-ion battery storage stations, providing valuable insights for improving safety protocols.

articleTitle: 0.4 Research on common mode voltage cancellation strategy for four-module motor driven by parallel balanced inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In response to the issues of common mode voltage and the resultant common mode currents and leakage currents in PWM motor drive systems, this paper proposes a topology using a parallel balanced inverter to drive a four-module motor. Traditional three-phase inverters, with an odd number of bridge arms, inherently struggle to eliminate common mode voltage. By employing a balanced inverter, the proposed method extends the degrees of freedom, achieving internal group common mode voltage cancellation. Furthermore, replacing the conventional three-phase motor with a four-module motor and altering the stator winding connections, combined with a carrier phaseshifting modulation strategy, allows the system to cancel common mode voltages using a parallel balanced inverter. To verify the efficacy of the proposed solution, a simulation of a parallel balanced inverter driving a four-module motor system was constructed and compared with a traditional three-phase inverter system. The simulation results demonstrate that the new topology effectively suppresses system-conducted interference, thereby improving the system’s electromagnetic interference performance.

articleTitle: Multimodal Pre-trained Model for Enhanced Transformer Health Assessment and Automated Fault Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Accurate transformer health assessment is essential for power system reliability and cost-effective maintenance. Traditional methods relying on single-modality data are limited in accuracy and scope. This paper introduces a multimodal pretrained model that integrates oil chromatographic data, oil temperature data, and core ground current data to generate coherent fault analysis text. Using ResNet-based encoders and a Projector, the model aligns features from different modalities into a unified textual feature space, processed by the LLAMA3-8b large language model. The training process includes feature alignment pre-training and end-to-end fine-tuning to minimize generation loss. Experimental results show that our model outperforms traditional single-modality and previous multimodal approaches in accuracy and relevance of fault diagnosis. This system improves fault detection precision, offers comprehensive transformer health insights, and enables automated diagnostic processes, underscoring the value of multimodal data integration and advanced text generation techniques.

articleTitle: Research on comprehensive assessment of regional renewable energy consumption in the electricity market environment
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Building a new power system with renewable energy as the main body is a key measure and inevitable requirement to help achieve the goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality. The electricity market is an essential source of support for the construction of new power systems. Research on the role of renewable energy in the assessment of the electricity market environment consumption is of great significance. First, a threestage mathematical model of the regional electricity market evolution process is constructed, and the market equilibrium at each stage is solved. Then, based on the Q-learning reinforcement learning algorithm, a multi-agent market clearing model regarding the subject’s quotation strategy under imperfect competition was established, and an evaluation system including multi-dimensional indicators such as renewable energy consumption space and adequacy was built. Finally, standard node examples are used to systematically analyze carbon emission models, market equilibrium results, renewable energy consumption, multi-agent simulation, and other scenarios under different regional electricity market evolution stages, providing feasible policy suggestions for the problems.

articleTitle: Analysis of Load Voltage Drop Faults During Solid Static Switch Transfer Operation and Corresponding Improvement of Auxiliary Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper addresses the issue of voltage drops across the load during switching of the solid state transfer switch (SSTS) with an auxiliary switching loop. This problem can lead to insufficient power supply to the loads, resulting in economic losses and industrial safety issues. Therefore, a multiplexed structure is put forward based on the existing auxiliary commutation branches, which can compensate for the voltage drop. The composite circuit reduces the voltage drop of the load during the switching process by increasing the equivalent capacitance, while the multiplex circuit simplifies the composite passive device structure. Simulation and comparisons verify the feasibility and innovation of the proposed structure.

articleTitle: Detection technology for inertial behavior of three degree of freedom wire galloping
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Due to the influence of various factors such as weather on wire galloping, when designing a three degree of freedom wire galloping inertial behavior detection technology, there is often a problem of low detection accuracy caused by inaccurate analysis of wire running trajectory. In this regard, a MEMS sensor detection technology for the inertial behavior of three degree of freedom wire galloping is proposed. Under the influence of MEMS (Micro-Electro-Mechanical System) sensor technology, wire related data is collected, and the three degree of freedom model of the wire is analyzed. The parameter matrix of the wire during motion is calculated, and the wire motion trajectory equation is constructed. Based on this, multiple characteristic parameters of wire galloping inertia behavior are calculated, such as the inherent vibration angular frequency of the wire, the equivalent moment of inertia of the wire, etc. The wire galloping detection value is calculated to achieve the detection of wire galloping. Through the above design, the design of the inertial behavior detection technology for three degree of freedom wire galloping is completed. The experimental results show that the MEMS sensor detection technology for the inertial behavior of the designed three degree of freedom wire galloping has high detection accuracy in practical applications.

articleTitle: Research on Photovoltaic Grid-Connected Converter with Nine-Level Injection Voltage Source
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In a high-power photovoltaic (PV) grid-connected system, a nine-level injected voltage source converter facilitates efficient power conversion and grid-connected application through the utilization of a 12-pulse wave conversion circuit and voltage injection technology. A modular PV direct current (DC)boosting and pooling system is constructed by combining the maximum power tracking control strategy with the nine-level injected converter PV grid-connected system. The integrated control strategy of the latter is explored with the objective of achieving a reasonable realization of the voltage injection features and a smooth grid-connection of the PV power generation system power. Ultimately, PSCAD is employed to construct the simulation model. The results demonstrate that the developed integrated control strategy for a nine-level injected voltage source converter can guarantee the safe and reliable operation of the injected converter PV grid-connected system.

articleTitle: Coordinated planning of centralized shared energy storage and distributed generation systems for jointly operated industrial parks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper investigates the optimal design of a centralized shared energy storage system and distributed generation systems for jointly operated industrial parks. A mathematical model is developed to determine the optimal capacity and power ratings for the shared energy storage system, as well as for wind and solar generation systems. The model considers both investment costs and the cost of purchasing electricity from the main grid in the objective function and includes key constraints, such as ensuring that each park’s distributed power generation can meet its own energy needs. Simulations comparing independent and joint operation modes demonstrate that shared resource management can significantly enhance efficiency and reduce overall costs. These results provide valuable insights for the design and operation of energy systems in industrial parks.

articleTitle: Research on Integrated Energy System Planning Based on the Whale Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In this paper, a comprehensive energy system planning optimization method based on heuristic algorithm is proposed, which aims to improve the economic efficiency of the system. Firstly, the background and development status of the integrated energy system are analyzed, and the challenges and optimization opportunities of equipment configuration and modeling are discussed. Subsequently, an optimization method based on economic performance was introduced, and the whale optimization algorithm was used for system optimization. Through case analysis, the results show that the proposed method can significantly reduce the operating cost of the system. Under the initial population size of 120 iterations, the whale optimization algorithm converged around the 44th generation, and the final solution obtained was ${\$}$6,218,367.29. The results obtained by the genetic algorithm are $1.90 \%$ higher than those obtained using the whale optimization algorithm. Therefore, the algorithm used in this paper shows strong global search ability and improves the optimization accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on overload fault early warning method for large-capacity pumped storage units
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This study presents a novel overload fault early warning method for large-capacity pumped storage units. By continuously monitoring and analyzing critical operational parameters such as voltage, current, and temperature, and applying sophisticated data analysis and fault diagnosis techniques, the proposed method enables real-time detection and prediction of equipment anomalies. The Composite Detection Index (CDI) is introduced to assess the health status of the units. The Long ShortTerm Memory (LSTM) network is utilized for managing time-series data, enhancing fault prediction accuracy. Experimental results demonstrate the method’s effectiveness in early warning of overload faults, ensuring operational safety and reliability of pumped storage units. The proposed approach provides both theoretical foundations and practical recommendations for the secure operation of high-capacity pumped storage systems, contributing significantly to grid stability and energy efficiency. This research underscores the importance of advanced monitoring and predictive maintenance in modern power systems.

articleTitle: Research on power grid user behavior analysis method based on deep learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The operation of power grid enterprises is constantly developing towards intelligence, and the number of smart meter users is also increasing. Behavioral analysis of power grid users can detect malicious electricity theft in a timely manner and provide data support for the overall operation of the power grid. Deep learning technology has the ability to interpret data by learning specific data sets, and it has unique technical advantages in the fields of graphics, text, audio and search. In view of the common problems of low analysis efficiency and inaccurate detection results in traditional power grid user behavior analysis methods, this paper conducts research on power grid user behavior analysis based on deep learning. A power grid user behavior analysis model combining external factors and deep learning neural networks is proposed. It has been verified that the model can effectively improve the accuracy of power grid user behavior analysis.

articleTitle: Co-optimization of Active and Reactive Power in Flexible Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: To improve the operational efficiency and stability of distribution networks, a two-stage coordinated optimization model for flexible distribution networks with intelligent soft switches is proposed to address issues such as increased voltage fluctuations and active power losses due to high proportions of distributed energy sources integrated into the grid. The model aims to minimize system network losses and voltage deviations, determining the operation states of discrete devices on a daily basis and rolling optimization of the output of continuous devices within the day to mitigate the impact of prediction errors and further enhance the economic operation of the distribution network. The proposed model is validated using the improved IEEE 33-bus system, demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed strategy.

articleTitle: False data injection attack detection of power grid based on IWOA-BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: False Data Injection Attacks (FDIA) disrupt or mislead the decision-making of the command center by injecting covert false data into the monitoring instrument to bypass the bad data detection mechanism. In this paper, a false data injection attack testing method based on IWOA-BiLSTM is proposed. The proposed method uses a BiLSTM network to transmit the timing information from the reverse LSTM back to the forward LSTM to alleviate the gradient vanishing problem, improve its convergence speed and performance, and introduce an improved whale algorithm to further optimize the neural network structure, so as to enhance the accuracy of the model. A mass of comparative simulation experiments are carried out in the IEEE14 node and IEEE118 node test systems, and the simulation outcomes indicate that in comparison with the RNN, LSTM, BiLSTM, and WOABiLSTM models, the proposed model has better measurement accuracy, recall, $\mathbf{F 1}$ score, and real-time detection performance.

articleTitle: Diffusion Behavior of Formic Acid in a Transformer Insulation System with Modified Natural Ester Oil
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: During the prolonged stable operation of transformers, insulating oil paper will be affected by acid. Studying the diffusion of acids is crucial as they can speed up the aging of the insulating materials. Natural ester oil, emerging as an alternative to traditional mineral oil, can improve its performance advantages by adding nanoparticles significantly. This study utilized molecular dynamics simulations to explore the diffusion behavior of formic acid in a transformer insulation system with modified natural ester oil. The results showed that the mean square displacement of formic acid was 66.41 Å<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> in the nano-modified oil-paper layer model, which was 47.19 Å<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> less than that in pure oil-paper layer model. Furthermore, the concentration of formic acid distributed at oil paper interface is relatively low, and its interaction energy with insulating oil is greater. This effectively inhibited the movement of formic acid, mitigating the degradation of transformer paper caused by formic acid. The nanoparticles’ adsorption of formic acid enhanced the insulation performance and anti-aging properties of transformers, thereby prolonging the use of insulating oil and improving the overall anti-aging performance of the transformer.

articleTitle: Effect of ETL and HTL Layers on The Performance of Perovskite Solar Cells Using SCAPS-1D Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The photovoltaic conversion efficiency of perovskite solar cells has been significantly improved by the global scientific community in a short period of time. From $3.8 \%$ to $25.7 \%$, this efficiency has increased dramatically. The goal of the current study is to model perovskite solar cells and enhance the performance of hole and electron transport layers. In this study, the SCAPS-1D simulation software is employed to assess the efficiency of solar cells. This study elaborated on different Electron transport layers and hole transport layers with SCAPs-1D. TiO2 functions effectively as an electron transport layer, while $\mathbf{C u 2 O}$ serves as an ideal hole transport layer. The device demonstrated an impressive photovoltaic conversion efficiency of $28.31 \%$, an open-circuit voltage (Voc) of 1.09 V, a current density of 30.14 $\mathrm{mA} / \mathrm{cm} 2$, and a fill factor of $\mathbf{8 5. 9 3 \%}$. Thus, lead-free perovskite solar cells are environmentally friendly and promising for future solar cells. The objective of this study is to determine the ideal thickness of the absorbent layer.

articleTitle: Research on Modeling Method for Long-Term Optimal Dispatching of High-Ratio New Energy Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the rapid development of new energy sources and large-scale grid connection, the computational cost becomes high when dealing with long-term optimal scheduling data. In this paper, we propose a temporal cycle-based optimal scheduling modeling method, which decomposes $\mathbf{7 2 0}$ hours of data into 30 days, 24 hours a day, and a cyclic new energy unit optimal scheduling model with one hour as the scenario, which significantly reduces the computational complexity of the model. The model fully takes into account the uncertainty of wind energy and photovoltaic units in the long-term optimal scheduling process with, the objective function is to achieve the minimization of the total cost of the unit. Finally, it is analyzed by the IEEE 24-bus system, a classical power system arithmetic example, and the results show that the computational efficiency of the system is significantly improved, the rate of wind and photovoltaic abandonment is reduced, and the overall operating cost is more competitive after considering the time-cycling optimization.

articleTitle: Electricity allocation algorithm for shared base stations based on the energy consumption model of the power environment system
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The efficient allocation of electricity has posed a formidable challenge for communication operators. This paper proposes an Electricity Allocation Algorithm (EAA) for shared base stations based on the power environment system’s energy consumption model. The EAA approach thoroughly analyzes factors influencing energy consumption and establishes a regression model for shared base stations using multiple linear regression. Parameters of the model are optimized through Quantum Behavior Particle Swarm Optimization (QPSO). Ultimately, a precise electricity allocation is achieved by calculating real-time energy consumption data from servers and other machines in different carrier base stations. Experimental results demonstrate the accuracy of this paper’s electricity allocation model for shared base stations. This study provides theoretical support for future applications of accurate electricity allocation in shared base stations.

articleTitle: Research on Gansu Power Transmission Capacity under Multi-energy Complementary
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the construction of a large number of new energy sources such as wind power and photovoltaic in Gansu, the rate of abandoning wind and light is increasing, and the problem of new energy consumption is becoming increasingly prominent. Considering the characteristics of various power stations in the multi-energy complementary power system, it is very important to formulate the working position and working capacity of each power station on the load curve and reduce the amount of new energy curtailment as much as possible. Different from the traditional production simulation method, the power production simulation program used in this paper can better adapt to the access of new energy sources such as large-scale wind power and photovoltaic. In this paper, different consumption guarantee measures are formulated for different new energy volumes. By analyzing the evaluation indicators such as power generation reliability, abandoned power, operation economy and tie-line transaction, the scale of Gansu power transmission that can guide the operation mode is proposed.

Author Keywords: proportion of the wind and solar energy abandon

articleTitle: A microgrid energy storage technology based on reinforcement learning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the increasing penetration of renewable energy sources in power systems, their inherent intermittency and stochastic nature, combined with dynamic load demands and fluctuating real-time electricity prices, pose significant challenges to the stability and efficiency of traditional grids. Addressing the economic dispatch problem within Microgrids (MG), we integrated Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) with Quadratic Programming. This innovative approach aims to optimize decision-making processes through autonomous learning by intelligent agents while leveraging the strengths of quadratic programming to ensure the efficiency and feasibility of the solutions. Through in-depth simulation analysis using real-world datasets, the effectiveness and superiority of the proposed method have been validated. Additionally, comparative assessments with existing DRL models highlight its unique capabilities in tackling the complexities inherent in advanced energy management systems. The average reduction of system load fluctuation reaches $\mathbf{2 2 \%}$. The experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method is effective in both predictable and unpredictable settings.

articleTitle: Prediction of Radiated Electromagnetic Interference Based on Four-module Motor Drive System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In recent years, wide bandgap semiconductor devices such as silicon carbide (SiC) and gallium nitride (GaN) have been increasingly applied in electric drive systems, effectively enhancing system power density. However, the high-frequency and high-speed characteristics of SiC devices exacerbate electromagnetic interference (EMI) issues within the system. Additionally, the cables in electric drive systems exhibit significant antenna effects, radiating conducted EMI into the surrounding space, thereby affecting the normal operation of other sensitive equipment. Therefore, it is essential to research motor drive system topologies that can actively suppress EMI and predict radiated interference in motor drive systems. The topology of a four-module motor paired with parallel inverters can achieve active suppression of EMI at the source. This paper conducts a simulation-based prediction of radiated interference for a parallel inverter-driven four-module motor system. It analyzes the coupling mechanisms of common mode and differential mode radiated interference and validates the radiated interference from both DC and AC cables through simulations, predicting the impact on surrounding sensitive equipment in practical systems.

articleTitle: Research on the prediction of thermal runaway risk of new energy vehicle lithium battery based on improved LSTM-HMM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the widespread adoption of new energy vehicles, the safety of lithium batteries, especially the issue of thermal runaway, is regarded as a critical challenge. To address this issue, an improved LSTM-HMM model is proposed in this study, aiming to enhance the accuracy and real-time performance of thermal runaway prediction. The model captures the time-series dynamics of key parameters such as battery temperature, voltage, and current, improving the shortcomings of the standard LSTM-HMM model. Experimental results show that the improved model outperforms traditional methods in terms of prediction accuracy and response speed, effectively enhancing the safety and reliability of the battery management system.

articleTitle: Research on optimal scheduling of wind-hydrogen integrated energy system considering wind power uncertainty
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The combination of energy storage technology and wind power to realize the time-space translation of electric energy is an effective means to solve the problem of operation stability of new power systems. Hydrogen energy storage has the advantages of large storage capacity, clean and pollution-free, and flexible operation, and has great development potential. However, due to the uncertainty of wind power, hydrogen energy storage systems face uncertain load demands when they frequently switch working modes. In order to ensure the safe and stable operation of the system, to achieve the maximum degree of wind power consumption, improve the system economy. In this paper, the basic structure and mathematical model of the wind-hydrogen integrated energy system are established. Secondly, a wind power scenario reduction method based on K-means clustering algorithm is proposed, and a robust interval optimization scheduling model for the wind-hydrogen integrated energy system considering wind power uncertainties is constructed with the aim of minimizing the expected annual cost. Finally, the MATLAB/Simulink simulation platform is used to simulate the integrated energy system in a certain area, and the rationality and effectiveness of the model are verified.

articleTitle: Research on sliding mode control method for bidirectional DC/DC converter in special vehicle DC grid based on extended state observer
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This article proposes an innovative control strategy–an improved sliding mode control method based on extended state observer (SMC+ESO)–for bidirectional DC/DC converters in special vehicle power systems facing system uncertainties such as constant power load disturbances and input voltage changes. The core of this method is first to design an extended state observer to accurately estimate the system state, constant power load disturbances, and changes in input voltage. Subsequently, based on these estimated values, sliding mode control technology is applied to design a sliding mode controller to ensure that the system can quickly and accurately track voltage.

Author Keywords: Bidirectional DC/DC converter Sliding mode control

articleTitle: Research on the optimal peak-to-valley electricity price considering the social cost of carbon emissions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the proposal of the national “ 3060 “ double carbon goal, the peak-valley tariff setting should consider the important effect of the peak-valley price policy on emission reduction. Setting the peak-valley price reasonably can not only reduce the physical cost of the power grid, but also reduce the carbon emissions of power system. In this paper, the social cost of carbon emissions was considered for the first time in the process of peak-valley tariff setting, and the maximum optimized objective function of total social surplus including the optimal peak- valley ratio was constructed. The constraint conditions of the extreme value of objective function was determined by Lagrange multiplier method, the relationship between the optimal peak-valley tariff and electricity price, carbon price and marginal carbon emission factor was obtained.
