Taking the actual operation data of Guangdong power system from January to March, 2022 as an example, the marginal carbon emission factors in each period of peak and valley were estimated, and the optimal peak-valley price ratio1.78: 1: 0.3 considering the social cost of carbon emission was obtained. The study found that the current peak to valley price difference needs to be further increased after considering the society cost of carbon emission, and the optimal peak price ratio can be raised by 0.084, while the optimal valley price ratio can be decreased by 0.08.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Based Joint Operation of Multiple Devices Strategy Optimization Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper proposes a machine learning-based optimization method for the joint operation strategy of multiple equipment, aiming to improve the economic efficiency of the system that jointly supplies multiple types of equipment. Firstly, the background and development status of multiple pieces of equipment joint operation technology are analyzed, and the challenges and optimization space in equipment configuration, equipment modeling and operation strategy are pointed out. Secondly, a start-up threshold joint supply optimization model under the electricity-heat-determined operation strategy is designed, and a new optimization method for equipment operation efficiency is proposed. Then the integration of a reinforcement learning framework into the optimization system. Finally, through the analysis of arithmetic examples, the results demonstrate that the method can significantly improve the average operating efficiency of the equipment and minimize the operating costs of the system.

Author Keywords: combined cooling, heating and power system

articleTitle: Intelligent decision Support Systems (IDSS)& Lowcarbon technology for water pollution control
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This study explores the innovative application of lowcarbon technologies in water pollution control, with a focus on enhancing energy efficiency and reducing carbon emissions. By integrating Intelligent Decision Support Systems (IDSS), real-time monitoring, predictive modeling, and optimization algorithms, this research demonstrates how water treatment processes can be optimized to reduce both energy consumption and environmental impact. The paper highlights key low-carbon technologies such as biofilm processes, membrane separation, and wet electrostatic fields, analyzing their effectiveness in improving water quality and minimizing energy use. IDSS provides a smart management approach by integrating multi-source data to dynamically adjust system parameters, achieving efficient low-carbon water pollution control. The study emphasizes the importance of technological research, policy support, and cross-sector collaboration in promoting the widespread adoption of low-carbon technologies for sustainable environmental management.

articleTitle: Intelligent Q&A System for Power Dispatching Based on Retrieval Augmented Generation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The knowledge of power dispatching is huge in scale and scattered in storage, making it time-consuming and laborious for operators to fully learn and utilize the knowledge documents. This paper proposes a intelligent Question and Answer (Q&A) system for power dispatching based on Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) technology. By optimizing the basic RAG for the characteristics of electric power documents and improving the text loading, chunking and retrieval methods, a set of intelligent Q&A system for electric power dispatching with accurate answers and reliable contents is constructed. And through experiments, it is verified that this system has a significant improvement in the electric power domain Q&A tasks compared with the basic RAG Q&A system.

articleTitle: Energy management method for virtual power plant based on double-layer deep reinforcement learning game
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In order to realize the stable and efficient operation of a Virtual Power Plant (VPP) in a complex power market environment, a VPP energy management method based on a double-layer deep reinforcement learning game is proposed. Firstly, the multi-agent transaction model in VPP is described, and the master-slave game model of combined heat and power operator (CHPO) and electric heating user aggregator (EHUA) in VPP is constructed by designing master-slave object and constraint. Secondly, a two-layer Markov decision process is constructed. Then, aiming at the problem of poor robustness of the traditional optimization method, a master-slave deep decision model based on a soft actor-critic (SAC) algorithm and double-depth Q network (DDQN) algorithm is proposed, and an offline training process of master-slave alternating training is constructed. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed methodology in this paper achieves optimization of the electricity-heat pricing strategy, estimation of user’s electricity-heat response Q-values, and robust and efficient decision-making in complex environments. This approach successfully accomplishes the synergistic optimization of multi-agent objectives within VPP.

articleTitle: Dynamic partitioning and evaluation of autonomous regions based on stochastic model predictive control under chance constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In order to obtain a reliable autonomous region partitioning scheme while taking into account the uncertainty of distributed energy output, this paper proposes a stochastic model predictive control-based dynamic partitioning and evaluation method for autonomous regions under chance constraints. First, the autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) model is applied to forecast wind and PV power. Finally, the SMPC model was used to solve and evaluate the dynamic partitioning correction. Secondly, with the goal of minimizing the risk of load loss in autonomous regions, a chance constraint system for partitioning autonomous regions is established, and stochastic simulation techniques are used to solve the chance constraints. Finally, the optimization model for distribution network partitioning based on stochastic model predictive control (SMPC) is constructed, and the improved active modularity function is used to evaluate and correct the partitioning scheme. Validation is carried out through the modified IEEE33 node arithmetic simulation. The results show that the partitioning method can ensure the effective and reasonable partitioning results at a certain confidence level, and effectively ensure the power supply stability in autonomous regions.

articleTitle: Research on carbon accounting and verification technology for power generation industry based on blockchain
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The carbon emissions of China’s power generation industry account for more than $\mathbf{4 0 \%}$ of the total, making it the first industry to be included in the national carbon market, and requiring carbon accounting and verification. However, the carbon accounting data has multiple links, diverse sources, and insufficient collection, which faces some problems such as poor reliability and transparency, weak trust transfer among subjects, and lack of data verification technology. Blockchain has the characteristics of decentralization, immutability, and transparency, which can provide technical support for credible carbon accounting and verification in the power generation industry. The paper first analyzes the current situation of carbon accounting and verification in the power generation industry and clarifies the technical integration point with blockchain. Then, it proposes a blockchain-based technology route and scheme. Finally, it designs a blockchain-based carbon accounting and verification system architecture and functional modules, proposes key technologies, and conducts experimental verification.

articleTitle: Fault Inference and Analysis of Hydrogen-Electric Coupled Systems Based on Bayesian Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In this paper, we build a fault diagnosis model based on Bayesian network for the key equipment faults in the hydrogen electric coupling system. By analyzing the accident data of key hydrogen-related equipment, the common faults of the equipment are summarized and the different effects on the overall system performance are discussed. The model was solved using Netica software, which verified the rationality and accuracy of the proposed Bayesian network model. The results show that the model performs well in handling uncertainty and causal inference in complex systems, and can dynamically update the Bayesian network model to accurately locate the root cause of failure, and can be effectively used for fault diagnosis and risk assessment of hydrogen electric coupling system.

articleTitle: Research on error detection method of smart meters based on classification algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The traditional error detection of electric energy meters uses the pulse method for inspection, which has a long cycle and low inspection efficiency when detecting low current errors. In order to improve the efficiency of intelligent electricity meter error detection, the article proposes a power testing method that integrates machine learning classification algorithms. This method preprocesses the detection data, using machine learning classification algorithm theory to learn the SVM (Support Vector Machine) model, using the training data to get the learned SVM model to process the data to be tested, improving the detection accuracy. In practical applications, this detection method has good stability and high detection efficiency. Partial project testing efficiency has increased by nearly 5 times and overall efficiency has increased by nearly 4 times. This method can be widely applied to electric energy meter manufacturers and measurement and testing institutions, better promote the development of electricity meter inspection technology, and achieve improved testing efficiency.

articleTitle: Capacitor Voltage Transformer Error Prediction Method Based on Fusion Convolution Module
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: A Capacitor Voltage Transformer (CVT) error prediction method based on fusion convolution module is proposed in this paper. Firstly, the CVT error sequence and its influencing factor sequence are decomposed by Seasonal-Trend Decomposition Using LOESS (STL) to construct a threedimensional input matrix. Then, the matrix is input into continuous feature extraction module. Each feature extraction module contains a fusion convolution module and a residual network. Inside the fusion convolution module, the data is subjected to three-dimensional convolution and deep separable convolution respectively, and the data is extracted and fused from the whole and the local respectively. Finally, the extracted features are reduced in dimension and input into the Long Short-Term Memory neural network (LSTM) for prediction output. The experimental results show that the prediction accuracy of the proposed method is better than the classical prediction model in deep learning.

articleTitle: Simulation Analysis of Heating Characteristics of Energy Storage Cabinets of LiIthium Battery Based on Thermoelectric Coupling Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Lithium-ion batteries dominate electrochemical energy storage, but their thermal effects can significantly impact their safety. To achieve rapid and precise characterization of the operational state of lithium-ion battery storage compartments and reduce the probability of accidents, this paper conducts simulation analysis based on a thermoelectric coupling model. The battery compartment was precisely meshed, and the temperature change process un-der different charging modes was simulated according to actual conditions. It was found that the presence of an alternating current component leads to in-creased heat generation and unstable current distribution within the energy storage cabinet, further exacerbating the uneven temperature distribution. These results are significant for ensuring the safe operation of lithium-ion battery storage compartments.

articleTitle: Fire Risk Assessment of Electric Vehicles in Underground Garages Based on Fuzzy Bayesian Network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In response to the phenomena of fire spread, explosion risk, and toxic gas release from electric vehicles in underground garages, We introduce a method for assessing the fire risk of electric vehicles, utilizing fuzzy approach to bayesian network. In this work, a fire cause-based model is developed based on expert experience and logistic regression analysis of historical samples. Twenty-three high-risk nodes were quantitatively analyzed using Netica to identify the high-risk factors. The experimental results indicate that fire hazard investigation and remediation (with a probability of 81.4%) is a primary factor contributing to the fire. This finding is highly significant for fire prevention, control, and safety management in underground spaces.

articleTitle: A Depth Analysis Algorithm for Characterizing the Regional Evolution of Soil Erosion for Power Transmission Projects in Alpine Regions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Conventional soil erosion analysis algorithms are mainly based on hydrological simulation, which is affected by climate, geomorphology and other evolutionary factors, and the analysis results are not comprehensive, affecting the construction quality of power transmission and transformation projects. Therefore, the depth analysis algorithm of regional evolution characteristics of soil erosion for transmission and substation projects in alpine areas is designed. It analyzes the landscape pattern of soil erosion in transmission and substation projects in alpine area, obtains the information of spatial distribution, area and intensity of soil erosion in the project area, and analyzes the landscape pattern parameters such as fragmentation degree, fractal dimension and patch shape index of soil erosion landscape. We analyze the dominant factors in depth in relation to the evolution characteristics of soil erosion areas, taking climate factors, geological and geomorphological factors, vegetation cover factors, and human activity factors into consideration, so as to reveal the intrinsic mechanism of the regional evolution of soil erosion. Comparative experiments were conducted to verify that the algorithm has higher analyzing accuracy and can be applied in real life.

articleTitle: Construction and Application of Integrated New DTS System Based on Training Cloud Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This project is dedicated to developing an advanced power system simulation and training environment tailored specifically for dispatchers. The intelligent panoramic simulation system, operating on a training cloud platform, can effectively model various grid dispatch scenarios and facilitate comprehensive and collaborative simulation training from any location. t addresses challenges in simulation technology while enhancing dispatchers’ understanding, cognition, and forecasting of new power system characteristics, effectively mitigating the current gap in the online grid dispatch training market. The system is currently used at the State Grid of China Technology College and will be promoted across the State Grid Corporation and its subsidiaries.

articleTitle: Contrastive Learning for Anomaly Detection in Power Distribution Monitoring Images Using Text- Induced Image Augmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Ensuring the reliable operation of power distribution systems is critical, and anomaly detection within these systems plays a vital role in maintaining their stability. However, this task is challenging due to the limited availability of labeled anomaly samples and the significant variability in normal conditions caused by environmental factors such as lighting, weather, and environmental interferences. In this paper, we propose an innovative approach that leverages contrastive learning, augmented with text-induced image generation, to enhance anomaly detection capabilities. Our method integrates traditional image augmentation techniques, like noise addition and rotation, with advanced text-guided editing. Specifically, “assimilation text” is used to generate varied normal images that simulate different benign conditions, while “dissimilation text” creates synthetic anomalies, reflecting potential faults like transformer leakage or arc discharge. This dual augmentation strategy not only balances the dataset by increasing the diversity of both normal and abnormal samples but also improves the model’s robustness in distinguishing between normal and anomalous conditions in complex monitoring environments. The experimental results demonstrate that our approach significantly enhances anomaly detection performance, offering a reliable solution for real-time monitoring and fault detection in power distribution networks.

articleTitle: The Uncertainty Evaluation in Measuring Dissolved Gases in Transformer Oil by Gas Chromatography Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Focusing on the application of uncertainty evaluation methods in the experiment of measuring dissolved gases in transformer oil, this paper discover the impaction of different experiment conditions, including measurement repeatability, standard gases, atmospheric pressure, peak areas of standard samples or samples. Then we apply this method to calculate and analyze the uncertainty of dissolved gas components in transformer oil from one specific experiment.

articleTitle: Wind shear detection based on wind lidar
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the increasing demand for wind shear early warning in areas such as civil aviation low-altitude safety and meteorological observation, the development of a laser wind lidar for wind shear information has been realized based on the principle of laser Doppler frequency shift. This paper uses the radial wind speed data obtained from the laser wind lidar in low-altitude areas as the basic data source. Based on data preprocessing, a wind shear detection model is constructed to achieve accurate extraction of wind shear information. The laser wind lidar integrated with this wind shear detection method was tested in a typical plateau airport, and the test results showed that the wind shear detection method based on laser wind lidar achieved good results. With the crew aircraft reports as the benchmark, the wind shear hit rate was over 90%, enhancing the reliability of low-altitude wind shear early warning based on laser wind lidar.

articleTitle: A Battery Thermal Management Strategy Based on Model Predictive Control with Online Markov Speed Predictor
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The energy efficiency of battery electric vehicles has reached a high level, but there remains significant potential for optimizing the efficiency of battery thermal management systems (BTMS). Existing control strategies for BTMS often fail to adequately consider preview information of the trip, leading to suboptimal energy efficiency. In this paper, an online Markov Chain (MC)-based model predictive control (MPC) strategy is used to reduce the energy consumption of the battery thermal management system. The MC-based speed predictor gathers speed data during driving to continuously update the transition probability matrix(TPM), thereby enhancing prediction accuracy. Firstly, the predicted vehicle speed sequence is used as a disturbance of the model predictive control. Then the battery degradation cost, electric power consumption cost, and deviation of battery temperature from target are selected as the objective functions, and finally the dynamic programming (DP) algorithm is employed to solve the local optimization problem within the prediction time domain. For simulation verification, the CLTC-P cycle was repeated 17 times as a test condition. Compared with the rule-based controller, the MPC algorithm reduced power consumption by 5.4% and battery degradation by 3% under test conditions. In addition, the BTMS with MPC tracks the battery reference temperature better.

articleTitle: Experimental study of smart buildings providing fast frequency response
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: As the penetration of renewable energy increases, the mechanical inertia of the power system decreases, weakening the system’s ability to withstand disturbances, particularly during large frequency events. Smart buildings on the demand side show promise as candidates for providing frequency regulation. This paper presents a fast frequency response test for smart buildings. A series of tests, including frequency step tests, frequency ramp tests, and hybrid tests, were conducted to assess the fast frequency response performance of smart buildings. The results indicate that the building has regulation capabilities comparable to traditional generator units in primary frequency control and demonstrates strong potential for fast frequency response. These findings are now being used to guide the development of standards for demand-side adjustable resources participating in fast frequency response.

articleTitle: Continuous Trust Assessment of Power Terminals Based on Conditional Variational Autoencoders
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The increasing scale of power IoT terminal access, in order to ensure that Web-based services are not damaged, automatic anomaly detection methods are needed to monitor hundreds of thousands or even millions of KPIs, detect anomalies and trigger troubleshooting in a timely manner, and at the same time, the zero-trust architecture concept is applied to the power IoT terminal security protection deployment on the basis of inheriting the existing security protection measures. However, when facing a large number of KPIs in practice, traditional statistical methods and supervised integration methods cannot meet this requirement. Donut, a leading supervised method, yields positive results but lacks sequential modeling capabilities and cannot effectively handle time-related anomalies. This paper introduces the Bagel algorithm, an unsupervised approach designed to address temporal information-related anomalies. Bagel utilizes the CVAE to incorporate temporal information and employs dropout layers to prevent overfitting. Experiments conducted with real data from internet companies demonstrate that Bagel enhances the top F1-score for anomaly detection by 0.08 to 0.43 when compared to Donut, highlighting its practical utility in anomaly detection.

articleTitle: Two-Stage Intelligent Identification of Dominant Instability Modes in Large Power Systems Based on Minimum Random Convolution Kernel Transformation and Extreme Gradient Boosting
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In large power systems, large disturbance rotor angle instability and large disturbance voltage instability often occur in an intertwined and coupled manner. Accurately identifying the dominant one, i.e., the dominant instability mode (DIM), during simulation analysis is crucial for developing effective control measures. This paper proposes a two-stage intelligent identification framework for dominant instability modes in large power systems, based on the indirect mapping concept of “high-dimensional electrical features” $\rightarrow$ “lowdimensional key features” $\rightarrow$ “dominant instability model.” In the first stage, the framework uses the minimally random convolutional kernel transform (MiniRocket) to extract key features from simulation data, converting high-dimensional timeseries simulation data of large power systems into low-dimensional vector features, thereby addressing the dimensionality disaster problem of large power systems. In the second stage, the framework employs the ensemble method of extreme gradient boosting (XGBoost) to classify based on low-dimensional vector features, accurately identifying the stability and dominant instability mode of large power systems. A case study of an actual regional power grid in China (2131 nodes) demonstrates that the proposed two-stage intelligent identification method outperforms existing machine learning and deep learning methods in terms of accuracy. Additionally, the proposed method has a faster training speed and better adaptability to large power systems.

articleTitle: Battery Life Early Prediction with Feature Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Battery life early prediction is significant to battery development and management. However, how to effectively select reasonable and efficient battery features for early prediction is still a big challenge. This paper proposes a novel method of early battery life prediction with feature optimization. Firstly, some ineffective and redundant battery features are filtered based on the mutual information between battery features and battery life, and correlation coefficient between battery features. Then, considering the complex nonlinearity of the battery capacity decline and the small amount of experimental data, kernel principal component analysis is adapted to reorganize the retained features to make the data more linear and differentiable. Finally, based on the reconstructed data, the early prediction model of battery life is obtained by using Gaussian process regression. The experiments on Severson’s dataset show the effectiveness of the proposed feature optimization method.

articleTitle: Research on Frequency Response Characteristics and Optimization Methods of Signal Cable Length to High Voltage Divider
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In modern high-voltage power systems, high-voltage dividers are used to convert high voltage signals into measurable low voltage signals, ensuring the safety and stability of the system. However, cable length has a significant impact on the frequency response characteristics of high-voltage dividers, which may introduce signal attenuation and phase distortion, thereby affecting measurement accuracy. This paper establishes an electrical model of cable distribution parameters and simulates cables of different lengths (0.1 m to 10 m) in the frequency range of $10^{-3} \mathrm{~Hz}$ to $10^{8} \mathrm{~Hz}$. It is found that cable length has a relatively small effect on the voltage divider ratio at low frequencies $\left(10^{-3} \mathrm{~Hz}\right.$ to $10^{5}$ Hz), while the effect of cable length is significant at high frequencies $\left(10^{5} \mathrm{~Hz}\right.$ to $\left.10^{8} \mathrm{~Hz}\right)$. The voltage divider ratio changes more significantly due to longer cables. The increase in cable length gradually brings the range of high-frequency signals affected closer to the low-frequency region. In addition, in logarithmic coordinates, a linear relationship between cable length and the frequency corresponding to 95% attenuation of the voltage divider ratio is observed, providing a basis for optimizing the frequency response characteristics of high-voltage dividers. To optimize frequency response, the paper proposes a correction method utilizing adaptive digital filtering techniques that integrate inverse filtering and model-based compensation, effectively mitigating high-frequency attenuation and phase distortion. This approach enhances measurement accuracy and stability in power systems, providing critical support for safe operation.

articleTitle: Frequency and Temperature Performance Comparison on the AC BTI of Commercial SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFET is currently widely used in many fields due to its several advantages, such as automotive drive train, solar inverter and aerospace applications. However, SiC MOSFET has always attracted much attention due to its poor gate oxide interface quality. One important way to determine the gate oxide quality is monitoring the drift in threshold voltage under AC bias temperature instability (AC BTI). Several teams have conducted comprehensive research on factors impacting on AC BTI. Two of the most important factors, frequency and junction temperature, may have different conclusions for different gate structures. Therefore, this paper uses three commercial gate structures of SiC MOSFET widely used nowadays as experimental device under test (DUTs), conducts experiments around the two influencing factors of frequency and temperature, and makes relevant conclusions and discussions on specific application fields.

articleTitle: Multi-Element Collaborative Optimization Strategy for Microgrids Considering Flexibility Resource Index Constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the advancement of energy technology, microgrids, as a form of power grid that can fully utilize wind and solar resources, have higher demands for their flexibility. Therefore, a multi-element collaborative optimization strategy considering flexibility resource index constraints for microgrids is proposed. First, considering the output characteristics of various flexibility resources and the uncertainty of wind and solar power, a quantification model for flexibility resource demand and supply is established. Secondly, a multi-element collaborative scheduling model is developed, aiming to minimize the total operation cost and flexibility deficit of the microgrid. Finally, the effectiveness and feasibility of the proposed method are demonstrated through case studies.

articleTitle: Load Forecasting Method Based on CEEMDAN Signal Decomposition and Improved BiLSTM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The accuracy of load forecasting in the power system becomes increasingly important with the step-by-step construction and improvement of new types of power systems. In this article, a method using the CEEMDAN algorithm for modal decomposition of sequences is proposed, where the decomposed sequences are separately analyzed for prediction and then reconstructed to form the complete signal sequence. The main prediction model uses BiLSTM. Compared to traditional LSTM, the ability of bidirectional reading allows BiLSTM to better understand and model the contextual information in the sequence, especially in tasks involving bidirectional dependencies where the effect is significant. Finally, the Love Evolutionary Optimization algorithm was used to improve the hyperparameters of the prediction model, further enhancing the prediction accuracy. By comparing the prediction accuracy results under different methods, further evidence was provided to support the advanced nature of this prediction method.

articleTitle: The obstacle avoidance path planning of flying robot for overhead power line inspection based on an improved A* algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In order to ensure the safe and collision-free navigation of electric power inspection drones in dynamic environments while simultaneously achieving optimal global and local paths and minimizing planning time, this paper presents a novel approach for obstacle avoidance path planning. The proposed method is based on an enhanced version of the $A^{*}$ algorithm specifically tailored for electric power inspection drones. Firstly, the $\mathbf{A}^{*}$ algorithm model analyzes the number and positional information of obstacle grid cells to quantify the density of obstacles in the environment. Next, the obstacle density information is integrated into the search strategy of the A* algorithm by enhancing the evaluation function and optimizing the selection of child nodes. Finally, by designing a node optimization algorithm, bidirectional smoothing and optimization of the path can be achieved.

articleTitle: Distributed Photovoltaic Multi-point Access Distribution Network Station Area Capacity Planning
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The massive quantity of distributed photovoltaic connections, will lead to a significant effect on the operation of the distribution station area. This paper presents a photovoltaic access capacity planning model and method for poverty alleviation photovoltaic access distribution network station area. A mathematical model with the goal of maximum photovoltaic access capacity is constructed, and the constraint conditions of node voltage, and line power flow, are optimized in the model by combining with the particle swarm optimization and penalty function. Taking the IEEE33-node standard system as an example, the consequences exhibit that the approach can efficaciously calculate the distributed photovoltaic capacity and location that can be accessed by the distribution network, and analyze the impact on the voltage and network loss, which provides a reference for guiding the distributed photovoltaic poverty alleviation security.

articleTitle: Open-Vocabulary Object Detection for Reliable Transformer Stand Installation Inspection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Ensuring the safety and proper placement of various components on transformer stands is critical in the installation inspection process within power grids. Traditional object detection methods often face challenges when dealing with the evolving requirements of installation processes and the potential introduction of unknown objects. This paper proposes a multimodal approach based on open-vocabulary object detection to enhance the reliability of transformer stand installation inspection. By integrating visual and textual information, the model effectively identifies known components and makes informed decisions when encountering unseen elements. Experimental results demonstrate the model’s robustness in complex scenarios, including background clutter and occlusions, as well as its ability to adapt to new equipment or signage. This approach not only improves detection accuracy and stability but also offers a flexible and adaptive solution for ensuring the safety and integrity of transformer stand installations. The findings of this study provide valuable insights into the application of open-vocabulary object detection in industrial settings, highlighting its potential for advancing intelligent inspection processes within power systems.

articleTitle: Optimal dispatch of power system based on joint operation of power plants with carbon capture technology and wind energy
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Global warming is becoming increasingly serious, and it is imperative to reduce carbon emissions. As the largest carbon-emitting industry, the power industry is responsible and obligated to reduce carbon emissions. First, carbon capture and storage (CCS) technology is introduced into traditional thermal power plants, and carbon capture power plants are built to capture and store emitted carbon to achieve low-carbon operation. Secondly, using wind energy as a power generation energy, its clean characteristics can realize low-carbon or even zero-carbon operation of wind power generation. Finally, the carbon capture power plant is combined with wind energy to improve carbon capture technology, reduce carbon emissions, improve wind power consumption, carbon capture efficiency, and the economy of the power system.

articleTitle: Loop Analysis and Compensation Design of Double-Clamped ZVS Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper presents the operating principles, loop analysis, and compensation design methods of the Double-Clamped ZVS (DCZVS) converter. This paper introduces a loop analysis and compensation design method for a Double-Clamped ZVS converter. The DCZVS converter, an optimized version of the flyback converter, employs four MOSFETs on the primary side of the transformer. By leveraging the resonance between the MOSFETs’ parasitic capacitance and the transformer’s leakage inductance, the drain-source voltage ($V_{D S}$) resonates to zero. In addition to the energy storage and energy transfer phases of a conventional flyback converter, a clamp phase is introduced to ensure zero-voltage switching across all MOSFETs, significantly improving efficiency. Compared to traditional flyback converters, the DCZVS converter offers greater design flexibility and a more complex control process. To rapidly obtain the small-signal model of the power supply loop, this paper employs frequency sweeping to determine the frequency response of the open-loop system. By fitting the obtained data, the transfer function of the system is established. Stability analysis is subsequently performed, followed by the design of appropriate loop compensation schemes to achieve closed-loop control of the system.

articleTitle: Research on main transformer neutral point grounding with small reactance and overvoltage protection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Transformer neutral point by small reactance grounding in the line to reduce the single-phase short-circuit current at the same time, improve the neutral point of the overvoltage level, small reactance resistance value is selected whether it is reasonable, will be directly related to the safe and stable operation of the power grid. In this paper, a 220 kV neutral point by small reactance system using ATP-EMTP (Alternative Transient Program - Electromagnetic Transients Program) software modeling, through the setting of single-phase faults in the station, quantitative analysis of the neutral point in series with different values of small reactance before and after the overvoltage and short-circuit voltage. The changes of industrial frequency overvoltage and short-circuit current are quantitatively analyzed before and after series connection of small reactors with different resistance values at the neutral point. Calculation and simulation results show that, with the increasing value of series reactance, the short-circuit current in the neutral point of the transformer decreases and gradually tends to be saturated, and the risk of insulation rises. If the purpose of connecting small reactance in series is to reduce the overvoltage and short-circuit current of the neutral point, to avoid the loss of ground overvoltage and to eliminate the insecurity caused by the discharge gap, it is recommended to choose transformer zero sequence reactance), which can ensure that the neutral point of both main transformers is connected to a small reactance. It is recommended to choose transformer zero sequence reactance), so as to ensure that the zero sequence reactance and short circuit current of the system remain unchanged after both main transformers are grounded by small reactance.

articleTitle: Planning and configuration method for DESS considering DN losses
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Distributed energy storage system (DESS) is the key way to improve the flexibility and stability of distribution network (DN) and promote the consumption of renewable energy. Aiming at the problem of location and capacity of the DESS connected to the DN, this paper proposes a planning and configuration method of the DESS considering the network losses of the DN. Firstly, aiming at minimizing the DN loss, a location model of energy storage system considering the DN losses are constructed. Secondly, aiming at the lowest construction cost of DESS, the capacity allocation model of DESS is constructed. Then, the DESS location model and capacity allocation model are combined to form a DESS planning and configuration model, which is solved by gurobi. Finally, taking the improved IEEE33 node grid structure as an example, the effectiveness of the proposed planning and configuration method is verified.

articleTitle: A temperature estimation method for lithium-ion batteries
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The temperature estimation of lithium-ion batteries is crucial for the safe operation of energy storage power stations. While existing thermal models for lithium-ion batteries can accurately estimate the temperature state of batteries, the estimation time is too long to meet the engineering requirements of timeliness. This paper focuses on the 280Ah square energy storage lithium-ion battery. Firstly, a variable-parameter secondorder equivalent circuit model and a variable-parameter thermal circuit model were established, and then a variable-parameter thermal circuit-circuit coupling model was established based on the coupling relationship between current, internal resistance, power, SOC (state of charge) and temperature. Secondly, the parameter identification of the model was accomplished using the least squares algorithm based on the data from the Hybrid Pulse Power Characterization experiment. Finally, the model is verified by the experimental conditions and the actual operating conditions of the energy storage station. The error between the temperature estimated by the model and the actual temperature is less than $0.3^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, and 2.97s can accomplish the temperature estimation of a single lithium-ion battery for one day of actual work.

articleTitle: Day-ahead Market Trading Strategies for VPP Considering Electric Vehicles and Interruptible Loads
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the increasing share of new energy generation worldwide, the scheduling optimisation of virtual power plant(VPP), as an important part of modern power systems, is crucial for improving the economics and stability of power grids. This paper proposes an optimal scheduling strategy for VPP considering electric vehicles(EVs) and interruptible loads, aiming to minimise the total system operating cost by exploiting the demand response capabilities of various resources within VPP. In this paper, the main resources within the VPP, including gas turbines, photovoltaic generation, energy storage systems, and two demand response resources, interruptible loads and electric vehicle loads, are firstly mathematically modelled and the corresponding optimal scheduling models are developed. The objective of the model is to be solved using the CPLEX solver of the MATLAB software to achieve coordination and complementarity of internal resources, optimise energy allocation and utilisation, and thus reduce operating costs, while satisfying multiple constraints. The results of the analyses of the algorithms show that the proposed method significantly reduces the total operating cost of VPP while improving the resource utilisation, especially during peak load hours, the optimised demand response strategy effectively reduces the system supply and demand pressures, and improves the economy and stability of the power system.

articleTitle: Stress Analysis of earthing grid laid in different modes under ground subsidence conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In China, the galvanized flat steels are often used as grounding grid horizontal conductor materials, and laid with their flat face (width and length plane) upwards. Under the ground settlement condition, this laying mode of horizontal conductor will subject to huge load and deformation, and then great risk of the fracture of earth conductors and down-leads. This paper proposes a new grounding grid laying mode, in which the horizontal conductors are laid with the thickness face (thickness and length plane) upwards. The stress and deformation distribution on the grounding grids laid in two different modes were analyzed by using finite element analysis. The deformation of the grounding conductor and down-lead of the grounding grid increases with an increase in the amount of ground settlement. Under the condition of ground settlement, for the small model grounding grid in this paper, when the settlement amount increased to 50 and 100 mm, the maximum stress on the grounding grid laid with new mode is just $\mathbf{1 7 \%}$ and $\mathbf{2 3. 9 \%}$ of that on grounding grid laid with old mode, respectively. Laying the he horizontal conductors with the thickness face (thickness and length plane) upwards can significantly decrease the fracture risk of down-leads and earthing conductors, and increases the ability of grounding grid to withstand the ground settlement disaster.

articleTitle: Short-Term Smart Grid Load Forecasting Based on CNN-BiLSTM with Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The existing power load data exhibits complex multidimensionality, while existing techniques often focus on learning and forecasting from single load data. To fully exploit the complex multidimensionality of the existing power load data and enhance the accuracy of short-term load forecasting, a smart grid short-term load forecasting model based on attention mechanism and CNN-BiLSTM is proposed. Firstly, the one-dimensional convolutional network (1D-CNN) slides along the temporal dimension to extract multidimensional features such as temperature and humidity from the raw power load data. Secondly, the Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory network (BiLSTM) captures both historical and future information of the data through gate mechanisms and the bidirectional network structure. Lastly, the attention mechanism allocates weights to focus on important parts of the load sequence data, enhancing the model’s ability to identify key information and further improving the accuracy of short-term power load forecasting. The method is experimented on a real-world multivariate load dataset and compared with existing learning methods. The proposed model achieved lower RMSE in 24-hour load forecasting compared to CNN-LSTM, CNN-BiLSTM, LSTM-Attention, BiLSTM-Attention and CNN-LSTM-Attention models by 13.2%, 10.6%, 6.7%, 5.7% and 5.9% respectively.

articleTitle: A Second-Order Cone Optimization Method for Distribution Networks Containing Renewable Energy Sources
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Vigorous development of renewable energy sources is an important way to achieve the dual-carbon goal. The large amount of distributed renewable energy sources introduces significant uncertainty and challenges the economic operation of the system. This paper proposes a second-order cone optimization method for a power distribution network with a high proportion of renewable energy to improve system operation economy. First, the wind power generation model is introduced to obtain the relationship between wind speed and wind power. Next, the photovoltaic power generation model is provided to derive the relationship between light intensity and photovoltaic output. Then, the power system optimization model containing renewable energy sources is constructed and transformed into a second order cone convex optimization problem through conditional relaxation, which is effectively solved via “Gurobi”. Finally, simulations are conducted on the IEEE 33-bus distribution system to verify that the proposed method could rapidly achieve the system solution while improving the system operation economy.

articleTitle: Coordinated optimal configuration scheme of wind-solar ratio and energy storage considering wind-solar complementary characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This study proposes a collaborative optimization configuration scheme of wind-solar ratio and energy storage based on the complementary characteristics of wind and light. On the premise of maintaining the stability of the wind-solar hybrid power generation system, the optimal allocation model of wind-solar ratio and energy storage considering the complementary characteristics of wind-solar is established with the minimum total cost of planning. At the same time, three indicators of power fluctuation index, wind-solar permeability and new energy abandonment rate are proposed to evaluate the scheme.

articleTitle: Electric theft system detection based on genetic algorithm optimization neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Electricity theft detection has always been a research problem in the power system. This paper introduces a novel approach utilizing genetic algorithm-optimized neural networks (GA-ANN) for electricity theft detection in power systems. The research focuses on leveraging raw data from current and voltage measurements to train and optimize neural network parameters, enhancing theft detection robustness. To validate the proposed approach, four simulated power system mechanisms are employed, showcasing the GA-ANN model’s effectiveness in accurately identifying theft incidents across diverse scenarios. Experimental results demonstrate the model’s high accuracy and robustness in theft detection, surpassing traditional models and algorithms.

articleTitle: Optimisation of electrochemical energy storage based on deep learning algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Currently, machine learning is widely used in the field of energy storage batteries, and its superiority has been proved in terms of time efficiency and prediction accuracy. Among them, various algorithms have different characteristics and adaptive ranges, and choosing a suitable machine-learning algorithm is a key step in constructing a machine-learning model, which greatly affects its prediction accuracy and generalization ability. The key to energy storage batteries is materials. Data-driven materials science makes use of the large amount of data accumulated by traditional experimental, theoretical, and computational simulation methods to model and analyze the performance-driving mechanisms of electrochemical energy storage materials with the help of data-driven artificial intelligence methods in order to accelerate the research, development, and design of new high-performance electrochemical energy storage materials. Currently, as one of the typical representatives of data-driven artificial intelligence methods, machine learning has been widely applied to materials performance prediction and new materials discovery. The application of machine learning in the field of batteries can be traced back to the use of fuzzy logic methods by Salkind et al. in 1999 to determine the state of charge and health of batteries. This paper is based on the combination of deep learning big data algorithms and electrochemical energy storage, which provides a breakthrough and analysis in the field of convergence.

articleTitle: Coordinated Voltage Control for Distributed Photovoltaic Storage System Based on Fast Finite-Time Consistency
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In recent years, the penetration of distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems in distribution networks has increased. The temporal and spatial mismatch between PV output and load often causes voltage overruns, impacting the safe and stable operation of the network. This paper proposes a two-stage distributed control strategy for photovoltaic inverters and energy storage, based on a fast finite-time consistency algorithm. First, the principle of voltage overruns in distributed PV low-voltage networks is analyzed. The reactive power utilization of the PV inverter and changes in the storage charge state are selected as consistency variables. The coordinated control of the PV inverter’s reactive power and the storage system’s active power is then achieved using the fast finite-time consistency algorithm. Finally, a 14-node low-voltage distribution network with a distributed PV storage system is used for validation. The results demonstrate that the proposed strategy overcomes the limitations of single-link control, effectively mitigates voltage overruns, and reduces voltage control costs.

articleTitle: Study on the optimal daily operating cost of electricity consumption for an integrated energy system with shared energy storage power station
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Shared energy storage is an innovative solution for managing electrical resources. It releases stored electricity during peak demand to balance supply and demand and charges during off-peak hours to improve efficiency. A well-structured pricing mechanism motivates active participation in demand response, leading to efficient energy use and significant cost savings. This study developed a detailed operational model for an integrated energy system with shared energy storage, considering the characteristics of transferable loads, cuttable loads and shiftable loads. An optimization function was formulated to reduce daily operating expenses using a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) method for scheduling strategies. The optimization challenge was addressed with the Yalmip toolbox and Gurobi solver, employing the branch-and-bound technique for case analysis. The conclusion showed that shared energy storage greatly improved system economics, effectively performed peak shaving and valley filling, and reduced total operational costs, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed model and methodology.

articleTitle: Massive measurement data continuity and safety guarantee technology in new power system
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Massive measurement data continuity and safety guarantee technology plays an important role in the normal development of power businesses. However, the power meter, acquisition terminal, concentrator, and other system terminals face different safety risk threats. Aiming at the problems of poor continuity and low safety of power measurement data in the new power system, this paper first designs the overall architecture of data continuity and safety guarantee components, studies the design scheme of each component, and clarifies the function of each component. Then, we propose the measurement data continuity and safety guarantee technology and use the adaptive threshold isolated forest algorithm based on the golden section rate to improve the accuracy of abnormal data identification. Finally, the data continuity and safety guarantee components are tested to verify that the proposed method can improve the continuity and safety of power measurement data.

articleTitle: Optimizing Off-Grid Island Microgrid Design with Green Energy Using HOMER Pro
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Off-grid island microgrids, which integrate renewable energy sources, are instrumental in addressing the challenges of electricity provision and environmental sustainability in remote locales. This study presents an optimization design of a microgrid system on a specific Chinese island, leveraging the HOMER Pro software for power system simulation as a design support tool. The design capitalizes on the island’s bountiful wind and solar resources by employing a hybrid wind-solar power generation strategy to supply the microgrid with electricity. The simulation outcomes from HOMER Pro demonstrate that the proposed system exhibits favorable economic viability, environmental sustainability, and reliability in power supply.

articleTitle: A short-term low-carbon economic dispatch method of power system considering carbon capture units and optimized mixed coal combustion
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In order to response the carbon peak and carbon neutrality strategy and enhance the emission reduction level of thermal power units, a short-term low-carbon economic dispatch model considering carbon capture units and mixed coal combustion is established. Firstly, analyze various coal emission requirements of thermal power units and consider the refined emission process of thermal power units. Secondly, take combustion characteristics of different coal types into account and propose a new thermal power unit operational method with mixed coal combustion. Then, rebuild thermal power units with carbon capture equipment and construct a short-term low-carbon economic dispatch model combining the economy and low-carbon benefits of carbon capture units. Finally, case studies demonstrate that the proposed method effectively reduces CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> emission while optimizing system economic operation.

articleTitle: Distributed photovoltaic reliability research
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the increasing emphasis on renewable energy, the importance of distributed photovoltaic systems in the energy sector is increasing. In this paper, the fault tree analysis (FTA) method is used to study the reliability of distributed photovoltaic systems. The failure modes and interrelationships of components such as photovoltaic modules, combiner boxes, inverters, energy storage devices and monitoring systems are discussed, and the weak links of the system are revealed. The results show that the string PV system has more advantages in matching the optimal working point of the PV array. This paper provides a theoretical basis for improving the stability and prolonging the service life of distributed photovoltaic systems.

articleTitle: Optimal Dispatch Strategy for Load Aggregators Considering Source-Load-Storage Interaction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: As the proportion of renewable energy generation in the power grid continues to rise, the inherent instability of its power output poses significant challenges to the stable operation of the power system. Therefore, how to leverage the flexibility of demand-side resources to interact effectively with renewable energy generation, thereby promoting the full utilization of new energy, has become an urgent research topic. This paper proposes a novel optimal dispatch strategy for load aggregators that takes into account the energy interaction mechanism among sources, loads, and energy storage, while also considering the cost of dispatch. Through simulation experiments, the effectiveness of this strategy in promoting the absorption of wind and solar energy has been verified.

articleTitle: 3D Simulation of Edge Diffraction of Sound Barrier in Substation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the development of urbanization, substations have started to be built in urban areas where the population is concentrated. In order to effectively control the noise pollution from substations, sound barriers are built inside the substations to block the propagation of noise, so the sound insulation value of the sound barriers becomes an important indicator. However, the edge diffraction phenomenon will lead to errors between the real sound attenuation and the laboratory measurement value. The classical geometrical diffraction theory is a commonly used method to estimate the sound attenuation from edge of the barrier. However, it is a 2D model which cannot be used for 3D problem. In order to correctly estimate the sound attenuation in a 3D environment, this paper conducts relevant research. Firstly, it investigates the influencing factors of sound attenuation caused by the edge diffraction. Then, a 3D simulation model based on the classical 2D geometric diffraction theory is proposed. The accuracy of the model is verified by simulation test and experimental test for barriers with different shapes. The results show that the model is capable of giving satisfied estimations of the edge diffraction from the sound barrier in substation.

articleTitle: A New Type of User Side Energy Storage Intelligent Operation System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the high penetration of distributed power sources into the power grid, the role of user side energy storage as a way to alleviate the randomness, volatility and other output characteristics of distributed power sources is becoming increasingly prominent. In order to better utilize user side energy storage to improve the reliability of power grid operation, this article develops a new type of user side energy storage intelligent operation system. The paper first studies the core content of hardware construction such as the constituent modules and specific functions of the household optical storage intelligent operation system; Then the Software architecture composed of terminal layer, human-computer interaction layer and core application layer is studied; Further analyze the working mode of the user side energy storage intelligent operation system. The operation of the developed user side energy storage intelligent operation system has proven its effectiveness.

articleTitle: A New four-dimensional chaotic spread spectrum technology for EMI suppression of Zeta converter
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper introduces an Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) spread spectrum technology with a new four-dimensional chaotic method for the Zeta converter. This paper introduces a novel approach to enhance EMI suppression in power converters. It presents a chaotic pulse width modulation (PWM) method derived from a four-dimensional chaotic circuit, aiming to achieve more effective EMI suppression by improving the spread spectrum distribution at both the switching frequency and its harmonics. Furthermore, a chaotic PWM has been simulated using Multisim for the Zeta converter under study and a comparison has been conducted with conventional PWM control. Finally, the circuit of the new system is implemented and the impact on mitigating output EMI has been shown.

articleTitle: Research on Intelligent Identification Method of CT Secondary Circuit Virtual Connection Based on Harmonic Current Spectrum Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The virtual connection of the secondary circuit of current transformers will generate risks such as heating, inaccurate measurement, and protection (refusal) maloperation, which not only endanger electrical equipment but also pose a huge threat to personal safety. It must be detected and eliminated early. In response to the problems and shortcomings of existing open circuit monitoring devices for current transformers, this paper proposes an intelligent identification method for virtual connections in the secondary circuit of current transformers based on harmonic current spectrum analysis. By analyzing the harmonic content of the secondary circuit, it can determine whether virtual connections have occurred. The virtual connection recognition device has a simple structure and high sensitivity and accuracy in judgment. It can recognize various forms and degrees of virtual connections of current transformers, making the system operate more safely and reliably.

articleTitle: Research on insulator infrared image segmentation based on GANR-UNet
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In order to address the problems of insulator segmentation accuracy caused by the existence of complex background, inconspicuous contrast, and image quality not guaranteed in insulator images taken by aerial photography of transmission line inspection, an optimized segmentation model based on Residual UNet (R-UNet) and Generative Adversarial Networks (GAN) is proposed. First, the R-UNet segmentation network is constructed by pre-training the ResNet18 network on a large dataset and using it as a coding network for the UNet model, which effectively improves the segmentation of insulator strings by utilizing its deep feature extraction capability. Then, combined with the generative adversarial network, the GANR-UNet model is proposed to further improve the insulator segmentation accuracy. Finally, the experimental results show that compared with the traditional R-UNet model, the GANR-UNet model improves the precision (Precision) by $\mathbf{0. 6 3 \%}$, the recall by 1.15%, and also excels in the intersection-to-union ratio (IoU) and other metrics, especially in the extraction of insulator edges. This study provides more accurate technical support for insulator infrared image segmentation, which has important practical application value.

articleTitle: Battery Health Prediction Based on Multi-Parameter Charging Feature Identification
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The estimation of battery health plays a crucial role in battery management and system safety. With the widespread use of batteries in various applications, such as electric vehicles, portable devices, and renewable energy systems, accurately extracting battery charging characteristics has become essential. This paper proposes a multi-channel charging feature extraction method. This method involves extracting degradation features from the voltage and current charging curves as health indicators. Heatmaps are used to demonstrate the strong correlations among these features. The method was validated using the NASA battery dataset and evaluated through various representative machine learning techniques to achieve accurate battery health assessment. Multiple performance metrics were employed for validation. The experimental results indicate that, compared to models trained with single features, the models trained with the proposed features exhibit higher accuracy, with prediction metrics falling below 4%.

articleTitle: A Security Monitoring Method for Distributed Photovoltaic Systems Based on Log Association and Fusion Analysis Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Traditional log analysis relies heavily on predefined rules, failing to detect unknown attacks promptly. Integrating log analysis with machine learning improves accuracy and the ability to detect complex attacks. This paper focuses on the log data of distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems, combining clustering algorithms and association analysis to enhance security monitoring techniques. Key contributions include: Proposing a parallel improved Apriori algorithm based on hash storage and transaction weighting to enhance association rule mining performance. This algorithm compresses the dataset by deduplication, reduces the number of database scans, and utilizes MapReduce for parallel computation, significantly improving efficiency. Developing a complete solution for anomaly detection in distributed PV systems using association rule mining. This solution addresses the low efficiency of handling massive log data through data collection, feature selection, and model training and detection, establishing a normal behavior rule base for anomaly detection.The proposed methods effectively improve the accuracy and efficiency of anomaly detection in distributed PV systems using log association fusion analysis technology.

articleTitle: Insulator Defect Detection Network Integrating the GD Mechanism with Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of poor detection effect of insulator defect images in complex inspection environment due to small target and large scale difference, an insulator defect detection algorithm based on improved YOLOv8 is proposed. Firstly, a new attention mechanism, Channel Prior Multi-scale Convolutional Attention, is proposed, which is added after Backbone to enhance the feature output and further strengthen the identification of different insulator defects; secondly, the introduction of the Gather and distribute mechanism to reconstruct the neck network, which improves the fusion ability of multi-scale target features; finally, multi-scale feature combination is achieved by adding the Scale sequence feature fusion module to the front of the Head, which enhances the detection ability of multi-scale and small objects. The experimental results show that the mAP0.5 of the algorithm in this paper reaches 92.3%, which is 7.5% higher than that of the standard YOLOv8, and the average accuracy of the flashover and broken defect detection is increased by 14.0% and 8.3%, respectively, and the defect detection algorithm proposed in this paper is able to better and accurately identify defects in insulators of different scales.

articleTitle: Research on Reinforcement Learning-based Optimization Algorithm for Electric Vehicle Charging Scheduling
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the rapid growth in the number of electric vehicles, how to effectively manage their charging demand has become an important challenge for power systems. In this paper, we propose an EV charging scheduling optimization algorithm that combines power big data analysis and deep reinforcement learning (DQN). The algorithm aims to optimize the charging scheduling to balance the grid load, reduce the charging cost and enhance the satisfaction rate of users’ charging demand. Through simulation experiments, the effectiveness of the DQN optimization algorithm in reducing the peak hour grid load, lowering the charging cost and enhancing user satisfaction is verified. The experimental results show that the optimization scheme significantly reduces the peak grid load, reduces the charging cost by about 10.29%, and improves the user demand satisfaction rate by 5.2%.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Temperature Control Based on Operator Theory for Microreactors Considering Disturbance and Interference
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In recent years, microreactors, in which reactions are carried out in tiny liquid channels, have attracted attention as a next-generation chemical reaction device using the flow method. Microreactors have the advantage of faster and more efficient chemical reactions than conventional batch methods due to their large surface area per unit volume. However, precise temperature control is necessary because temperature changes in the flow path due to reaction heat can adversely affect reactions. The objective of this study is to design a control system for microreactor systems cooled by Peltier devices that is resistant to disturbances and interference, thereby achieving more robust temperature control of microreactors. A control system including a disturbance compensator will be designed based on operator theory, and its effectiveness will be confirmed through experiments. Experimental results under external thermal disturbance are also compared to demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed disturbance compensator.

articleTitle: A Method of Generating Ice Accident Disposal Plan and Evaluating Power Supply Capacity Based on Power Flow Transfer Relationship
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: To solve the problems of many high-risk lines and fault combinations in the event of ice accidents, and the heavy workload of grid mode personnel in formulating ice accident plans and evaluating the power supply capacity of ice-constrained areas, a method for generating ice accident disposal plans and evaluating power supply capacity based on power flow transfer relationship is proposed. The enumeration method is used to automatically generate the ice disaster accident mode data of the power grid, and the active power flow of the fault state branch is described as a function of the active power flow of the base state transmission channel based on the power flow transfer relationship, so as to establish the accident disposal plan and power supply capacity evaluation model, and reduce the computation amount of the model solution through the redundant constraint filtering technology. Through the solution, the unit output adjustment strategy, regional power supply capacity and control key constraints are automatically given, which greatly reduces the workload of the grid mode personnel and provides auxiliary decision-making. The example results of Guilin Power Grid show that each ice accident approach takes 3.6 seconds on average, and the proposed method can well meet the requirements of practical engineering applications.

articleTitle: Calculate of Probabilistic Power of RERs Participating into Power Balance Considering Loss Load Probability
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the participating of renewable energy resources (RERs) into power balance, power system is confronted with loss load probability due to the inherent fluctuation and uncertainty of RERs. In this paper, a probabilistic power model of RERs considering loss load probability is proposed to calculate the power of RERs which participating day-ahead generation scheduling. Firstly, the Information Entropy (IE) theory is introduced to quantify the uncertainty of the system at each moment. Leveraging the level of uncertainty, historical data is divided into multiple time periods and the loss load probability is selected. Secondly, the equivalent power model of RERs is developed to reduce supply risk, with a full consideration of derived power balance constraint which was transformed into a probabilistic form after taking into account the stochastic characteristic of load and RERs. Finally, the simulation result reveals that proposed model can effectively calculate the equivalent power of RERs participating day-ahead power balance, which greatly improves power supply reliability and reduces the supply risk of power system.

articleTitle: Design of Remote Fault Diagnosis System for Hydropower Unit Based on Cloud Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: As the installed capacity of power plants continues to increase, the complexity of equipment is getting higher and higher, and the importance and difficulty of fault monitoring also increases. In this paper, a human-machine closed-loop remote fault diagnosis system with self-learning function is designed. The establishment of the remote fault diagnosis system for hydropower units based on the cloud platform can fully integrate the accumulated experience and expert knowledge of power plants, and be able to collect and deeply mine the data of related units in different power plants during the operation process, so as to improve the diagnostic efficiency and accuracy of the system. The system introduces the concept of “improvement factor”, realizes the remote interconnection of the inference machine system with domain experts and technicians, and includes human beings in the diagnostic loop to calculate the “improvement factor”, so that the diagnostic process can continuously improve its confidence level. The system consists of three core modules: a fault knowledge base containing confidence factors, a hydropower unit fault diagnosis engine, and an equipment health assessment engine.

articleTitle: Optimization strategy of multi-type energy storage considering carbon constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of difficult carbon and electricity coupling and new energy consumption in the new power system, this paper proposes a multiple energy storage optimization operation model considering carbon constraints. Firstly, a mathematical model is established according to the response characteristics of each energy storage, and the corresponding constraints are set; secondly, a carbon trading mechanism for an integrated energy system is constructed by considering the actual carbon emission of a gas turbine; finally, the linear programming problem is solved by a solver with the objective function of minimising the sum of the carbon trading cost and the operation and maintenance cost. The results show that the reasonable allocation of the proportion of each energy storage is conducive to improving the system operation economy, and the carbon emissions are significantly reduced after the introduction of the carbon trading mechanism.

articleTitle: Research on Task Scheduling Methods in 5G Mobile Edge Computing Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the development of smart grids, power data presents characteristics of massive volume, high speed, and high heterogeneity, posing higher requirements for data processing and transmission capabilities. The innovation of 5G technology has made edge computing more widely applied in smart grids, helping to solve data transmission bottlenecks, reduce latency, and enhance real-time monitoring capabilities. This paper combines the FCFS, EDF, and SJF algorithms to propose a new comprehensive scheduling algorithm, DWECS (Dynamic Weighted Edge Computing Scheduler). By setting task priorities and resource allocation strategies, DWECS effectively improves task completion efficiency and controls system operating costs. This research provides a new method for edge computing task scheduling in smart grids and supports the intelligent and economic management of distribution networks.

articleTitle: Optimization of Relay Protection Device Renovation Plan for East China Power Grid Using Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG)
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
