abstract: In this paper, a method for optimizing the retrofit scheme of relay protection devices in East China Power Grid based on Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) algorithm is proposed. By constructing a state evaluation model and life cycle management method, the timing and strategy of relay protection device retrofit are optimized by combining the DDPG algorithm. The experimental results show that the average trouble-free operation time of the modified equipment increased from 555 hours to $\mathbf{7 1 0}$ hours; the correct action rate increased from 89.83% to $94.83 \%$; the number of power outages was reduced from 5.3 to 3.3, and the duration of outages was reduced from 10.6 hours to 6.6 hours. In the conclusion of the above data, the DDPG optimization scheme can significantly improve the operational reliability of relay protection devices and the stability and security of the power grid.

articleTitle: Output Feedback MPC with N Free Control Moves for DC-DC Boost Converter System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper studies the output feedback model predictive control (OFMPC) for DC-DC boost converter systems via the N free control moves strategy. First, a new deviation model of DC-DC boost converter system is established to describe the dynamic characteristics of the investigated system. Second, in view of the state observer provided by off-line solving an optimization problem, the OFMPC with N free control moves, which involves splitting the infinite horizon control moves into the single state feedback law in the terminal region and a sequence of free control moves, is presented by minimizing the performance index upper bound respecting the input and state constraints of the DC-DC boost converter system. Finally, the provided algorithm about DC-DC boost converter is validated by simulation experiments.

articleTitle: Fault Reconfiguration in Distribution Networks through Multi-Energy Cooperative Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper develops a novel configuration for fault recovery in a distribution network by implementing a multi-energy cooperative energy network. The interconnected energy subsystems enable a coordinated response to system disruptions, leveraging coupling elements. Upon active network segmentation of the distribution network, the system transitions to an islanded operational mode, with distributed generation (DG) supplying power to each island. Simultaneously, parts of the loads are reconfigured as non-electrical systems, facilitating the transfer of energy across different forms. Coupling elements, such as gas turbines and combined heat and power (CHP) units, enhance electrical output, contributing crucial support for the network. These elements play a pivotal role in restoring energy supply and directly influence the effectiveness of the recovery process. The innovation significantly enhances the resilience and reliability of distribution networks, offering a robust solution for modern energy systems.

articleTitle: Research of short circuit Level Improvement of Transformation Substation Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: During the 15th Five-year Plan period, with the access of DC and its supporting power supply, the overall short circuit current of northwest power grid continues to rise, and short circuit current of more and more substations will be more than 63 kA. When there are no measures to limit the short circuit current by adjusting the grid structure, installing the series reactor or the fault current limiter, it is particularly urgent to develop a higher block capacity circuit breaker and other equipment in the distribution device to meet the needs of the future development of the power grid. According to the system forecast, the recommended short circuit current level is increased from 63 kA to 80 kA. Through the investigation of the mainstream substation equipment manufacturers at home and abroad, theoretically there is no insurmountable technical bottleneck problem of increasing the short circuit current level from 63 kA to 80 kA. According to the research results of the equipment manufacturer and the transformation design experience, this paper proposes the design requirements of increasing the short circuit level from 63 kA to 80 kA.

articleTitle: Distributed new energy generation prediction method in DN based on FOEO grey prediction model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In view of the problem that the existing grey prediction model (GPM) is difficult to fully adapt to the expanding practical application scenarios. In this paper, a new distributed new energy generation forecasting method in distribution network (DN) based on fractional order extended operator (FOEO) grey forecasting model is proposed. Firstly, the GPM of FOEO is constructed, and the fractional order accumulation generation operator and fractional order subtraction generation operator are used to process the data. Secondly, the solution method of the prediction model is given. Then, the effectiveness and accuracy of the proposed method are verified by comparing the prediction method proposed in this paper with the traditional grey prediction method. Finally, the generation of distributed new energy in a regional DN during the accelerated transition period (2024-2030) in China is predicted, and the prediction data can provide reference for the construction of distributed new energy in the DN in the future.

articleTitle: Analysis of characteristics in motor failure of power system based on power spectral entropy
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In power systems, the asynchronous motor is a critical equipment, and it has a wide range of applications in power generation, transmission and distribution, and production. Therefore, monitoring the operation status of the asynchronous motor in real time and interpreting the type of fault plays a vital role in the entire power system. To this end, this paper uses the power spectral entropy to identify the fault for the asynchronous motor, introduces the concepts of information entropy and power spectral entropy, and proposes the analysis of the fault characteristics of the asynchronous motor in the modified IEEE 9bus system. The measurement is taken from the voltage and current signals inside and outside the asynchronous motor. The result shows that the value calculated by the power spectral entropy is the auxiliary indicator for fault discrimination in asynchronous motors.

articleTitle: A TEC-Based Thermal Solution for Quantum Current Sensors in Grid Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper investigates the heat dissipation problem of a diamond NV quantum current sensor with an integrated laser diode in practical applications. Firstly, the heat generation of the internal components of the sensor is evaluated through experimental analysis. The findings indicate that the sensor with this structure is susceptible to heat accumulation during high-power operation, which subsequently affects the sensor’s performance. To address this issue, a heat dissipation scheme utilizing a thermal electric cooler (TEC) in conjunction with heat sink fins is proposed, and the performance of two distinct heat sink fins is evaluated. The experimental results demonstrate that the heat sink fins with heat pipes exhibit an enhanced heat dissipation effect while maintaining a compact size and minimal weight. Furthermore, in order to reduce the magnetic field interference caused by the TEC, a distal-mounted TEC scheme is designed. However, this scheme exhibits a lower heat dissipation efficiency compared to the proximal-mounted TEC scheme at 2W heating power. This study proposes a solution for the heat dissipation design of this type of quantum current sensor, which provides a reliable method for its future application in power grid systems.

articleTitle: Prediction of dissolved gas content in transformer oil based on VMD-GRU
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This study presents a novel prediction model founded on Variational Mode Decomposition (VMD) and Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) techniques, aimed at addressing the challenge posed by the nonlinearity and non-stationarity of sequences on the accuracy of dissolved gas content prediction in transformer oil. Initially, the model employs the differential method to extract the trend term from the original sequence, followed by VMD decomposition of the residual sequence to derive a series of stationary modal components. Subsequently, GRU is employed to forecast each modal component, and ultimately, the prediction outcomes are reconstructed to yield the final prediction value. Experimental validation demonstrates a significant enhancement in prediction accuracy for H2 dissolved gas with the VMD-GRU model. Furthermore, simulation experiments conducted on other dissolved gas components such as CH4, CO, total hydrocarbons, etc., corroborate the efficacy of the prediction model, underscoring its broad applicability and reliability in forecasting dissolved gas content in transformer oil.

articleTitle: Evaluation Method for Moisture Content of Oil-Immersed Bushing Based on Davidson-Cole Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The oil paper insulating bushing is the core components which power transformer connects the external equipment. There is a risk of external moisture entering during operation. An increase in moisture content will significantly reduce the oil paper insulation characteristics. To achieve a non-destructive testing method for moisture content in oil-paper insulation bushing, the paper analyzes the complex frequency domain dielectric spectroscopy of oil-paper insulation bushing based on the double relaxation Davidson-Cole model, and proposes a method for extracting moisture characteristic parameters and evaluating moisture degree. Firstly, the double relaxation Davidson Cole model was used to analyze the model parameters of the frequency domain dielectric parameters of oil-immersed bushings with different moisture content. Secondly, the variation pattern of parameters in the double relaxation Davidson-Cole model was analyzed, and the DC conductivity $\sigma$ and polarization intensity $\triangle \varepsilon 1$ were determined as a characteristic parameter to characterize the moisture content in oil-immersed bushings, and the two have an exponential relationship with moisture content. Finally, the fitting formula with moisture content and the characteristic parameter (DC conductivity $\sigma$ and polarization intensity $\triangle \varepsilon 1$) were proposed, and a moisture evaluation method for oil-paper insulating bushing based on frequency domain dielectric spectroscopy and double relaxation Davidson-Cole model was proposed. Related research can provide a basis for evaluating the degree of moisture content of oil-immersed bushings.

articleTitle: Short-term Recovery of Silicon Carbide Power MOSFET Threshold Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the growing application of silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs, the instability issues of the threshold voltage have attracted significant attention. However, there is limited research on the recovery performance of the threshold voltage of SiC MOSFETs. In this paper, the SiC MOSFET short-term threshold voltage recovery was experimentally studied. It is found that the short-term recovery properties of threshold voltage are affected not only by the gate bias but also by the bias time. The research results not only provide a reference for threshold voltage measurement but also improve the understanding of threshold voltage instability.

articleTitle: Orderly Charging Strategy for Electric Vehicles Based on Elite Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The rapid growth of clean and efficient electric vehicles (EVs) is becoming an important flexibility resource. However, the scale of disorderly charging into the grid poses a challenge to the grid. Therefore, guiding the orderly charging of EVs is crucial to alleviate new energy fluctuations and stabilize grid load. Firstly, this paper establishes the system architecture for orderly charging of EVs. Then, it models the charging behavior of EVs in sub-functional areas and sets up multi-optimization objectives. Finally, it achieves the orderly charging scheduling of EVs through the use of the elite genetic algorithm for solving. The simulation results show that the orderly charging method for EVs proposed in this paper can effectively reduce the net load peakvalley difference rate, improve the new energy consumption rate, and reduce the charging cost; the elite genetic algorithm used has better optimal results and better convergence than the traditional genetic algorithm.

articleTitle: Scheme for automatics transfer switch without splitting new energy source
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the large-scale integration of photovoltaics into the power grid, traditional automatic transfer switch device may fail to operate correctly. Traditional solutions can lead to a decrease in energy utilization efficiency of photovoltaic power plants. Another solution can result in significant impulse current during grid connection in the case of a mismatch between the source and load. This article focuses on the situation where the source is greater than the load, adopting the perturbation and observation (P&O) method to control the duty cycle of the Boost circuit in the photovoltaic array. When the output power approaches the target value after applying a disturbance, continue to apply the disturbance in that direction. Conversely, apply a disturbance in the opposite direction, so that the output power of the photovoltaic array continuously approaches the load power, achieving the goal of minimizing the impulse current during grid connection. Finally, through simulation experiments, compare the impulse current generated during grid connection by adopting the traditional solution and the solution using P&O method after a fault. The simulation results show that the solution using P&O method can reduce the inrush current during grid connection.

articleTitle: The feature recognition algorithm of reactive power metering difference considering dynamic and static power meter misconnection
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In the power system, the accurate measurement of electricity meters is the basis for ensuring the fairness of power trading and maintaining the stable operation of the power grid. However, misconnection occurs frequently, especially in reactive power measurement, which seriously affects the accuracy and reliability of measurement. Therefore, this paper deeply studies the influence of misconnection of watt-hour meter on the difference characteristics of reactive power measurement under the dynamic and static relationship, and proposes a recognition algorithm. Firstly, the specific effects of wrong wiring on the principle of reactive power measurement are systematically analyzed, including voltage wrong wiring, current wrong wiring and phase mismatch of voltage and current. Then, combining the characteristics of dynamic and static data, an efficient feature recognition algorithm of reactive power measurement difference is constructed. By comprehensively analyzing the stability of static data and the real-time performance of dynamic data, the algorithm effectively extracts the key features caused by wrong wiring, and realizes the accurate identification of wrong wiring problems. The experimental results show that the algorithm has significant advantages in improving the accuracy of reactive power measurement and timely detecting misconnection problems, which provides strong support for the metering management of the power industry and the development of smart grid.

articleTitle: Multi-objective optimization design of flat-wire permanent magnet synchronous motor based on IWOA-KELM
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of large computational volume and low efficiency of motor finite element optimization. In this paper, a multi-objective optimization design method for flatwire permanent magnet synchronous motor combining IWOA-KELM agent model and genetic algorithm is proposed to optimize the performance of the motor. Firstly, according to the actual engineering experience, the motor structural parameters that have a greater impact on the optimization objective are selected as the optimization variables, secondly, the sample data are obtained through optimal Latin hypercubic sampling and finite element simulation, and three kinds of agent models of the optimization objective are established for the comparison of the fitting accuracy, and then the IWOA-KELM agent model that has the best fitting accuracy is selected for the multi-objective optimization with NSGA-II algorithm. Finally, the optimized results are compared with the simulation calculation results to verify the effectiveness and accuracy of the method in the field of motor optimization and design.

articleTitle: Fast calculation method of adaptive weights for water and steam physical properties based on neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The thermophysical property calculation module in the thermohydraulic safety analysis program of nuclear power plants greatly affects the calculation speed and accuracy of working conditions. Therefore, efficient algorithms for thermophysical properties are one of the key technologies for nuclear power software autonomy. To ensure the calculation accuracy of thermal hydraulic analysis software and improve the efficiency of physical property calculation, this study is based on the generalized regression neural network learning method and the multivariate interpolation method for efficient calculation of physical properties. We take the calculation of water and steam as an example. First, to improve the physical property form for the interpolation method, the neighborhood parameter memory algorithm is introduced for the interpolation calculation of largevolume data to simplify the calculation process. Then physical property parameters in the physical property database REFPROP get the accurate interpolation weights and establish the sampling scheme to generate the data set, and the interpolation calculation method is corrected by the predicted value of weight correction coefficients obtained by the training of the generalized regression neural network. After completing program development, we evaluate program performance by conducting a comparison of computational accuracy and efficiency. The research results show that improving the table and introducing the neighborhood memory algorithm can improve the efficiency of interpolation calculation, and the adaptive weight assignment module trained by coupled neural networks can effectively improve the accuracy of traditional interpolation calculation.

articleTitle: Load Optimization Control Method for Multiple Open Rack Vaporizers in Liquefied Natural Gas Station
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: From the operating data of open rack vaporizer (ORV), we found that: the smaller the liquefied natural gas (LNG) flow rate, the lower the seawater heat required per unit LNG. Possible reasons: When the LNG flow rate is low, the proportion of cold naturally lost during transportation to the total cold capacity becomes larger. We can reduce the seawater heat required by ORV by increasing the number of operating ORVs. As the number of ORVs in operation increases, if the calculated seawater flow rate of a single ORV is lower than the minimum film-forming flow rate, it can only be maintained at the minimum film-forming flow rate, resulting in an ineffective increase in seawater flow rate. The lowest overall seawater heat does not necessarily lead to the lowest total seawater flow rate. This paper proposes a new method for optimizing the operation of multiple ORV vaporizers in an LNG station. First, the required seawater heat is calculated based on the LNG flow rate, and then the optimal combination with the lowest total seawater flow rate is found based on the ORV constraints and environmental protection requirements. This paper gives a case study of an LNG station with 4 ORVs operating in parallel.

articleTitle: Optimization configuration method for energy storage capacity of electric vehicles connected to distribution networks based on RIME algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In the process of optimizing the configuration of energy storage capacity for electric vehicles connected to the distribution network, it is necessary to consider a balance between economic and environmental benefits. To optimize energy storage capacity, reduce lifecycle costs, and improve energy utilization efficiency, a method based on the RIME algorithm for optimizing the configuration of energy storage capacity for electric vehicle access to distribution networks is proposed. Considering the economic benefits of electric vehicle integration into the distribution network, three optimization objective functions are selected: full life cycle cost, renewable energy power change, and tie line utilization rate. Constraints that meet the objective factors are set to achieve the optimal objective factor. A model for optimizing the energy storage capacity of electric vehicle integration into the distribution network is constructed. Using the RIME algorithm to solve the optimization configuration model for the energy storage capacity of electric vehicles connected to the distribution network, in order to obtain the optimal configuration results. The experimental results show that the proposed method has a good optimization effect on the energy storage capacity configuration of electric vehicle access to the distribution network, and can effectively improve the energy storage configuration capacity of electric vehicle access to the distribution network.

articleTitle: Assessment of distributed energy trading impacts on grid operations and additional grid integration costs
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: High penetration of rooftop solar will lead to non-negligible utility costs. However, this amount cannot be effectively mitigated through the existing price mechanism. In order to clarify the responsibilities of each entity in distributed transactions, this paper first introduced typical utility charges for distributed energy transactions at domestic and abroad, and then qualitatively evaluated the influence of distributed transactions on power system functioning at the same node. Subsequently, we calculated associated network charges on power balancing, ancillary services, and network loss according to simulation results. Based on above discussions, we concluded a basis for utilities to charge prosumers for distributed transactions at the same access point, providing a theoretical basis and suggestions for promoting distributed energy integration and market transactions.

articleTitle: Research on EMI suppression and ripple reduction of Cuk converter based on chaotic spread spectrum and soft-switching technology
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In this paper, a method that combines chaotic spread spectrum and soft-switching technology is proposed to suppress Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) noise in Cuk converters. Firstly, the basic principles of chaotic spread spectrum and soft switching technology were analyzed, and the two technologies were introduced into the Cuk converter to effectively suppress EMI noise in the converter, but the spread spectrum technology increases output voltage ripple. Then a ripple elimination circuit is designed to effectively reduce the ripple. Finally, SIMPLIS simulations confirm the method’s effectiveness. This paper demonstrates this novel approach that not only suppressed the EMI noise of Cuk converters, but also reduced the output voltage ripple.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of the Conductor Grip Based on Multibody System Dynamics
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The Conductor grip is a crucial fitting in the construction of transmission lines, particularly during the tensioning and hanging phases. This study conducts a theoretical analysis of the mechanical performance of the Conductor grip-conductor system during tensioning operations. The calculation formulas for the clamping force and pull-pressure ratio exerted by the grip jaws on the conductor are derived. A refined rigid-flexible coupling multibody system model of the grip and conductor system is established, and the performance of the grip is analyzed through simulation. Compared to theoretical calculations, the flexible characteristics of the conductor reduce the clamping force and pull-pressure ratio by $\mathbf{2 . 6 2 \%}$ under the same pulling force applied to the ring. Furthermore, the simulation experiments reveal that as the angle between the pull ring guide groove and the conductor increases, the clamping force and pull-pressure ratio decrease. These results provide scientific guidance for the design, structural optimization, and construction operations of grips.

articleTitle: Power electronic electromagnetic transient simulation method based on exponential difference
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In power electronic circuits, the high frequency operation and nonlinear characteristics of switching devices often lead to complex electromagnetic transient phenomena, which puts forward higher requirements for the accuracy and efficiency of simulation algorithms. Traditional numerical simulation methods, such as trapezoidal integration method and Euler method, are widely used, but numerical oscillation and error accumulation may occur when dealing with high-frequency dynamics. In this paper, a power electronic electromagnetic transient simulation method based on exponential difference method is adopted. This method introduces exponential difference approximation into the state equation of the circuit, and introduces a virtual resistor to overcome the problem that the inductance and capacitance components cannot be directly discretized, which can effectively improve the simulation accuracy in the response performance of the switching transient process. Through the simulation of basic circuit and typical power electronic circuit, the advantages of exponential difference method in reducing numerical error and improving simulation efficiency are verified.

articleTitle: Cost Prediction for Grid Technical Renovation Projects based on XGBoost and SMA
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Forecasting the costs of power grid technology renovation projects is instrumental in enabling power utilities to plan investments effectively, ensuring timely equipment updates to maintain the health and operation of the power grid. This paper presents an innovative cost forecasting model, SMA-XGBoost, for power grid technological renovation projects. It integrates the XGBoost algorithm with the slime mould algorithm to address the complexities of cost prediction in an evolving energy landscape. The model leverages the predictive power of XGBoost and the adaptive search capabilities of SMA to improve accuracy and reliability. The study demonstrates the model’s superior performance over existing benchmarks, offering a robust tool for strategic planning and project execution within budgetary constraints.

articleTitle: Study on the Direct Current Temperature Rise Law of Contact Wire and Supporting Cable Under Icing Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In winter, the overhead contact line (OCL) of rail transit systems is highly susceptible to icing during periods without train traffic, leading to train suspensions and passenger delays. Currently, de-icing of overhead lines is mainly performed manually, as the current-based de-icing techniques used in power systems cannot be directly applied to rail transit OCLs. Therefore, this paper analyzes the temperature rise mechanism during the OCL de-icing process and establishes a thermal balance equation for OCL de-icing. After denoising with MATLAB, curve fitting and simulation are conducted. Finally, an artificial climate chamber is used to simulate the temperature rise test during the de-icing process, and the current-temperature rise curve obtained during the OCL de-icing process is validated. The study shows that the temperature rise process of the OCL and load-bearing cable during direct current (DC) de-icing is positively correlated with DC current and negatively correlated with ice thickness and external environmental conditions. Under the same current, the temperature rise of the rail transit OCL and load-bearing cable is smaller compared to power transmission lines, and the simulated temperature rise curve strongly correlates with the experimentally derived curve. The research results provide theoretical guidance for OCL de-icing.

articleTitle: Residual life prediction of submarine cable based on health index and GM(1,1)
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the rapid development of Marine energy and communication technology, the submarine cable is an important link between the offshore platform and the land, and the accurate prediction of its health state and remaining life has become the key to ensure the safe operation of offshore engineering. Therefore, on the basis of the current submarine cable operation status assessment technology, this paper proposes a comprehensive submarine cable life prediction method by integrating the equipment health index theory and GM(1,1) gray prediction model. A three-core submarine cable HYJQF41 on an offshore oil and gas platform is used as an experimental object to verify the reliability and accuracy of the model. This method provides important decision support for the long-term operation of submarine cables, enricfies the theoretical system of submarine cable life prediction, provides technical support for the safe operation and sustainable development of Marine engineering, and contributes to the further development and utilization of Marine resources.

articleTitle: Experimental study on the inhibition effect of intermittent spraying on thermal runaway propagation of lithium-ion batteries in confined space
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The rapid development of the new energy sector has brought lithium-ion batteries (LIBs) to the forefront of energy storage and electric vehicles. However, the batteries pose significant risks due to thermal runaway (TR), which can lead to fires and explosions. This study investigates the TR propagation (TRP) characteristics of ternary battery pack in confined space and evaluates the effectiveness of water mist (WM) for cooling. We compare the cooling performance of WM under conditions with and without a top perforated board and assess the effectiveness of intermittent spray (IS) strategies with varying unit time ($t_{u}$) and duty cycle (DC). Continuous spray (CS) for 180s failed to stop TRP. Among various IS strategies, $t_{u}=15 \mathrm{~s}$ with $\mathrm{DC}=0.5$ was most effective in halting TR and minimizing battery damage. In contrast, strategies with $\mathrm{DC}=0.25$ and 0.75 were less effective. The study concludes that IS is superior to CS, with optimal cooling achieved by a $t_{u}=15 \mathrm{~s}$ and $\mathrm{DC}=0.5$ strategy. These findings highlight the importance of optimizing spray strategies for improving the safety and effectiveness of fire suppression in LIBs.

articleTitle: Virtual Power Plant Energy Scheduling Method Considering Energy Storage SOC State
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In virtual power plants containing distributed resources such as Photovoltaic Storage Charging, there are problems such as limited capacity of energy storage equipment leading to insufficient adjustable energy and unreasonable power allocation leading to internal voltage exceeding limits. To achieve balanced energy scheduling, a scheduling method considering the State of Charge (SOC) of different energy storage devices is proposed. Firstly, the state of charge of the energy storage device is considered in the droop control strategy, and a SOC model of the energy storage device is constructed; Then, based on the internal load demand of the virtual power plant, the SOC values of different energy storage devices, and the total power output demand of the virtual power plant, establish an energy scheduling objective function; Finally, set constraints to complete the energy scheduling of the virtual power plant. Simulation results have shown that the proposed method can effectively complete energy scheduling and control optimization of energy storage equipment in virtual power plants, and has good robustness.

articleTitle: A Novel Compensation Network for Resonance Conditions Independent of Coupling Coefficient with Two Outputs Modes in WPTS
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Wireless power transfer (WPT) has found extensive applications in battery charging due to its unique advantages compared to traditional wired charging. To achieve efficient charging, it is essential to maintain constant current and constant voltage in battery charging mode while keeping the input impedance at a zero-angle phase (ZPA). Furthermore, it is also crucial that resonance conditions are independent of coupling coefficient (k) in WPT. Based on this, the paper proposes a novel compensation network LCLC-S that fulfills the aforementioned requirements. Using the loop current method, the resonance conditions including $\mathrm{CC}, \mathrm{CV}$, ZPA and independent of k are analyzed using the loop current method. This compensation network achieves CC with ZPA and CV with by switching the system operating frequency while the resonance conditions are independent of k both in two outputs. Finally, a simulation platform is developed to validate the input-output characteristics of CC and CV modes for the LCLC-S topology.

articleTitle: Infrared fault detection of photovoltaic module based on improved YOLOv8n
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The current photovoltaic module defect identification means encounter difficulties in feature extraction, and the model calculation amount is too large, these two points directly affect the accuracy of photovoltaic module defect detection. In order to solve these problems, the improved algorithm based on YOLOv8n is proposed for the detection of infrared thermal imaging defects of photovoltaic modules. First, the CBAM attention mechanism was added to the original YOLOv8n nalgorithm, and the lightweight convolutional attention module was used to improve the proportion of small target features and improve the detection performance. Secondly, the SPPFCSPC module is introduced, which effectively integrates the pooling results through convolution, thereby improving the accuracy and efficiency of feature extraction. Finally, the GhostConv convolutional layer is selected to reduce the computational load to reduce the amount of model computation. The improved algorithm’s average detection accuracy on the detection of infrared images of photovoltaic modules mAP can achieve $91.4 \%$, which is $2.7 \%$ higher than the original YOLOv8n algorithm $88.7 \%$, and the convergence effect of the accuracy and recall rate is also improved compared with the original YOLOv8n algorithm model.

articleTitle: Analysis and Research of Technical Loss Reduction for Distribution Line
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Energy conservation and loss reduction are effective ways for the economic development of the power grid. Line loss management is developing towards lean direction and is receiving increasing attention. Based on the analysis of the structural characteristics of the distribution network, this article proposes technical loss reduction methods from multiple dimensions. Combined with examples of high loss lines, a mathematical model is established through simulation methods to deeply calculate and analyze the composition of various component losses and the causes of high losses. Practical and feasible loss reduction measures are proposed for the causes of high losses, which provides reference value for future loss control and reduction work of high loss lines and is of great significance for ensuring the economic operation of the power grid.

articleTitle: Transmission Method of Electric Power Communication Network Based on Physical Layer Security
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Based on the security problem in the electric power communication network, this paper studies the secure transmission method of the physical layer in an electric power communication network assisted by an intelligent reflecting surface (IRS). Considering the constraint of transmit power and the phase shift, the transmitted beam and the reflected phase shift of IRS are designed to maximize the total achievable safety rate. We combine model-free meta-reinforcement learning with the strategy gradient to solve the question of slow convergence and poor generalization. Simulation results reveal that the proposed method can achieve better performance than the convex optimization method and ordinary reinforcement learning.

articleTitle: A high-sensitivity design method for Rogowski coils on stacked PCB
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Rogowski coils made of printed circuit boards (PCB) are hard coils, with the advantages of uniform wire distribution, good parameter consistency, and small size compared with traditional Rogowski coils. Restricted by the PCB thickness fabrication process, the Rogowski coil fabricated by a single PCB board has low sensitivity due to its small thickness, and the output voltage is still very small when measuring larger currents. To improve the sensitivity of the PCB Rogowski coil and the mutual inductance coefficient between the coil and the conductor to be measured, a kind of Rogowski coil stacked with multiple PCBs of the same size is proposed. Different coil heights can be realized by stacking different numbers of PCBs, which improves the mutual inductance coefficient per unit volume of the PCB Rogowski coil. The electromagnetic parameters of the stacked PCB Rogowski coil were extracted, the circuit model was established to make theoretical calculations, and its finite element simulation model was established to make simulation analysis. Then, an experimental platform with low voltage and variable high current was built, and experiments were conducted. The experimental results show that the stacked PCB Rogowski coil performs well with high sensitivity and a large mutual inductance coefficient per unit volume.

Author Keywords: High Mutual Inductance Per Unit Volume

articleTitle: Analysis of Transient Stability in Wind Power Grid Integration Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: After a fault occurs in a wind farm, the output current of the multilevel converter is generally determined by the AC voltage control, and there is a significant transient process, which has a significant impact on the transient response of the phase-locked loop. However, in the transient synchronization stability analysis of existing wind power grid connected systems, it is assumed that the output current of the multi-level converter on the wind farm side reaches the limit value instantaneously after a fault, and the multi-level converter on the wind farm side is equivalent to a constant current source. The results of the transient synchronization stability analysis may be overly optimistic. In response to this issue, this article analyzes the transient synchronous stability of wind power grid connected systems. Firstly, a fourth-order synchronous stability model considering the dynamic AC voltage control of multi-level converters on the wind farm side is proposed. Then, using the equivalent swing equation to reveal the transient synchronization stability mechanism of the system, analyze and improve the transient synchronization stability of the system. Finally, the correctness of the theoretical analysis is verified through electromagnetic transient simulation.

articleTitle: Research on Identification of Key Influencing Factors of Transmission and Transformation Project Cost Based on DEMATEL-CRITIC Weighting Method
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the continuous growth of electricity demand and the increasing investment in power grid projects, the refined and precise management of transmission and transformation project costs has become an important task for power grid companies. This paper aims to systematically identify and quantitatively analyze the key influencing factors at multiple levels, including policy, management, and technology, of transmission and transformation project costs by introducing a combined method of DEMATEL and CRITIC weighting method. It effectively identifies factors that have a significant impact on costs and proposes corresponding countermeasures. This research provides new ideas for the lean management of transmission and transformation project costs.

articleTitle: Analysis of the transmission characteristics of voltage fluctuations in the power grid and rapid response prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The new power system exhibits the characteristic of multiple time-scale processes being mutually coupled, with voltage issues serving as a vital link to various safety and stability concerns. The importance of voltage safety and stability assessment is increasingly evident. Presently, the primary approach to voltage stability assessment is conducted through electromechanical transient simulation or electromagnetic transient simulation, which is accompanied by issues of unclear mechanisms and slow efficiency. There is a lack of systematic research on the mechanisms of overvoltage generation and propagation in the power grid, as well as a deficiency in fast assessment methods for voltage safety issues. This paper proposes an analytical expression for the voltage fluctuation propagation process, identifies indicators for evaluating the propagation capacity of voltage fluctuations in the power grid, and presents a rapid prediction and assessment method for voltage safety issues.

articleTitle: Development of High and Low Temperature Testing System for Solenoid Valves
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The aviation solenoid valve, as a vital component in the aircraft fluid control system, has a direct impact on the system’s overall performance. In accordance with the requirements of the project partners, a high and low-temperature performance testing system for aviation fuel solenoid valves has been designed. Initially, the hydraulic system was engineered based on the specific testing requirements of the solenoid valve. Subsequently, the utilization of Laboratory Virtual Instrument Engineering Workbench (LabVIEW) and Programmable Logic Controller (PLC) facilitated the control of the system, enabling it to meet the testing conditions of high and low temperatures, as well as low atmospheric pressure. Finally, the fuel solenoid valve underwent static flow tests and step response tests on the test bench, successfully meeting the demands of the partners.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a 4-20 mA Digital Current Output Interface Using Domestically Manufactured Components
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In response to the urgent need for domestic nuclear reactor instrumentation and control (I&C) systems, this study employs the NSA2860 chip, NSi8141 digital isolator, and GD32F450 microcontroller, all manufactured domestically, to design the circuit and drive of a 4-20 mA output interface provided with digital isolation. The current outputs are experimentally verified for precision. The results show that the digital current output interface is capable of high-precision digit-current conversion. From 1.845 mA to 23.8337 mA, the maximum relative error is only 0.0493%, fully satisfying the precision required for $4-\mathrm{2 0 ~ m A}$ current output interfaces in reactor I&C systems.

articleTitle: Optimisation of Virtual Inertia Control and Parameter Stability Analysis of PMSG-Based Wind Turbine
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Currently, high power permanent magnet synchronous generator (PMSG) wind turbines and even renewable energy generation systems are connected to the AC bus through a power converter, and the turbines need to pass through a step-up transformer as well as a very long transmission line in order to deliver the energy to the grid. The long transmission lines make the grid impedance larger and the grid characteristics weaker. Virtual inertia control is analogous to traditional thermal power units in that the virtual inertia embedded in the unit is added to the grid system, which is widely used because of its excellent performance in dealing with frequency support problems under weak grid characteristics. Conventional virtual inertia control involves adding frequency variations to the power command to simulate the characteristics of a synchronous generator. However, in traditional wind turbines, the power command has a large delay because it needs to be sent through the main control system. Based on the traditional virtual inertia control, this paper proposes the virtual inertia optimization control by superimposing the additional command of power regulation on the current loop command to speed up the system inertia response and optimize the frequency support characteristics. Then the influence of relevant control parameters on inertia response speed and frequency stability is analyzed in combination with control system theory. Finally, the simulation model is built on the MATLAB/Simulink to verify the support ability and stability analysis conclusion of the optimal control strategy for power grid frequency.

articleTitle: Research on Patent Analysis of New Energy Battery Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: New energy battery electric vehicles have attracted a lot of attention in recent years, and in the context of the global implementation of sustainable development and energy saving and emission reduction, new energy battery electric vehicles are the trend of the world and the people. The main content of this paper is to analysis the patent situation of new energy battery electric vehicles in the world and China, and the main method is to use Incopat patent database to analysis the new energy battery electric vehicles in terms of geographic ranking, patent disclosure trend, subject clustering, applicant type and ranking. From the results of the analysis, we can see that: new energy battery electric vehicles have a broader market and more research in China. In the subject matter clustering of PCT applications, the largest number of clusters are power exchange systems and charging systems, reflecting that they are the focus and hotspot of patent inventions in the field of new energy battery electric vehicles, and China continues to lead in the number of applications filed in power exchange systems and charging systems, further reflecting its leading position in the new energy battery electric vehicle sector. In addition, in the category of patent applicants, more than 75% of the applicants are enterprises, followed by schools, and scientific research institutions and organizations occupy a small portion, so enterprises are the pioneering force and the main force in the future development of new energy battery electric vehicles. Therefore, in the future, China should continue to pay attention to the development of outstanding enterprises in the field of new energy battery electric vehicles, and introduce relevant policies to support the development of their scientific and technological innovation, and shine in the key areas. At the same time, all sectors of society should improve their knowledge and understanding of new energy battery electric vehicles, correctly understand their advantages and disadvantages, and actively provide feedback and suggestions to help the prosperous development of new energy battery electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Consideration of risk variations in decision-making for large users participating in medium- and long-term market transactions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the proposal of the Carbon Peak and Neutrality Goals, the coupling between the electricity market and the carbon market has been further strengthened. Formulating strategies for large users to participate in electricity and carbon market transactions while considering risk preferences is beneficial for improving user transaction benefits. The paper proposes a decision-making model considering risk variations for large users participating in both the carbon market and the long-term electricity market. Unlike other studies, in formulating trading plans, we utilize a rolling model to re-predict the original risk coefficient based on market changes. The aim is to enhance the purchasing benefits for large users while reducing the risks associated with electricity and carbon procurement.

articleTitle: Harmonic Compensation Control Srategy for Multilevel Active Power Filters Based on Silicon Carbide Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Harmonic pollution caused by nonlinear loads is seriously affecting the power quality and the safety of electricity consumption. In order to solve the problems of lower harmonic compensation accuracy, response speed and power density in existing active power filters (APF), firstly, a modular multilevel APF topology based on silicon carbide (SiC) metal oxide semiconductor field effect transistor (MOSFET) semiconductor devices was proposed. Secondly, an improved adaptive filtering detection algorithm based on adaptive noise cancellation (ANCT) and least mean square (LMS) was adopted, the weight of the step size was updated to achieve fast and accurate harmonic detection. Based on a double closed-loop structure, a current tracking controller was constructed. The current loop is improved by adopting the principles of proportional integral (PI) control and repetitive control, and a composite current tracking compensation method is designed, which improves the effect of current tracking compensation. Finally, a simulation model was built to validate the proposed strategy, and the experimental results proved the feasibility and effectiveness of the harmonic compensation control strategy.

articleTitle: Design and research of hydraulic support self-power supply system based on hydraulic motor power generation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: At present, the underground coal mine power supply environment is very complicated, electronic equipment is constantly put into use, and the safety of coal mine power supply is becoming increasingly serious. In order to realize the lightweight power supply of low-power electrical appliances for the hydraulic bracket in the underground coal mine, and improve the underground power supply environment, a set of hydraulic bracket self-power supply system has been designed. The basic design principle of the system, the design of each module are introduced in detail and the field industrial test is carried out. Through the data analysis of the energy loss of the system, the input and output parameters of the battery, as well as the thermal runaway analysis of the battery, it is determined that the system can achieve a stable power supply to the electrical appliances; the system has a high degree of integration, strong maintainability, and provides a safety guarantee for the power supply of low-power electrical appliances of the hydraulic bracket in the underground mine.

articleTitle: PDN impedance prediction using cross-stage densely connected network based on attention augmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Traditional full-wave electromagnetic simulation is inefficient in modeling and simulating the impedance of power distribution network (PDN) for printed circuit board (PCB) with multiple layers of stacking. This paper utilizes convolutional neural networks (CNN) to model the PDN networks of different PCBs and proposes an attention-enhanced cross-stage densely connected network (CSDNet) for PDN impedance prediction. Compared to DenseNet, CSDNet improves the accuracy of PDN impedance prediction by 41.5% and speeds up training by 12.2%. This paper innovatively introduces transfer learning (TL) into PDN impedance prediction, performing transfer training on a small amount of PDN impedance data from different PCBs. Compared to direct training, the accuracy of TL is improved by $\mathbf{6 6. 7 \%}$, and the amount of labeled data required for training is reduced by 80%. Additionally, CSDNet takes 2.3 seconds on average to predict the PDN impedance of 100 sets of 6-layer stacked PCBs, which is $\mathbf{1 3 2 0}$ times faster than traditional full-wave electromagnetic simulation.

articleTitle: A Novel Random Pulse Width Modulation for PMSM Drive System Based on Unified Voltage Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The electromagnetic interference (EMI) problem caused by power electronic switching devices and pulse width modulation (PWM) affects the normal operation of the motor drive system. In this paper, a random PWM based on unified modulation is proposed for permanent magnet synchronous motor (PMSM) drive system. The theoretical basis of unified modulation and the implementation scheme of random modulation are analyzed. Finally, the effectiveness of the proposed random PWM is verified by simulation.

articleTitle: The Impact of Virtual Power Plants Participating in Peak Shaving on Distribution Network Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This research delves into the ramifications of virtual power plants’ engagement in peak load reduction strategies on the operational dynamics of distribution networks. Initially, tailored simulation frameworks were devised for diverse distributed energy resources, encompassing photovoltaic systems, energy storage mechanisms, electric vehicle charging stations, building HVAC systems, and electrode boilers. Subsequently, leveraging the aggregation capabilities of virtual power plants, an innovative operational optimization model was formulated to facilitate their effective participation in mitigating peak loads within distribution grids. The findings reveal a dual-edged sword effect: while virtual power plants significantly diminish the peak-to-valley load disparity, enhancing grid stability, they concurrently amplify voltage fluctuations at nodes and elevate line losses within the distribution network.

articleTitle: Research on the Evaluation System of Central Air Conditioning Demand Response Interaction Capability Considering Time Delay Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper addresses the evaluation of central air conditioning demand response capability, with a focus on the time delay effect. Evaluating user-side resources is crucial for predicting and adjusting electricity demand, aiding in peak shaving, and ensuring grid stability. Existing methods often overlook social factors, time delays, and confidence levels, leading to unreliable assessments. To improve accuracy and reliability, we develop an integrated evaluation index system combining social and physical indicators, using cumulative prospect confidence and prospect theory for weight calculation. Simulations confirm that the proposed method significantly enhances evaluation accuracy and reliability, optimizing demand response management in power systems.

articleTitle: Research on Parameter Optimization of Offshore Wind Power Parallel Converter Based on Virtual Synchronous Generator
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Through energy storage devices and converters, the external characteristics of synchronous generators were simulated, with inertia and damping characteristics, achieving virtual synchronous generator control. Firstly, the influence of various parameters in the virtual synchronous generator (VSG) on the system was analyzed. Secondly, a small signal model of the VSG parallel system was constructed, and the effects of changes in rotational inertia, damping, adjustment coefficient, and virtual inductance parameters on the parallel system were analyzed through the model. Finally, a simulation model was built using MATLAB/Simulink to verify the correctness of the theoretical analysis.

articleTitle: Optimized Configuration of Energy Storage in Solar Thermal Power Station Considering Solar Multiple
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: At present, energy shortage and environmental pollution have become the number one problem restricting the development. Therefore, the new energy power generation represented by solar energy has been developed rapidly. However, due to the excessive dependence on weather conditions for photovoltaic power generation, its output causes randomness and uncertainty. Compared with photovoltaic power generation, solar thermal power generation, as an emerging power generation technology, can flexibly adjust its output because of its large capacity heat storage system. The construction of photovoltaic thermal power stations near photovoltaic power stations to form photovoltaic-thermal power generation will become a common form of energy development. In order to use the output of the photothermal power station to alleviate the uncertainty of photovoltaic output, it is necessary to rationally configure the heat storage capacity of the photothermal power station in the combined power generation system, and use the output of the photothermal power station to alleviate the uncertainty of photovoltaic output. According to the uncertainty of photovoltaic forecast output and load prediction, this paper adopts scenario analysis method; establish the two-stage optimal configuration model of heat storage capacity of photothermal power station to further calculate the optimal heat storage capacity in each period. Through the example analysis, the proposed method can maximize the photovoltaic power supply and improve the operation efficiency of the whole system.

articleTitle: Simulation and Experiment of Metal Particle Motion Behavior in SF6 Gas under AC Superimposed Impulse Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Gas insulated switchgear (GIS) is widely used in power grids, but equipment failures caused by various defects have been threatening the safe and reliable operation of GIS. There have been many insulation failures caused by metal particles in the engineering site. Under the action of strong electric field, metal particles move freely in GIS and show various motion behaviors, and induce field intensity distortion and partial discharge in different motion states, which seriously threatens the operation safety of GIS. In this paper, the motion trajectory model of free metal particles established based on the finite element method and the AC superimposed impulse voltage partial discharge test platform were built to study the partial discharge and motion behavior of metal particles under AC superimposed impulse voltage in SF<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</inf> gas. The force and partial discharge results of the particles were analyzed, and the small amplitude random jumping behavior of metal particles was investigated experimentally. And the randomness of motion behavior is analyzed.

articleTitle: Branch Insulation Detection System With Leakage Current Sensors Based on Power/Signal Dual Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The leakage current sensing detection method has a wide range of application in the branch insulation detection in new energy scenarios to ensure the safe and stable operation. However, the existing branch detection system has certain deficiencies in terms of installation and maintenance convenience, system cost and complexity, and alignment convenience. In this paper, a leakage sensing branch circuit insulation detection system based on power/signal dual modulation is proposed, which realizes local detection and alarm through the system structure of host-slaveconcentrator with powerline communication. The transmission between the host and the concentrator is realized bya flyback converter in the host and a buck converter in the concentrator, whose ripple voltage and ripple current are used as the carrier in powerline. It simplifies the system alignment and reduces the cost of the communicationsystem compared with the traditional bus communication method. This communication system can realize full-duplex communication at 20 kbps in simulation, and the effectiveness of the system is verified.

articleTitle: Visualization of the development of micro piezoelectric self-generating system
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Power generation by cutting the magnetic induction line is a new type of self-generating technology which is widely used in self-power generation modules, which can be applied to wireless switches, wireless doorbells, bath controller remote controllers, access control systems and other fields. Self-generating circuit, environmental protection and energy conservation, no wiring process, convenient and simple. The main technical principle is that the self-generating device converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by cutting the magnetic line of force. This paper provides a visual design method. This method combines simulation technology with practical application requirements to solve the confusion of disorderly exploration of current self-generating device design and the problem that the power utilization of power generation circuit design cannot be optimized. In this paper, the design concept of “ what you see is what you get “ (WYSIWYG) is visualized from end to end, which solves the maximization of power generation efficiency of self-generating development equipment, and makes the development equipment the most economical and flexible to meet the needs of different application scenarios. This method has been implemented in enterprise projects and improved the design efficiency of enterprise products.

articleTitle: Design of low power consumption icing monitoring system for transmission lines
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In China, the icing monitoring of transmission lines in remote areas depends on the image recognition of video equipment, which leads to the problem of high power consumption of icing monitoring system. In this paper, the core of ice-coating triggering and wakefulness mechanism is applied, the low-power long-distance communication technology of LoRa is introduced. The high-precision micro-weather sensor data is used as the triggering source, wake up the dormant video device into working mode to complete the accurate identification of ice thickness. Then, upload the monitoring results to the cloud platform, in order to carry out subsequent anti-ice measures. Based on the trigger mechanism, the ice-covering monitoring system does not need the camera to be in working mode all the time, which can greatly reduce the power consumption of data transmission, data processing, energy supply and so on. The experimental results show that the daily average power consumption of the system is significantly lower than that of the traditional monitoring and setting system under the low power consumption mode, it is proved to be effective in reducing energy consumption and cost.

articleTitle: A Simulation Study on Ventilation and Drainage of Current Sensor Casing Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In this paper, a ventilation and drainage shell structure for power application current sensors is designed, and the internal design and air guide design are carried out through simulation iteration to achieve high efficiency ventilation and drainage. By using the two-stage simulation method to simulate the inlet wind velocity and the ventilation and humidity exhaust in the cavity respectively, the calculation cost of the simulation was effectively reduced; by using the calculus method to calculate the dehumidification via steady simulation rather than transit simulation, the computational amount and convergence difficulty of the simulation are significantly reduced. Finally, the performance of this casing structure design is evaluated according to the meteorological characteristics of Guangzhou.

articleTitle: SOC estimation of battery systems for ultra-large capacity battery-powered ships under multiple constraints
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the increasingly stringent environmental regulations and the increasing progress of energy storage power electronics technology, battery power, as one of the green ship power technologies, has become a current research hotspot. The ultra-large capacity battery system generally has the disadvantages of short cycle life, easy reduction of capacity influenced by external factors and high replacement cost. In order to make better use of battery energy, it is necessary to accurately estimate the size of the battery pack’s charge state and restrict it to prevent overcharge and overdischarge. Comparing the adaptive untracked Kalman filter algorithm with the extended Kalman filter algorithm to estimate the SOC reliability and error size of the energy storage element, it is proved that the SOC estimation results obtained by the adaptive Kalman filter algorithm are more reliable, which lays a foundation for the DC bus voltage stability control strategy.

articleTitle: Intelligent Operation and Maintenance Architecture and Key Technologies for Power Grid Dispatch and Control Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In response to the increased complexity and enhanced concealment of faults arising from the evolution of power grid dispatch and control system architectures, which pose significant challenges to maintenance, this paper proposes an intelligent operation and maintenance solution specifically tailored for power grid dispatch and control system. The primary goal is to elevate the quality of operation maintenance for power grid dispatch and control system and alleviate the workload associated with maintenance activities. This paper elaborates on the design of the software, hardware and data flow architecture, as well as key technologies including unified modeling, system risk early warning, fault diagnosis and localization, and fault-assistance handling. These elements collectively aim to lay the theoretical groundwork and offer technological support for establishing a smart, efficient operations and management system for power grid dispatch and control system.

Author Keywords: power grid dispatch and control system

articleTitle: Research on Multi Scale Grid New Energy Consumption Optimization Model Based on Energy Synergy
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the rapid development of social economy, the contradiction between energy problems and environmental problems has become increasingly prominent. In this paper for high proportion of new energy grid continuously important influence on the safe operation of power grid stability, based on energy collaborative grid given optimization model of new energy given, considering the traditional thermal power, wind power, photovoltaic, energy storage, power grid energy structure, combined with a variety of power grid boundary constraints, establish a grid new energy given optimal as the goal, energy synergy under multi-scale grid new energy given optimization model, and use the CPLEX solution analysis. This paper uses the simulation analysis of historical power grid data to verify that the proposed model can reflect the actual operation of the power grid, realize the maximum consumption of new energy under energy coordination, and reduce the wind and light abandonment rate of new energy. At the same time, this paper compares and analyzes the influence of the flexible transformation of thermal power units and the long-term installed capacity of new energy on the consumption rate of new energy, which can be seen that the proposed model can provide technical support for the operation and management of the power grid.

articleTitle: Research on an Anti direct current Transformer Detection Device
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the diversification of electrical equipment, more and more DC (direct current) components are added to AC (alternating current) metering circuits, resulting in traditional AC transformers being unable to correctly capture DC signals and causing inaccurate electricity metering. To solve this problem, an anti DC transformer was designed, and a detection device was developed in this paper to meet the calibration requirements of anti DC transformers. The device consists of an anti DC transformer calibrator, a digital synthesized wave AC/DC high current source, an AC/DC current ratio standard, a calibration platform, a programmable load box, and corresponding calibration software. Compared to traditional transformer calibration devices, this article has added calibration functions for power frequency ratio errors with DC components, ratio errors under sinusoidal half wave currents, phase errors, as well as ratio errors and phase errors of harmonic currents in the design. Practical application has shown that the device is stable and reliable, with fast verification speed, wide testing range, and accurate testing data.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Impact of Power Grid Structure and Equipment Types on Distribution Losses
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The structure of the power grid and the type of equipment are important components of the distribution network, which will affect the distribution of power flow and network losses. Based on the above factors, this article constructs a power grid model for simulation analysis. The simulation results show that selecting appropriate medium voltage line switch positions, power supply radii, branch stages, wire types, and substation transformer types can effectively reduce network losses in the distribution network and promote energy-saving and economic operation of the distribution network.

articleTitle: Numerical study on high-pressure hydrogen induced self-ignition under various tube cross-section geometry and burst disk open mode
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Hydrogen is a promising alternative fuel to traditional fossil fuels due to its high energy density and clean combustion. However, handling and storage of high-pressure hydrogen pose significant safety risks, primarily due to its propensity for self-ignition upon sudden release. This study numerically investigates the impact of tube cross-section geometries and burst disk opening modes on high-pressure hydrogen-induced self-ignition. Employing the Large Eddy Simulation (LES) model with the Eddy Dissipation Concept (EDC) for combustion and a detailed 21-step chemical reaction mechanism for hydrogen and air, the study analyzes the shock wave propagation, flow structures, and temperature under various configurations. Results indicate that cross-section geometries and burst disk opening modes significantly influence the self-ignition phenomenon, with instantaneous openings exhibiting higher self-ignition tendencies, and non-circular cross-sections exhibiting more complex shock wave patterns. The findings provide insights for optimizing designs to mitigate ignition risks in hydrogen storage and transportation systems.

articleTitle: Novel Graph-based Transient Analysis Method for Bulk Power System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: As the modern power system is undergoing a major transition to a self-aware and self-autonomous system to address the more and more complex system dynamics and operation conditions, the transient analysis of power system is also facing challenges to fast response to transient disturbances and take corresponding preventive and control measures to increase system security. However, traditional transient analysis methods rely on time-domain simulations are very time consuming. This paper proposed a graph computing based power system transient analysis approach to achieve efficient and accurate solution for power system stability analysis. To overcome the data management challenges, a spatiotemporal graph model is constructed for efficient data management in power system transient analysis. Then, a graph computing based transient analysis method is proposed to leverage the parallel computing power to speed up the computational process. The case study shows that the proposed graph computing based parallel computing approach can achieve 5.16 times speed improvement rate over the traditional serial computing method.

articleTitle: Research on Resource Aggregation Application of Virtual Power Plants in the Grid Auxiliary Service Market
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Virtual power plants, as an emerging power system technology, have the core value of aggregating dispersed energy resources through modem information technology to form a virtual entity that can participate in electricity market activities. This article will analyze and explore the application of distributed resource aggregation technology in the participation of virtual power plants in grid auxiliary services, in order to help the construction of economic dispatch in virtual power plants and promote further innovative development of resource aggregation technology.

articleTitle: Nonlinear Control of Linear Sliders Using Cascade Control Based on Operator Theory
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Recently, The demand for smart devices, including smartphones, has been rapidly expanding, along with the development of higher performance devices, and this trend is expected to continue in the future. For the manufacture of these devices, miniaturization of semiconductor devices and improvement of productivity are required. Precise control of semiconductor lithography equipments is critical for the manufacture of ultra small semiconductor devices. Semiconductor lithography equipments use linear motor stages, and this paper describes a high precision perfect tracking control of these stages. Perfect tracking control is a control method that ensures the system constantly follows a command value, even as it changes over time, and requires a high level of accuracy. But the dynamic characteristics of linear motors are strictly nonlinear, which requires nonlinear control for precise control. Therefore, operator theory, which compensates for the stability of nonlinear control systems, is used to control the position of stage. In this paper, we propose a new control system design method using cascade control based on operator theory to achieve model reduction. Experimental results show that the proposed method improves the tracking performance compared with previous studies.

articleTitle: Research and application of automatic generation of interval configuration diagram based on secondary circuit model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: To address the issues of large workload, low efficiency, high error rate, and inconvenience in viewing associated with manually drawn interval configuration diagrams by design institutes, as well as to meet the interval configuration needs in the design and operation of modern power systems, a method for automatically generating interval configuration diagrams based on a secondary circuit model is proposed. This method utilizes System Specification Description (SSD) files and Station Physical Circuit Description (SPD) files, establishes the association between device windings and equipment, automatically determines circuit types based on circuit characteristics, and adopts different search logics for CT and PT to filter circuits and establish hierarchical placement principles for interval types. This achieves automated processing for generating interval configuration diagrams based on the secondary circuit model, ensuring the correctness and standardization of the diagrams.
