Additionally, the paper explores advanced carbon monitoring approaches for power systems with concurrent multiple energy sources, developing a comprehensive framework for collaborative electric-carbon monitoring that encompasses data collection, processing, analysis, and storage. This framework effectively spans various temporal and spatial scales, enabling precise and dynamic monitoring of power carbon emissions, thereby strongly supporting the power industry’s transition to a low-carbon future.

articleTitle: Enhancing Fault Prediction of Ultra-High Voltage Transformers Based on a Multi-Model Adaptive Weighting Ensemble Approach for Dissolved Gas Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Ultra-high voltage (UHV) transformers are critical components in power systems, where their operational reliability is essential for ensuring grid stability. Dissolved Gas Analysis (DGA) is a widely used technique for the early detection of transformer faults. However, traditional DGA-based prediction methods often struggle with the complexities and dynamics of operational environments. This study introduces a novel fault prediction approach utilizing a multi-model adaptive weighting ensemble. This ensemble integrates Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, multivariate grey prediction models, exponential smoothing, and big data analytics to cater to the specific demands of various fault types. By dynamically adjusting the weights of each model, the proposed ensemble enhances both prediction accuracy and robustness. Experimental results demonstrate that this method significantly improves fault prediction precision across diverse fault scenarios, offering a valuable tool for the maintenance and reliability of UHV transformers.

articleTitle: Impact of Transformer Flux Saturation on Tranisent Overvoltage Analysis of Sending-End Power Grid with Wind Farms
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper analyzes the impact of transformer saturation on sending-end power system transient overvoltage caused by the high-voltage direct current (HVDC) transmission system commutation failure. It illustrats that transformers absorbs reactive power when entering the saturation state, which will affect overvoltage assesment and control of sending-end power grdi. First, it analyzes the transformer magnetic saturation impact on transient overvoltage results of sending-end power grid. Second, it introduces the electromagnetic transient simulation model of the transformer with magnetic saturation. Then, it demonstrates that the saturated transformer will absorb reactive power when overvoltage occurs, and derives the relationship between the reactive power absorption and the overvoltage. Next, a correction method for overvoltage simulation results that do not consider transformer saturation is proposed. Finally, the correctness and feasibility of the theory analyses and correction method proposed in this paper are verified through two different test systems with different scales.

articleTitle: Research on the Evaluation of the Construction Process and Investment Demand Calculation Technology for New Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Under the background of the new power system, there have been significant changes in the forms of the grid side, power source side, and load side. Clarifying the construction process and investment structure changes of the new power system from a development perspective is the key to discovering investment change patterns, guiding efficient investment of funds, and discovering and improving the investment efficiency of power grid infrastructure. This article first constructs a new power system evaluation index system and a new power system construction evaluation method from four dimensions: macro policies, power structure, grid structure, and terminal demand. Secondly, based on the higher demand for system regulation capability in the development stage of the power grid, as well as the urgent need to further improve power supply reliability, transaction flexibility, and diversity of power supply forms, an analysis of the investment direction of the power grid is conducted. Then, considering the changes in the demand for power grid investment functions, a power grid investment demand system that adapts to the new power system is constructed, including building a power grid investment demand calculation model based on project requirements at the project level, coordinating execution and planning, and considering factors such as load growth to construct a power grid investment demand calculation model that takes into account multiple factors. The power grid investment demand is calculated by combining bottom-up and top-down approaches. Finally, taking X province as an example, empirical calculations are conducted to verify the usability of the model.

articleTitle: Study of fast startup criterion for AC microgrid faults based on Hankel matrix singular value decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: New energy generation technologies such as photovoltaic and wind turbines are frequently integrated into AC microgrids as distributed power sources. This integration presents new challenges for fault detection and other aspects of microgrid operation. This study focuses on the rapid detection of faults in AC microgrids. The performance benefits of utilizing the wavelet algorithm and Hankel matrix singular value decomposition for detecting signal anomalies are examined. A fault start determination method based on Hankel matrix singular value decomposition is proposed to address the detection delay issue associated with conventional fault start determination methods. This approach enables the precise identification of the fault start moment.

articleTitle: New Energy GCI Impedance Identification Based on PSO-XGBoost Model
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The large-scale grid connection of new energy units has brought many adverse effects on system stability, which has a negative impact on the grid connected inverter of new energy units, mechanism analysis and impedance characteristic identification of grid-connected inverter (GCI) are one of the key prerequisites for effectively addressing the above issues. Therefore, this paper proposes a new energy GCI impedance identification method based on the PSO-XGBoost model. The impedance characteristics of GCI were scanned using RT-LAB hardware-in-the-loop testing technique combined with small disturbance method to obtain the actual impedance values required for model validation. The effectiveness and superiority comparison experiments have shown that the PSO-XGBoost model has higher GCI impedance identification accuracy compared to other models.

articleTitle: Cooperative energy management of renewable agricultural power system integrating demand response and multi-energy hub
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper presents an economical energy framework for rural electrification through agricultural microgrids. It delves into the synergistic energy management, harnessing demand response and a multi-energy hub to satisfy the multifaceted energy requirements of agriculture. With an emphasis on mitigating risks, the study introduces metrics for Expected Power Not Served (EPNS) and Expected Power Curtailment (EPC), providing a quantitative assessment of wind power variability. Advancing this, a probabilistic day-ahead operational model is formulated to streamline the interplay between a wind-integrated pumped storage system and agricultural water management. The overarching goal is operational cost minimization coupled with load peak mitigation, leveraging the pumped storage system’s potential. The model’s efficacy is underscored by its ability to optimize energy distribution, curtail costs, and even out the demand curve, as evidenced by simulations surpassing current methodologies.

articleTitle: Research on blockchain architecture for terminal side business applications of distributed iot
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: As the most important energy exchange hub of the new power system, the distribution network is of great significance for supporting clean energy production and electricity substitution for energy consumption. The blockchain-based distribution network supports distributed power generation and has the function of good interaction with the main network and users, adapting to the construction and development of a strong intelligent distribution network. The focus of this article is on the authenticity and security requirements of data on the intelligent terminal side of the distributed Internet of Things system. A blockchain and chip software and hardware collaborative technology framework are designed for the terminal side business, and an embedded edge intelligent framework and efficient parallel blockchain hardware acceleration architecture are designed. Ultimately, high-performance, highly trusted, and highly secure underlying technology support is provided for blockchain end-side applications, creating a trustworthy software and hardware integrated environment, hence improving the operational efficiency of the underlying blockchain platform, reducing blockchain latency, and supporting adaptation to multiple types of blockchain basic service platforms.

articleTitle: A Power Fluctuation Smoothing Method for Distribution Networks considering Flexible Loads Hierarchical Dispatch
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: As the installation capacity of distributed renewable energy sources has been growing rapidly in recent years, it significantly increases the difficulties in smoothing power fluctuation for distribution networks due to the intermittence and fluctuation of renewable energy. Although tapping the dispatch potential of flexible loads participating in the power regulation in distribution networks is an effective measure to solve the problem, massive number and small individual capacity of flexible loads have made it difficult to implement in a collaborative way. In this paper, based on smoothing power fluctuation scenario, the massive dispersed heterogeneous flexible loads are clustered at first to realize the decision variables degradation and resources hierarchical dispatch. Based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) algorithm, a smoothing power fluctuation control method is then proposed considering the hierarchical dispatch of flexible loads with economic optimization as the objective and power fluctuation rate as the coupling constraint for distribution networks. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method can effectively reduce the dimensionality of the flexible load variables and the difficulty of solving the problem, and improves the interaction capability between sources and loads and flexible controllability of distribution networks.

articleTitle: Unit Commitment in a System Integrated with Adiabatic Compressed Air Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Adiabatic compressed air energy storage (A-CAES) has grown rapidly in China recently. The paper investigates the unit commitment (UC) problem for a hybrid system containing thermal plants and an A-CAES plant. The time-varying charging characteristics of A-CAES are analyzed and then modeled with a pressure-based state of charge (SOC). The hybrid system’s UC model is constructed and finally reformulated in a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) way. A modified IEEE-30 bus system is used to verify the model’s effectiveness. Numerical results demonstrate that integrating A-CAES could reduce the number of unit startups and shutdowns and lower the system operating costs. Finally, the effect of the initial state of A-CAES on the UC results is studied.

articleTitle: Preliminary exploration of the application of digitalization of power standards in the power industry
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In the context of the digital transformation of the new power system, the digitalization of power standard services and applications is an important direction for the digital transformation of the power system. To this end, this article first reviews the development of standard digitization at home and abroad and the application of standard digitization in some industries. It discusses the key technologies of digitization of power standards, proposes a distribution transformer detection scheme based on a digitization knowledge graph of power standards, analyzes the challenges faced by digitization of power standards, and provides suggestions for researching digital application of power standards. Finally, a summary of the digital application of power standards is made.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a High-Frequency Protection Scheme for DC Microgrid Line Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: As an effective access method for renewable energy, the application scenarios of Direct Current (Hereinafter referred to as DC) microgrids are gradually increasing. However, in comparison with the traditional Alternating Current (Hereinafter referred to as AC) power system, the DC system fault current rises rapidly and with a significant amplitude, which results in considerable mechanical stress and overheating on the power lines and equipment. Consequently, the rapid fault location and removal have become the pivotal issues of DC systems that require urgent resolution. In this paper, we This paper proposes a high-frequency protection system for DC microgrid lines. The system extracts the high-frequency component of the fault by fast Fourier transformation (FFT) when the fault occurs and uses this component to judge whether it meets the action conditions of each segment protection. When the action conditions are met, the protection I and II sections cooperate with each other to selectively isolate the fault from the line, thus ensuring the safety of DC microgrid operation. During the fault, the equivalent impedance of the high-frequency components generated by the DC/DC converters on both sides of the line is minimal, forming an evident fault boundary within the fault line. This boundary can be utilized to rapidly ascertain the fault location. This paper is based on the PSCAD/EMTDC 4 simulation platform for model construction, design experiments, and simulation verification. This paper presents a simulation study of inter-pole short-circuit faults and high-frequency protection schemes for flexible DC microgrids. The performance of the protection system in the event of an inter-pole short-circuit at different locations along DC lines is evaluated. The results demonstrate that the high-frequency overcurrent protection can satisfy the selectivity, reliability, sensitivity, and rapid response requirements of DC microgrid protection.

articleTitle: Enhancing power security: Attack detection based on cost-sensitive SVM and attention mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In order to proactively block attack paths and secure the power monitoring host, a cost-sensitive SVM-based method for detecting attacks on power monitoring hosts is proposed. This method aims to accurately identify network and user attacks. A model for detecting power monitoring host attack behavior using a cost-sensitive SVM approach is developed. The data on power monitoring host attack behavior, encompassing both user and network attack behaviors, is gathered, and the data characteristics are used to create training samples for the model. By resolving the misclassification cost of each sample using a dynamic cost function based on class membership, the cost-sensitive SVM classifier is trained to detect attacks. The classifier then processes the data for classification and other operations to output the detected instances of attack behavior on the power monitoring host. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach can effectively reduce the overall misclassification cost of power monitoring host attacks. It can detect network attacks and user attacks by analyzing abnormal network traffic and user keystrokes, as well as accurately identify other types of attacks on power monitoring hosts. This method enhances the detection capabilities of power monitoring host attacks, thereby ensuring the security of power systems.

articleTitle: Research on the Calculation Method of Openable Capacity of Distributed Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper summarizes the current status of research on calculation methods for the openable capacity of distributed photovoltaic (PV) systems, and discusses the specific content and application of the six main calculation methods. The method based on voltage deviation opportunity constraints is planned by building a probabilistic tidal current calculation model for distribution networks, combining the correlation of PV output and opportunity constraints. The integrated demand response model is by constructing a steady state model of the integrated electric-thermal energy system, combined with price-based, incentive-based and elastic thermal load response. Active management and demand-side management methods use a two-stage robust optimization model to improve PV access capacity under “source-load” uncertainty by combining multiple active management measures. Hybrid particle swarm algorithms are used to accurately calculate capacity by combining constraints such as voltage deviation and line current carrying capacity. The method of considering reasonable light abandonment is to allow a certain percentage of PV power to be abandoned, combined with control means such as transformer tap regulation; the method based on harmonic constraints is to analyze the harmonic characteristics generated by PV inverters, and consider voltage, capacity and harmonic constraints comprehensively. Each of these methods has its own characteristics, and together they promote the refinement and intelligent development of the calculation of the openable capacity of distributed PV systems.

articleTitle: Research and Application of the Energy Science and Technology Intelligence Brain Integrating Large Model Technology and Patent Big Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Purpose/Significance] In the context of global carbon peak and carbon neutrality, China’s new energy industry has experienced rapid development, with its installed capacity consistently ranking first worldwide. To further strengthen and optimize this industry, there is an urgent need for technological empowerment to create a new quality of productivity and maintain competitive advantages. [Method/Process] This paper proposes an integration concept based on “energy technology + intelligence methods + digital intelligence technology”, incorporating advanced digital intelligence technology of large language models, and an energy technology analysis method with patent big data analysis as the starting point. [Results/Conclusion] D developed and established an energy central enterprise technology intelligence system that encompasses core functions such as industrial technology, enterprise talent, and industry trends. Based on this system, we have conducted an analysis study on cadmium telluride solar technology. Furthermore, the system has already provided practical support for the technological innovation work of national ministries, energy central enterprises, and others, which is of great significance for enhancing the development of China’s energy technology.

articleTitle: Short-term Wind Energy Forecasting Using Attention-based Encoder Decoder GRU Framework
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With growing penetration of renewable energy in power grids, the significance of accurate forecasting for renewable energy such as wind power is increasing. However, wind power exhibits stochastic temporal variations, which makes the forecasting task as a challenge. To alleviate this problem, this paper proposes an attention-based encoder decoder neural network. The overcome the long sequence dependencies vanishing problem in existing recurrent neural network, the attention mechanism is introduced to dynamically model the relations among features in global context. The variant of long-short term memory (LSTM) neural network, gated recurrent unit, is introduced to act as the encoder and decoder. To improve model’s robustness and stability in long sequence forecasting, teacher forcing mechanism is adopted in training process. Further, multiple features including time-period, temperature and wind speed are delicately processed. A real-world wind farm power generation dataset is used to verify the performance of proposed model. Compared with other benchmark models. The numerical results demonstrate that the proposed model outperforms other benchmarks and enables to accurately forecast wind power generation in different time scale.

articleTitle: Study on Distributed Photovoltaic Penetration Rate of Local Area Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the increasing penetration rate of distributed photovoltaic, the safety and stability of distribution networks faces challenges. This paper investigates the impact of distributed power penetration on local distribution networks and establishes relevant assessment indicators. The results show that a high percentage of distributed PV access to the distribution network may affect the distribution network automation and relay protection actions, leading to low power quality and the expansion of the scope of grid accidents. In addition, the stochastic and fluctuating nature of distributed PV may cause power back-feeding and return power to higher voltage level grids. To cope with these challenges, this paper proposes metrics such as voltage deviation, short-circuit current, power back-feeding assessment, and thermal stability assessment to comprehensively assess the impact of distributed power access on the distribution network. The reasonableness of the established metrics is verified through example analyses, and the changes in distribution network currents under different PV access scenarios are demonstrated to further confirm the impacts of distributed PV access on distribution network thermal stability, voltage deviation, and return-to-feed.

articleTitle: Step Resolution-Based Optimal Capacity Configuration of Renewable Microgrids with Shared Hybrid Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: To address the challenges of high investment cost, long payback period, and time-series capacity mismatch in selfbuilt energy storage for renewable energy microgrids, we propose an optimal allocation strategy for renewable energy park microgrids, considering shared electricity-hydrogen hybrid storage. First, an operation mechanism is proposed for PV park microgrids to participate in electricity-hydrogen hybrid storage sharing. Next, a pricing method for shared hybrid storage services is formulated based on the full life cycle cost, incorporating both throughput and capacity prices. Finally, annual capacity planning for the renewable energy park microgrid is conducted using step resolution instead of the conventional hourly resolution. The proposed method is verified to effectively reduce the annual operating cost for the microgrid and promote the consumption of renewable energy.

articleTitle: A Cellular Traffic Prediction Method with Energy Tracking Secure Federated Learning in 5G Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Predicting cellular traffic is crucial for intelligent design, resource optimization, and anomaly detection in fifth-generation (5G) and future networks, particularly in the realms of power grid management and energy distribution. Accurate traffic forecasts can enhance network performance, improve energy efficiency, and ensure the stable operation of power grids. However, traditional centralized prediction methods pose risks related to data security and privacy breaches, especially given the sensitivity of grid data. This study proposes a cellular traffic prediction method that combines federated proximal optimization aggregation algorithms with differential privacy techniques. The goal is to securely aggregate prediction model parameters across base stations while safeguarding the privacy and security of grid data. This approach allows us to provide power grid operators with accurate traffic forecasts, thereby optimizing energy distribution and demand response strategies while maintaining data privacy. We evaluated the proposed secure federated learning method using a real 5G cellular base station traffic dataset from Barcelona. The results demonstrate its advantages in terms of prediction accuracy and data privacy protection. Additionally, this study considers the environmental impact of federated learning, focusing on the trade-offs between security, accuracy, and energy consumption. By assessing the energy consumption and carbon dioxide emissions of the proposed method, this paper not only offers an energy-saving reference for distributed modeling of 5G base stations but also provides new perspectives for the green and sustainable development of power grids.

articleTitle: Study on dynamic characteristics of load torque of motor control mechanism of high voltage vacuum circuit breaker
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In this paper, based on the motion and dynamic coordination characteristics of the high-voltage vacuum circuit breaker and the motor control mechanism, the mathematical model of the insulating tie rod in the motor control mechanism is constructed in the process of breaking and closing. Secondly, the travel and pressure characteristics of the contact spring of the vacuum circuit breaker are given, and the composition of the load torque of the motor control mechanism is broken down and analyzed. At last, Adams software is used to simulate the motor turn-displacement curve and the motor load torque. Through the simulation analysis, the load torque of the drive motor is small in the Angle range of $-12^{\circ} \sim 72^{\circ}$ during the opening and closing movement. When the motor Angle is 104°, the load torque reaches the peak, which provides a theoretical basis for the future high voltage vacuum circuit breaker to consider the influence of load torque on the motor control mechanism.

articleTitle: Dispatching of Combined Heat and Power Distribution System based on Market Transactions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The broad implementation of combined heat and power (CHP) plants and energy conversion facilities is rapidly advancing energy system integration, creating both opportunities and obstacles for system operation and management. Comprehensive mathematical models and analytical techniques are essential to consider the interconnection of energy flows in multi-carrier energy systems and the strategic actions of various market participants. This paper examines the CHP distribution system from the viewpoint of market transactions. The distribution electricity market, taking into account network losses, is cleared using the nonlinear AC Optimal Power Flow (OPF) model. The power flow model is formulated as a mixed integer linear program (MILP) by polyhedral approximation of the second-order cone mode. A new optimization model which takes market clearing as a constraint to analyze the impact of consumer demand on the market is proposed. The JVPP-ADMM is proposed to improve the iteration speed of the ADMM algorithm by changing the penalty parameters and adding parallel measures. Case studies validate the efficacy of the suggested model and approach.

Author Keywords: combined heat and power distribution system

articleTitle: Research on Optimization of Virtual Power Plant Operation Mode and Profit Calculation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In order to improve the consumption level of distributed new energy, reduce the construction cost of power sources, improve energy utilization efficiency, and maximize the value of virtual power plants, a virtual power plant will be constructed with wind power suppliers, photovoltaic suppliers, energy storage suppliers, and controllable load suppliers as the main beneficiaries to participate in electricity trading. Firstly, construct an optimal operating mode model for virtual power plants that considers typical daily patterns; Secondly, the model is solved using a combination of particle swarm optimization algorithm and commercial solvers; Based on the optimal operating mode obtained through model solving, the Shapley value method is improved with risk preference, cooperation willingness, and participation level as factors, and a profit correction model is established; Finally, the feasibility and applicability of the established model and method are verified through numerical simulations and result analysis.

articleTitle: Multi-level Assessment Method for Joint Hosting Capacity of Wind Power, Photovoltaic and Electric Vehicles in Distribution Grids
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the proliferation of renewable energy and the expansion of electric vehicle (EV) scales, the instability of wind and solar power, as well as the irregular charging behaviors of EVs, have altered load characteristics, potentially negatively impacting distribution networks at various levels. Therefore, it is crucial to regularly estimate the hosting capacity of distribution networks for new energy sources to ensure safe and stable operation. This paper proposes a multi-level estimation method for the joint hosting capacity of wind power, photovoltaic (PV) systems, and EVs to comprehensively assess the hosting capacity of multi-tiered distribution networks. First, based on foundational data, comprehensive demand coefficients and simultaneous rates of wind, solar and load, are obtained under a certain confidence level. Next, the joint hosting capacity (JHC) for equipment-level, county-level, and provincial-level distribution networks is evaluated separately. Finally, the results are adjusted to achieve consistency in hosting capacities across different levels. Simulation calculations on a virtual case demonstrate that the proposed method effectively assesses the maximum hosting capacity of multi-tiered distribution networks, providing guidance for the operation of distribution networks and the development of new energy sources.

articleTitle: A Transformer-Based Load Forecasting Approach for Power Systems in Cold Regions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the seasonal fluctuations in energy demand and the growing frequency of extreme weather events in cold regions, the significance of load forecasting for power grids in these areas has become increasingly prominent. This paper proposes a Transformer-based load forecasting model specifically designed for power systems in cold regions. The effectiveness of model is validated through comparisons with Random Forest (RF), Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), and Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) utilizing actual grid data. The Transformer model achieves a Mean Squared Error (MSE) of 0.0033 and a Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) of 0.0575, significantly outperforming benchmark models. The proposed approach demonstrates superior accuracy in capturing the complex interactions within power systems in cold regions, enhancing system stability, energy efficiency, and resource allocation across system components. These results highlight the model’s potential as a robust tool for enhancing load forecasting in power systems within cold regions.

articleTitle: Research on Efficiency Evaluation Method for Energy Flow Interface Configuration of Multi-energy Integrated Equipment
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper proposes a systematic performance evaluation method for the energy flow interface configuration efficiency of multi-energy integrated equipment in the field of road transportation. The method first analyzes the energy flow topology of the multi-energy integrated equipment and, in conjunction with typical energy flow conversion circuits, such as Alternating Current (AC)-Direct Current(DC) Conversion, AC-AC, DC-AC, DC-DC, constructs a detailed energy flow interface model. By applying the Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP), seven key evaluation indicators are proposed, including energy conversion efficiency, interface stability, compatibility, safety, reliability, maintainability, and flexibility. Furthermore, using the scale judgment matrix and normalization algorithm, the weights of the evaluation indicators are scientifically calculated, ensuring the consistency of the judgment matrix. Additionally, three different energy flow interface configuration schemes are proposed, and the effectiveness of the evaluation method is verified through case studies. The research findings provide theoretical support for the design, optimization, and application of energy flow interfaces in multi-energy integrated equipment, contributing to improved energy utilization efficiency and promoting technological innovation.

articleTitle: Economic Control Strategies for Combined Heat and Power Source-Grid-Load-Storage System in Cold Regions
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In Northeast China, characterized by a high proportion of renewable energy and a cold climate, ensuring renewable energy integration and heating stability is of critical importance. This study addresses these challenges by aggregating electric-thermal flexibility resources within source-grid-load-storage systems and enabling their participation in the ancillary service market. The research first models the involvement of electric-thermal integrated source-grid-load-storage systems in the ancillary service market, focusing on real-time peak shaving for gas turbines and compensation mechanisms for adjustable loads and energy storage across different time periods. The study then explores economic control strategies for these integrated systems within the context of the ancillary service market. It considers the aggregation of various generators, including gas turbines, electric-thermal cogeneration units, wind turbines, and photovoltaics, while also accounting for the peak load-shaving capabilities of energy storage devices and the demand response potential of flexible electric and thermal loads. The proposed model is validated using actual data from a region in Jilin Province over a continuous 7-day period in December 2022. An incremental benefit analysis is conducted on the operation of the source-grid-load-storage system. The case study results demonstrate that the proposed economic control strategies for electric-thermal integrated source-grid-load-storage systems, when considering the ancillary service market, can effectively enhance economic benefits, improve renewable energy integration capacity, and maintain heating stability in cold regions.

Author Keywords: Peak Load Regulation and Auxiliary Services Markets

articleTitle: Research on the Evaluation Method of Green Electricity Consumption Potential for Distributed Aggregators
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: In the context of the new power system, it is of profound significance to clarify the resources aggregated by distributed resource aggregators and conduct predictive analysis through the assessment of green power consumption potential. However, with the rapid development of new energy, the problem of wind and solar power curtailment has become prominent, becoming a bottleneck hindering the sustainable development of new energy. Based on this, this article proposes a green power consumption potential evaluation method that is applicable to most distributed aggregators, conducts response regulation modeling, and uses typical distributed resource aggregators as examples for calculation. The practicality of this green power consumption potential evaluation method is verified through numerical examples.

articleTitle: Wind power interval forecasting based on RF-VMD-LSTM and non-parametric estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Wind power has a high level of technological maturity and is ideal for large-scale applications as a renewable energy source. The large-scale grid connection will pose problems to the safe and steady functioning of the grid due to the fluctuation and intermittency of wind power output. For secure delivery of the energy system and to avoid the economic risks associated with wind power grid connection, precise and reliable short-term wind power forecasting is crucial. This work offers a combination forecasting model including Random Forest, Variational Modal Decomposition, and Long Short Term Memory that utilizes the notions of choosing features and decomposition-reconstruction to improve forecasting accuracy. Firstly, the feature selection is performed by RF to calculate the feature importance of each environmental factor. Secondly, to diminish the non-smoothness, VMD decomposes the wind power time series. Thirdly, to acquire the wind power point forecasting results, the decomposed components of VMD from the chosen environmental factor series are input into the LSTM model. The computed results are then compared with those from the BPNN and SVM models. Finally, the absolute error of point prediction is used for kernel density estimation. The experimental findings reveal that the RF-VMDLSTM built in this work has an excellent degree of accuracy and proves the effectiveness of the model. For the interval prediction results, the PICP (prediction interval coverage probability) reaches 94.53% with a 90% confidence interval, which proves the validity of interval prediction and contributes to the decisionmakers making relevant decisions.

articleTitle: Economic Energy Management of Flexible Irrigation Load in the Rural Distribution System
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: As the number of flexible irrigation load increasing, the potential operation flexibility of rural distribution system is improved. In light of this, this study proposes a mathematical model for crop evapotranspiration and soil moisture considering the relationship between various agricultural production factors and well irrigation electricity consumption. And based on this, an energy management model for rural distribution systems considering flexible irrigation load was established. Finally, an economic energy management of flexible irrigation load in the rural distribution system is formulated. Numerical simulation in IEEE 33 bus system verified that the proposed strategy fully considers the growth laws of crops in the agricultural production process, quantifies the output value of daily agricultural production, and improves the economy of agricultural production process compared with the existing method.

articleTitle: Distributed Rapid Fault Self-Healing Scheme for Active Distribution Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The high penetration of renewable energy sources (RES) into distribution networks poses multifaceted challenges to traditional protection and control mechanisms. To achieve rapid fault self-healing in active distribution networks, a distributed fault self-healing scheme based on smart terminal units (STUs) is proposed. This scheme employs a waveform similarity comparison algorithm as the principle for fault segment localization, thereby rendering it adept at addressing active distribution networks containing various types of RES and varying levels of RES penetration. The proposed scheme enables rapid fault segment localization, isolation, and power restoration of non-faulty segments, while meticulously coordinating with the coordination with distributed generation (DG) anti-islanding protection and low-voltage ride-through capabilities. Each STU boasts the capability of automatic network topology recognition, allowing it to adapt its control strategies in response to real-time changes in the network topology.

articleTitle: Virtual energy storage sharing based multiple renewable energy stations cooperation to improve relisience of power system
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Extreme weather events can result in substantial economic losses to distribution networks. Enhancing the resilience of distribution networks is crucial for swiftly restoring power supply and mitigating economic losses. Consequently, this paper proposes a novel renewable energy station that relies on virtual energy storage (VES) sharing to bolster the resilience strategy of the power grid. Firstly, a peer-to-peer (P2P) transaction framework is devised. Within this framework, users in the distribution system can manage and allocate electrical energy in accordance with load demand, thereby facilitating the coordinated scheduling of power grids through renewable energy stations. Subsequently, a VES sharing model, which integrates mobile energy storage (MES) and flexible load, is introduced. Leveraging the transferable and reducible characteristics of demand-side flexible loads, the system’s resilience is enhanced by optimizing the routing and charging/discharging power of the MES. Through scenario comparisons, the coordinated scheduling impacts to improve the grid resilience of renewable energy stations are analyzed. Moreover, the judicious scheduling of VES is demonstrated to effectively reduce system losses and expedite power restoration. Finally, an illustrative example is presented to validate the efficacy of the new energy station coordination strategy based on VES sharing in enhancing the power grid’s resilience.

articleTitle: Study on Adsorption Kinetics and Hygroscopic Properties of LiCl/ Porous Matrix Composite Desiccant
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: This paper investigates the moisture adsorption characteristics of a composite desiccant incorporating LiCl and porous matrices. Various composite desiccant samples and coatings were prepared using an impregnation method, with LiCl as the moisture-absorbing agent, and utilizing silica gel and KIT-6 mesoporous molecular sieve as the matrix. Different loadings and various relative humidity levels were examined to evaluate the moisture adsorption properties of the composites. Additionally, dynamic and static adsorption properties of the composite desiccant were analyzed using mathematical models. The results demonstrated enhanced moisture adsorption performance in the composite desiccant compared to the pure matrix. At 30°C and 60% relative humidity, the maximum equilibrium adsorption capacities of LiCl/silica gel and LiCl/KIT-6 composite desiccants were found to be 1.028 g/g and 1.273 g/g, respectively, approximately 6-7 times higher than that of their pure matrices. Moreover, the composite desiccant exhibited a larger adsorption rate coefficient than the pure matrix and reached adsorption equilibrium at a faster rate.

articleTitle: One-Key Sequential Control Technology for Intelligent Substation Based on Convolutional Neural Network and Natural Language Processing
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Intelligent substations, as an important part of modern power grids, have been widely used in the automation control of power systems. Although the existing One-Key sequential control technology has significant results in improving operation efficiency and reducing the risk of misoperation, there are still major limitations in the efficiency of operation ticket writing and checking, as well as the manual error rate. In this paper, we propose a One-Key sequential control scheme for intelligent substations based on CNN and NLP technologies, aiming to improve the automation of generating and checking operation tickets by integrating these two technologies. This paper investigates the application of CNN in the recognition of main wiring diagrams of intelligent substations and explores the effectiveness of NLP in the verification of operation tickets and database signals. In order to verify the feasibility and practicality of the proposed scheme, this paper designs and implements a system architecture integrating CNN and NLP technologies, and conducts systematic tests on a 500 kV substation. The test results show that the technical scheme proposed in this paper can significantly improve the efficiency of generating and verifying operation tickets, reduce the errors caused by human intervention, and has wide application value and development potential.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Self-storage Potential and Investigation of Regulation Strategies for Cooling system
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Addressing the limitations of conventional cool storage methods in cooling systems, which often struggle with high investment costs, site constraints, and limited participation in grid peak shaving, this paper introduces a novel self-storage approach. This method leverages the modulation of chilled water temperatures within the user-side piping network to achieve cool storage and release, thereby facilitating grid peak shaving without incurring additional costs. To quantify the self-storage potential of cooling systems, it then progresses to a simulation to compare the cool storage rates, cool storage durations, and cool storage energy efficiency ratios (EERs) under both conventional and optimized regulation strategies. The findings reveal that, compared to conventional strategies, an optimized operation strategy targeting the maximization of cool storage EER can effectively reduce the cool storage duration and elevate the upper limit of the cool storage rate.

articleTitle: Research on strategy of renewable energy electric hydrogen synthesis ammonia system based on two-stage robust optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Renewable Power to Ammonia is one of the largescale consumption ways of renewable energy such as wind power generation and photovoltaic power generation, and it is also one of the important technical routes for the chemical industry to achieve low-carbon and clean development. Aiming at the uncertainty of renewable energy and load in the system, a two-stage robust optimization model of min-max-min structure was established in this paper. The model of hydrogen synthesis ammonia system using wind power photovoltaic electrolysis water was based on wind speed data, fan parameters, light data, environmental parameters, synthetic ammonia output, power consumption of hydrogen production process and economic data, etc. Under the conditions of real-time power balance of hydro-gen-producing ammonia system, new energy power rejection rate, electrolytic cell characteristics, hydrogen demand for synthetic ammonia and upper and lower limits of energy storage, the objective function of the first stage is the optimal investment cost of the mi-crogrid, and the second stage is the optimal operation cost of the mi-crogrid. Finally, the validity of the proposed model and algorithm is verified by using real-time landscape data simulation analysis in Da ‘an District.

articleTitle: A Defect Recognition Method for Switchgear Infrared Images Based on Improved YOLOv9s
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Currently, switchgear infrared inspection is primarily based on manual assessment of temperature overrun faults, exhibiting a limited degree of automation. This paper proposes the integration of a target recognition algorithm to identify equipment within the switchgear cabinet and the utilisation of the relative temperature difference method to assess equipment faults. In the domain of target detection, Yolov9s (You Only Look Once Version 9 Small) exhibits a notable advantage and can be employed for the recognition of infrared image defects. However, there are limitations to the detection accuracy and the model is too large to be effectively deployed on the mobile side. Accordingly, this paper proposes an enhanced lightweight YOLOv9s-mobilenetv3-adowncbam network to efficiently achieve lightweight implementation. The primary enhancements entail substituting the backbone with a lightweight MobileNetv3 (Mobile Neural Network Version 3) network architecture, incorporating a novel Adown downsampling and CBAM (Convolutional Block Attention Module) attention mechanism at the neck layer, and constructing a YOLOv9s-mobilenetv3-adown-cbam model. The experimental results demonstrate that the enhanced network model exhibits a $\mathbf{9 5. 9 \%}$ high-precision performance in the Map@0.5 indicator, while the GFLOPs value is only 25.8. In comparison to the original YOLOv9s model, the accuracy is enhanced by 5.4%, and the computational load is reduced by approximately 19.9%. This enables the model to operate effectively on mobile devices with enhanced performance.

articleTitle: Adaptive control strategy of virtual power plant based on peak shaving demand response
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: A flexible load virtual power plant (VPP) with airconditioning load as the main load is affected by uncertainty in operation, which makes the peak shaving demand response deviate from the expected effect, because the existing DR strategy is based on the static target load curve, and therefore, an adaptive control method is proposed for the VPP with flexible load to participate in the peak shaving demand response (DR), In the proposed closedloop control model, the controlled process is decoupled into a small-scale and linear progress deviation model and a peak shaving correction model, where the progress deviation model apportions the planned peak shaving amount and the peak shaving correction model adjusts the target load curve, and an example verifies the validity of the method in terms of shaving mode, error and delay.

articleTitle: Research on the Design and Optimization of a Compact Air-Cooled Battery Module Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Due to the advantages of high energy density, long cycle life, and no memory effect, lithium-ion batteries play a crucial role in promoting the development of global new energy vehicles and achieving the “dual carbon” strategic goals. However, the temperature rise of the battery during charging and discharging may lead to a decrease in battery capacity and lifespan and even result in thermal runaway. Therefore, the development of an efficient thermal management system is essential. This paper proposes an innovative side-throat throttling air-cooled battery module design for parallel air-cooled battery modules that may experience excessive temperature rise and uneven temperature distribution in restricted spaces. Using FLUENT software to simulate the temperature distribution of individual cells in different parallel air-cooled and flow field distribution within the module, the specific impact of different wind speeds on thermal performance was thoroughly analyzed. The results show that the side-throat throttling air-cooling technology can effectively regulate the flow resistance of each branch flow path inside the module and optimize the uniformity of the internal flow field distribution, thereby enhancing the thermal performance of the module.

articleTitle: Information gap decision theory based PV and energy storage planning considering endogenous and exogenous uncertainties
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The large-scale access of distributed photovoltaic (PV) poses significant challenges to the safe and stable operation of distribution network. This puts forward higher requirements for the configuration of energy storage system. However, traditional energy storage planning only considers exogenous uncertainty unrelated to decision-making, but ignore endogenous uncertainty caused by decision-making itself. This limitation may lead to poor performance of PV and energy storage planning in dealing with uncertainties in practical operation. To address this issue, this paper firstly develops the exogenous load and endogenous price uncertainties model. Then, an information gap decision theory based energy storage planning that comprehensively considers endogenous and exogenous uncertainties is proposed. The effectiveness of the proposed model is verified on the IEEE 33-node distribution network.

articleTitle: Orderly Charging Price Mechanism for Vehicle Network Interaction Using Transformer-CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: China’s electric vehicle ownership is rising year by year, becoming a potential resource that the power grid can dispatch. To better utilize V2G technology to serve the grid, it is necessary to establish a relevant market, which cannot be separated from government support and subsidies. Previous V2G research focused on multi-scenario applications, based on EV simulation, with more assumptions and simplifications on EV user behavior, which is difficult to reflect real user habits. Predicting EV charging order distribution based on charging pile historical data would be more accurate and credible. In this paper, firstly, based on the EV vehicle-network interaction mechanism, we propose a model to formulate the upper and lower limits of subsidized price considering the cost reduction price and narrowing the peak-valley difference of the power grid. Then it establishes Transformer and CNN based, predicting order distribution for charging and discharging model solving. Finally, two different operating habits of private cars and buses are brought into the vehicle data to verify the effectiveness of the price mechanism proposed in this paper. The strategy provides a reference for real-time incentive adjustment to orderly charging for vehicle-network interaction, which contributes to the long-term construction and operation of the V2G market.

articleTitle: Design of a Cloud-Native and Highly Available Method and Device for Electricity Spot Market Clearing Based on Breakpoint Recovery
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The electricity spot market clearing method is key to ensuring optimal short-term operation of the power grid. However, once the current algorithm is interrupted during execution, it often needs to be recalculated, resulting in a waste of computing resources and prolonged response time. This paper proposes a power spot market clearing method and equipment based on breakpoint algorithm, and expands and improves the fault-tolerance mechanism and data persistence. By refining and persisting the algorithm execution phase and designing a corresponding breakpoint recovery device, the system can recover from the most recent calculation phase after an interruption, significantly improving the algorithm’s disaster recovery capabilities. When an interruption occurs during computing, the system can resume from the most recent computing stage, thereby improving overall computing efficiency and system reliability. In addition, this article introduces an improved data persistence mechanism, combined with cloud native database and blockchain technology, to improve data consistency and recovery speed in large-scale failure scenarios. The fault-tolerance mechanism extends the application of multi-active disaster recovery technology to enhance the system Adaptability under wide-area failure or network security attack scenarios. This method has significant advantages in improving system availability in the electricity market.

articleTitle: Investigation of the effect of top clearance on cavitation characteristics and stability of axial flow pump
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: To investigate the influence of top clearance on the cavitation characteristics of axial pumps and their safety and stability after cavitation, this paper carries out numerical simulations of axial pumps with different lobe top clearances based on the SST(Shear-Stress-Transport) $\kappa-\omega$ turbulence model and the Rayleigh-Plesset homogeneous flow cavitation model. Comparative analyses of blade surface pressure distribution, vacuole volume fraction distribution, turbulent kinetic energy distribution, blade deformation and equivalent stresses are carried out through fluid-structure interaction calculations. The results show that the head and efficiency of the pump decrease with the increase of the gap, but the increase of the gap does not change the primary part of cavitation, which occurs at the inlet edge of the blade, and expands along the chord direction of the blade, and finally covers the whole blade. With the increase of clearance, the area of low-pressure area and cavity volume on the blade surface decreases, and the distribution area of high turbulent kinetic energy increases first and then decreases. The maximum deformation and maximum equivalent stress under cavitation show a trend of increasing first and then decreasing. The maximum deformation area occurs at the tip of the blade, and the stress distribution at the root of the blade is the most concentrated, which is prone to fatigue damage. Appropriate increase of the gap is beneficial to improve the anti-cavitation performance and stability of the pump. When the gap is 2 mm, the operation condition of the pump is the best.

articleTitle: Coordinated Control Strategy for User-Side Integrated Energy Network Based on Carbon Emission Responsibility Factor
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: With the severe challenges of global climate change and the urgent need for sustainable development, the efficient use of energy and low-carbon transformation on the user side have become crucial. This paper proposes a coordinated control method for the user-side integrated energy network based on the carbon emission responsibility factor, aiming to achieve low-carbon and efficient energy use of the user-side integrated energy system through advanced physical information technology and innovative management models. This paper sorts out the physical structure and energy coupling relationships of the integrated energy system, constructs the network energy flow distribution matrix and carbon flow density matrix, and calculates the carbon flow rate distribution matrix through the Hadamard product, thereby calculating the carbon emission responsibility factor of each load node. By comparing the actual total carbon emissions with the limit, combined with the prediction of the autoregressive time series model, the coordinated control of the user-side integrated energy network is realized to ensure that the carbon emissions per unit time and the total carbon emissions meet the limit requirements within a unit of time. This method has a wide range of applicability, high robustness, and load friendliness, providing an effective control strategy for the low-carbon operation of the user-side integrated energy system.

articleTitle: Multi-level Estimation Method for the Hosting Capacity of Charging Infrastructure Integration in Power Grid
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: The rapid expansion of the global electric vehicle market has brought new challenges to the distribution network, including load peaks, degraded power quality, and increased difficulty in grid dispatching. Large-scale EV access is not considered in traditional distribution network planning, making it difficult for existing facilities to accommodate it. This paper proposes an innovative evaluation method that constructs a hierarchical evaluation system from 220kV to $220 \mathrm{~V} / 380 \mathrm{~V}$ for the first time. This system aims to guide the coordinated development of electric vehicle charging infrastructure with the power grid, simplify the power grid’s actual situation, and enhance practicality. Finally, a single 220kV station is used as an example to verify the proposed method.

articleTitle: Ranging backup protection scheme adapted to photovoltaic inverter control strategy in grid-connected scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 6th International Conference on Energy, Power and Grid (ICEPG)
abstract: Large-scale photovoltaic grid connection will bring serious challenges to the adaptability of traditional relay protection, and distance protection is the first to bear the brunt due to its weak feeding effect. In this regard, this paper made the following improvements to the traditional distance protection scheme. For the protection of the large grid side, based on the negative and zero sequence networks under faults, a short-circuit impedance algorithm independent of the transition resistance size was constructed to solve the fault distance by using the sequence current conditions constructed by the negative sequence current suppression strategy of the photovoltaic field station side and the zero sequence current branching coefficients which were not affected by the control strategy of the photovoltaic inverter. When the protection on the grid side recognizes that the fault occurred in the zone and tripped the breakers, the feeding effect on the fault point disappeared and the virtual synchronizer control strategy was used on the photovoltaic field station side to ensure safe and stable operation during the fault. The protection can thus solve the short-circuit impedance triangle formed by the impedance relay, and then realize the calculation of the short-circuit impedance. The simulation results based on PSCAD/EMTDC show that the proposed scheme eliminates the effect of transition resistance, has high-ranging accuracy, can protect the full length of the line, can act as backup protection in scenarios where the pilot protection is not applicable due to communication failure, and has the role of fault ranging.
